Panne de chauffage du cottage du personn: black staff cottage heating failure; Anna Moellenhoff wants to house them in Lee Hall; Rubye Lipsey refuses (village antagonism)
Le village vote la prohibition ; Roy (pa: The village votes prohibition; Roy (master of a beer outlet near the station) and student Stephen Forbes open a coffee outside the city, financed by Forbes; Rice sometimes dances

Article d'Adamic sur Black Mountain dans: Adamic article on Black Mountain in Harpers (April 1936, p. 516-530) with Bernard DeVoto's response (p. 605-608); Condensed in the Readers Digest; 40 to 50 letters of application per day
Mangold en vacances au Mexique ; Neal Va: Mangold on holiday in Mexico; Neal Van Middlesworth succeeds him as guardian
Arrivée de l'économiste William Edward Z: Arrival of economist William Edward Zeuch (founder of Commonwealth College, Llano Colony, Guggenheim Fellow 1931-32)

Barbara Beatty (fille du commissaire aux: Barbara Beatty (daughter of the Indian Affairs Commissioner) helps recruit Indian painter Harrison Begay (who leaves Albers and college after one year)
« Spectodrama » de Xanti Schawinsky (con: “Spectodrama” by Xanti Schawinsky (designed at Bauhaus in 1927): pantomime, movement, sound, color, light

Discussions sur l'achat de Lake Eden (jo: Discussions on the purchase of Lake Eden (Journal of Mort Steinau, 12, 13, 30 April and 1 May 1937)
Visite d'Aldous Huxley (avec sa femme, s: Visit of Aldous Huxley (with his wife, son and Gerald Heard) in early May 1937; Heard talks about communities, yoga, telepathy; Huxley's notes on the United States
Knickerbocker absent deux semaines et de: Knickerbocker absent two and a half weeks without the college seeing it (“his cause have practically completely folded up”)
Causerie d'Aldous Huxley devant tout le: Talk by Aldous Huxley in front of the entire college: “limitations of the novel” (ideas and artwork, Dickens, Homer, Fielding)

Achat de la propriété de Lake Eden (anci: Purchase of Lake Eden property (former holiday centre: 667 acres, artificial lake, stilt dining room, two lodges, a dozen cottages) for $35,000 ($2,000 cash, $7,000 per year for five years) through subscription, including from the Forbes family
Séjours du compositeur-violoncelliste Da: Stays of composer-violincellist Dante Fiorello: he composes and plays “The Black Mountain Suite” and “The John Andrew Rice Suite”
Visites de Ted Shawn et de sa troupe de: Visits of Ted Shawn and his troupe of dancers, Fernand Léger (translated by Lucian Marquis) and Henry Miller (two days, with Abraham Ratner)
« Alice » entre au college (55 étudiants: “Alice” enters college (55 students in the fall) despite a negative vote (“another vampire”)
Un jeune économiste, engagé au dernier m: A young economist, hired at the last moment, and his wife are the target of the mockery of Rice at the beginning of the quarter
Fugue de deux étudiants, environ trois m: Two students fled, about three months after school; the rector (Rice) more upset than anyone
Lancement du BMC Newsletter ; David Bail: Launch of the BMC Newsletter; David Bailey (former student) advertising director for one year
Un dimanche soir, deux étudiants d'Antio: One Sunday evening, two students from Antioch arrive at Lee Hall during Debussy's White and Black Study with two pianos; one, Will Hamlin, decides to transfer to Black Mountain
Wunsch monte Bury the Dead d'Irwin Shaw,: Wunsch mounts Bury the Dead from Irwin Shaw, section decors surrounding the audience (George Hendrickson)
« Danse Macabre » de Schawinsky : théâtr: Schawinsky “Danse Macabre”: total round theatre, John Evarts music played by the orchestra on Allan Sly, masked audience and cape
Début de la liaison de Rice et d'Alice «: Start of connection of Rice and Alice “by midwinter”; Evening of sketches where Alice, in paper mâché costume, parody an opera singer; Rice is called “shocked”
Première visite de Walter Gropius (sur s: First visit of Walter Gropius (at the suggestion of Albers): conference on modern architecture (“nobody can get to essentials better than he”)
Arrivée du psychologue Erwin Straus (All: Arrival of psychologist Erwin Straus (Germany), who buys a briefcase as a sign of brotherhood during the construction program
John Cage (Cornish School, Seattle) écri: John Cage (Cornish School, Seattle) writes to request a position; then in 1942 proposed a Center for Experimental Music; No further action
Dernière réunion générale de l'année : W: Last general meeting of the year: Wunsch summarizes the Rice case for students (“You are in no condition to direct the College affairs now”)
Départ de Portell-Vila à la fin de l'ann: Departure from Portell-Vila at the end of the following year
Retour de Rice, « ghostlike existence »: Return of Rice, “ghostlike existence”; he writes his autobiography in a room of Lee Hall; Alice remains, the link is finished; arrival of Peggy (Loram) and David Bailey
Le Board élit Robert Wunsch recteur à la: Board elects Robert Wunsch rector instead of Rice
Nell Rice entre hôtesse de son frère Ayd: Nell Rice between hostess of his brother Aydelotte in Swarthmore, School of Librarians in Chapel Hill and apprenticeship at Asheville
Jalowetz entre aux États-Unis ; par le N: Jalowetz enters the United States; by the National Coordinating Committee to Aid Refugees, he learns that a position is vacant at Black Mountain
BMC Newsletter n° 4 (achat de Lake Eden): BMC Newsletter No 4 (purchase of Lake Eden)
Lake Eden exploité comme auberge pendant: Lake Eden operated as a hostel for two summers; Summer music and singing courses to find funds
Arrivée de Heinrich Jalowetz (élève de S: Arrival of Heinrich Jalowetz (student of Schönberg, former opera director in Cologne and Regensburg), his wife Johanna and his daughter Lisa, for the year 1939-40
La Cerisaie en répétition d'octobre à ma: Cerisaie in rehearsal from October to May (“it would be put on when it was ready”)
BMC Newsletter n° 6 : origine des étudia: BMC Newsletter #6: Student Origin (18 of New York, 8 of Massachusetts, 6 of Illinois); Northeast 58 per cent
Pendant la construction : arrivée d'un w: During construction: arrival of a car of 54 tons of coal (four volunteers, three days, steak dinner); “The Sawing Off of the Pile Posts”; fire of a small building (drained pipes); Three-day storm (11 inches of rain): two students carried away by the spill, one drowns
BMC Newsletter n° 7 : annonce du départ: BMC Newsletter #7: Rice Start Announcement (to focus on writing)
Séjour d'Aristide Mavridis (beau-frère d: Stay of Aristide Mavridis (brother of the Greek ambassador Cimon Diamantopoulos, former Greek Secretary General for Agriculture) who came to learn English: a few weeks to teach fencing to little Eddie Dreier, then abrupt departure
Début du programme de construction : cou: Start of the construction programme: lessons in the morning and evening, voluntary work in the afternoon at Lake Eden (drainage, insulation, foundations) for almost three years; foreman Charles Godfrey, Chief Carpenter Bascombe Allen; Richard Gothe organizes teams (stones, concrete...)
A. Lawrence Kocher et sa famille s'insta: A. Lawrence Kocher and his family settle at the college: he builds his plans and teaches architecture; students of Harvard (including Thai “Nim” and “Nik”)
Arrivée de Molly Gregory (30 ans) : assi: Arrival of Molly Gregory (30 years old): assistant of Albers, carpentry, furniture, farm; Community arbitrator
Wallen étudie avec Carl Rogers à Ohio St: Wallen studied with Carl Rogers in Ohio State (master's), then again six months in 1944; offer to succeed Rogers at the head of the USO counseling, declined
BMC Newsletter n° 10 (avancement de la c: BMC Newsletter No. 10 (progress in construction; n° 11 Feb. and No. 12 March 1941)
Affiche « WANTED: ZOMBIES FOR THE WORK P: Display “WANTED: ZOMBIES FOR THE WORK PROGRAM”; “hot general meeting” on manual work in a college of liberal arts (Straus and mathematicians motorcyclists)
Compte rendu d'une page sur la carrière: One-page report on the career of BMC graduates
Déménagement de Lee Hall à Lake Eden : D: Moving from Lee Hall to Lake Eden: Derek Bovington makes a tractor shuttle with crafts, pianos, books, equipment... and all the heating of Lee Hall
Collecte de fonds à travers le pays : Ev: Fundraising across the country: Evarts in California (Henry Fonda, March, Herman Mankiewicz; only Melvyn Douglas gives); $5,000 anonymous donation announced by Dreier
Rentrée retardée de deux semaines ; pres: Reentry delayed by two weeks; almost all students come back in advance to help
Arrivée de Frances de Graaff (37 ans, do: Arrival of Frances of Graaff (37 years old, doctor of Leiden on Essenin, come from Reed College)
Première réunion générale à Lake Eden :: First general meeting at Lake Eden: speech by Albers, returning from one year of teaching to Harvard (“Life means change. Our aim is forward”)
Journal de Betty Brett (2, 4, 25 nov. 19: Betty Brett Journal (2, 4, 25 Nov. 1941) on Student Claims
John Andrew Rice, I Came Out of the Eigh: John Andrew Rice, I Came Out of the Eighteenth Century (Harper & Brothers), Harper Award; Albers, Dreier and Nell Rice first refuse to read the chapter on BMC
Les enseignants renoncent à leur salaire: Teachers give up their salaries beyond $10 per month; second $18,000 mortgage (balance of first $11,500)
Extension de la ferme : troupeaux laitie: Extension of the farm: dairy and slaughter herds (a bull offered by Marshall Field), 500-600 chicks, vegetables, barn, dairy, stable; Molly Gregory runs the farm
Arrivée du musicologue Edward Lowinsky ;: Arrival of musicologist Edward Lowinsky; anthropologist Paul Radin teaches at college
Photo 13 : Nell Rice, avril 1942, par Ho: Photo 13: Nell Rice, April 1942, by Howard Dearstyne
Demandes d'attestations aux colleges (An: Applications for college certificates (Antioch, Swarthmore, Reed, North Caroline University of Frank Graham...); getting a quota in the V-1 (Navy) and Listed Reserve Corps programs
Nouvelle campagne de fonds : Albers, Koc: New fund-raising campaign: Albers, Kocher, Mangold and Dreier devote almost all summer
Lettres de recommandation pour Frederic: Letters of recommendation for Frederic Cohen and Elsa Kahl: Cohen (20 Jul), Carleton Sprague Smith (7 Aug), New York Times John Martin (8 Aug), Martha Graham (13 Aug. 1942)
Arrivée du chimiste Fritz Hansgirg et de: Arrival of the chemist Fritz Hansgirg and his wife (Cadillac cream, Hammond organ installed in the dining room, records: evenings “Bach and cookies”)
Arrivée de Frederic (« Fritz ») Cohen, c: Arrival of Frederic (“Fritz”) Cohen, co-founder of Ballets Jooss, Elsa Kahl, dancer, and Eric Bentley (25 years old)
Les étudiants refusent l'« agreement » t: Students refuse the traditional “agreement” prohibiting visits to rooms of the opposite sex
Mort de Richard Carpenter (cancer du pou: Death of Richard Carpenter (lung cancer, 31 years old), one year after roof construction
Mort Steinau quitte la communauté (gesti: Mort Steinau leaves the community (financial management)
Negro History Week : causeries d'enseign: Negro History Week: teacher talks, Harmon Foundation film on Hampton Institute, W. A. Robinson lecture; Wunsch invites black teachers of Asheville
Extraction de mica : 250 livres en deux: Extraction of mica: 250 pounds in two days; inspectors of the Colonial Mica Corporation (“good muscovite”); a minor hired
La ferme fournit l'essentiel de la nourr: La farm provides most of the food; pork and beef sold outside; Albers panelled and painted the dining room and lodge halls; gravel roads lined with gallax and bay
Arrivée de Clark Foreman (New Deal, Defe: Arrival of Clark Foreman (New Deal, Defense Housing Authority, Southern Conference for Human Welfare)
Conférences de Bentley sur la guerre (se: Bentley Conferences on the Second Front; Straus counterseries on the history of materialism; Straus invites Emilio von Hofmannsthal to warn against Russia
Hansgirg annonce au Board la création d': Hansgirg announces at Board the creation of a company for its process of extracting magnesium from olivine and gives 20% to the college (project not continued: pilot fire)
Le comité exécutif de la Southern Confer: The Executive Committee of the Southern Conference for Human Welfare (Chair: Foreman) meets several days in Black Mountain; two long meetings with the community on the “démocratie”: unanimous opinion for admission of black students
Quatre mois de débat sur l'admission d'é: Four months of debate on the admission of black students (secret caucuses, marathon sessions); resignation of a student and the assistant-treasurer; Students vote 2 to 1 for admission in autumn 1944; shared faculty (Foreman, Bentley, Graaff, Cohen, Jalowetz, Radin for ; Straus, Albers, Hansgirg, Kurtz, Wunsch, Gregory, Miller, Dreier, Lowinsky against)
Visite de l'anthropologue Zora Hurston à: Visit of anthropologist Zora Hurston to Black Mountain
Les étudiants montent une exposition des: Students set up an exhibition of Bertrand Russell books in the library; Straus accuses of Graaff, who no longer talks to him for weeks
Photo 12 : Eric Bentley dirige un sémina: Photo 12 : Eric Bentley leads a seminar, 1944
Robert Creeley, étudiant à Harvard, pass: Robert Creeley, a student at Harvard, spent a few days at Black Mountain with his wife Ann, briefly studying in 1944
Visite de deux étudiants noirs et d'un p: Visit of two black students and a black professor from Fisk, housed in ordinary dormitories after discussion, without incident
Foreman, « Summary of Discussions Regard: Foreman, “Summary of Discussions Regarding Admission of Negro Students” (Rosenwald Fund offers funding for black students)
Production d'Outward Bound par Wunsch, m: Production of Outward Bound by Wunsch, mocked by Bentleyites (“a major college disgrace”)
Bal costumé surréaliste « Out of This Wo: Surrealist costumed ball “Out of This World” (Bentley: “to shock Erwin Straus”) : Janey Stone, Jeanne Wacker in “hula girl”, Hansgirg disguised in one another, Albers in tweed suit with paper cones, which leaves furious
Dreier s'en prend à Paul Radin (commérag: Dreier attacks Paul Radin (commerces, intrigues, “Communist plots”); Radin announces that it will not return; Radin leaves a few days before the end of the quarter without warning
Été 1944 : Clark Foreman travaille au CI: Summer 1944: Clark Foreman works at the IOC Committee for Political Action for the Re-election of Roosevelt; Eric Bentley teaches summer at Fisk
Institut de musique 1944 : presque tout: Music Institute 1944: almost the entire Schönberg circle — Rudolf Kolisch, Marcel Dick, Edward Steuermann, Ernst Krenek, Roger Sessions, Mark Brunswick; Schönberg sends a message to the opening; Jean Charlot leaves two frescoes on the Studies Building batteries; income over $3,000
Institut de musique d'été 1944 : Kolisch: Summer Music Institute 1944: Kolisch Quartet, Ernst Krenek, Edward Steuermann, Yella Pessl; Schönberg Quartet op. 7 rehearsals in the North Lodge lobby
Institut d'art d'été 1944 (une semaine a: Summer Art Institute 1944 (one week after the beginning of the music institute): Gropius, Amédée Ozenfant, José of Creeft, Jean Charlot (freezes on the Studies Building batteries)
José de Creeft organise une « corrida »: Creeft José organizes an “corrida” to play anger (toreros, picadors mixing opponents); No effect
Série de réunions du Board of Fellows pe: Board of Fellows meeting series for three weeks on the case of Graaff (then Bentley); the two factions sit on both sides of the dining room; Graaff twice called
Départ définitif des dissidents : France: Final departure of dissidents: Frances of Graaff, Eric Bentley, Frederic Cohen, Elsa Kahl, Clark Foreman and about twenty students — one third of the college
Dreier, épuisé (« nerves were shot »), e: Dreier, exhausted (“nerves were shot”), is convinced to take a short vacation
Après la scission : Bentley à la Kenyon: After the split: Bentley at the Kenyon Review a few months, then at the University of Minnesota; Graaff at Anderson and Wacker (Greenwich Village), then with the Cohen in the house rented by the Foreman (Park Avenue); project of a new college in an abandoned hotel ~100 miles from Washington; from Graaff to the Office of War Information, Elsa Kahl to the Army Service Groups
Erwin Straus en congé de recherche au Jo: Erwin Straus on research leave at Johns Hopkins Hospital during the year — he will never return; Kurtz also on leave
Année 1944-45 sans biologiste, économist: Year 1944-45 without biologist, economist, historian, psychologist or language teacher; Maria Hansgirg teaches French, Lowinsky Renaissance culture; mostly new students
Peggy Bennett (Cole) étudiante à Black M: Peggy Bennett (Cole) student at Black Mountain in 1944-45 (she worked in the office in 1947); souvenirs: George the cook hits the triangle at 6am and 6:30am, table-to-table songs (“Green Grow the Rushes, Ho!”), Jalowetz and Lowinsky concerts, Bach choral rehearsals directed by Jalowetz some evenings
Arrivée de George Zabriskie (poète, The: Arrival of George Zabriskie (poet, The Minds Geography): “The Psychodynamics of Creativity”, “Modern Poetry”, “Verse Writing”, then French after Maria Hansgirg's heart attack; it remains 1944-45
Alfred Kazin (29 ans, auteur d'On Native: Alfred Kazin (29 years old, author of On Native Grounds) teaches only one term: courses on Melville and Blake, small course on the Old Testament
Épisode de la bouse de vache : des étudi: Episode of the cow's dung : hostile students present a building in dung during Werklehre of Albers
Un soir de janvier, après six mois de pr: One evening in January, after six months of preparation, Foreman announced that he would become secretary of the National Citizens Political Action Committee: end of the college project; Fritz Cohen tries to sell the Music Institute to other schools, then runs the Opera Workshop of the Juilliard; from Graaff to Wells (two years) then Bryn Mawr
Fred Schwartz (docteur en économie de la: Fred Schwartz (doctor in economics of the Sorbonne, former textile industry in Czechoslovakia), a few months at the college, resigned with an eight-page review
Albers parle en classe de l'élection du: Albers speaks in class about the Student Moderator election (“the preceding year”)
Mai 1945 : le college arrête sa formule: May 1945: the college stops its formula — two black students admitted to the summer institutes of music and art, then a black teacher (or a series of invited teachers) for the autumn
Instituts d'été 1945 : deux étudiants no: Summer Institutes 1945: two black scholarship students and two black guest artists, Carol Brice and Roland Hayes — fees and scholarships paid by Julius Rosenwald Fund
Wunsch démissionne aussitôt ; revient à: Wunsch resigns immediately; returns at one o'clock in the morning looking for his things and leaves before dawn, as agreed with the Board; Molly Gregory wants to carry his books
Dreier parti en vacances à Lake George,: Dreier went on holiday to Lake George, Molly Gregory brings the whole community together; Herbert Miller announces the truth about the arrest of Wunsch
Instituts d'été 1945 : art — Gropius, Ly: Summer Institutes 1945: Art — Gropius, Lyonel Feininger, Ossip Zadkine, Alvin Lustig, Mary Callery, Robert Motherwell; music — Roland Hayes, Carol Brice, Erwin Bodky, Hugo Kauder, Alfred Einstein; complaint: too many events
Carol Brice, venue avec sa mère et son b: Carol Brice, coming with her mother and baby, stays four weeks and gives several concerts
Dernier concert de Carol Brice ; le même: Last Carol Brice concert; the same day arrives Roland Hayes (with his wife and daughter); at the Lowinsky party, Hayes sings its new spiritual arrangements
Wunsch rentre en Louisiane, malade plusi: Wunsch returns to Louisiana, sick several months (“a bad jaw infection”), then goes to California where he disappears (postman, according to rumor)
Les Wallen en visite à Black Mountain ;: Wallen visiting Black Mountain; Two “vocaux” teachers (Albers suspected) delay the appointment on the rumour (letter from Gordon Allport, July 19, 1945) of a reform for “nervous instability”, denied by the army
Concert public de Roland Hayes (accompag: Roland Hayes public concert (with Reginald Boardman from New Hampshire): the largest crowd in the history of the college, ~400 people including 300 outside guests and 30-40 Blacks; Non-segregated seats (“Wherever you please”); no incidents
Photo 14 : John Wallen et son fils Kurt: Photo 14: John Wallen and his son Kurt in front of the Wallen apartment, 1945-46
Sylvesta (« Vesta ») Martin, venue à l'I: Sylvesta (“Vesta”) Martin, who came to the Music Institute, remains as the first full-time black student; Dr. Percy H. Baker, “visiting lecturer” in Biology for the Fall Quarter 1945 ($700, Rosenwald Fund)
Le chœur du college (avec Vesta Martin): The choir of the college (with Vesta Martin) prepares the Passion according to St Matthew of Schütz for a white Methodist church of Black Mountain; veto of the church council; the choir sings in the black church (contradictory versions on the crowd)
Rentrée 1945 : neuf nouveaux enseignants: Return 1945: nine new teachers (eight young Americans with children), one-year appointments; 60 students (25% men); GI Bill accreditation (music, English, social sciences, mathematics, conditional chemistry)
Arrivées : John L. Wallen (27 ans, psych: Arrivals: John L. Wallen (27 years old, psychology, PhD at Harvard), Albert William “Bill” Levi (philosophy) and Mary Caroline Richards (literature and writing), from Chicago; Theodore Rondthaler (finance, Latin); Max Dehn (mathematics, Plato, ethics; Sunday hikes)
Le Board of Fellows adopte une nouvelle: Board of Fellows adopts new appointment policy: first year trial, then one, two, three and five year renewals
Dreier en congé à Cambridge presque tout: Dreier on leave in Cambridge almost all year 1945-46, elected rector in absentia after the departure of Wunsch; periodic visits to the college
Cours de Wallen : « Introduction to psyc: Wallen course: “Introduction to psychology” (without manual, T.A.T. at the beginning of the course) and seminar on the master-pupil relationship (Cantor, The Dynamics of Learning; Rank, Fromm, Rogers, Horney) ; session on King Oedipus
Groupe d'étude du corps enseignant sur «: Teaching staff study group on “the aims of education at BMC”: one session, the second session never takes place
Étudiants de Wallen : accompagnement deu: Wallen students: two afternoon a week accompaniment to a young patient from a nearby psychiatric hospital, Southern Negro Youth Congress, petitions, electoral registration; Question of the picket in front of Lucky Strike
Wallen au comité d'admission : choix d'u: Wallen on the admission committee: choosing a student “imaginative and erratic” rather than a good student; the student then has difficulties
Après la guerre, pas de fermier professi: After the war, no professional farmer: Molly Gregory plows, harrows, returns the crops, holds the dairy with students
Dépenses : nourriture 23 595 dollars en: Expenditure: food $23,595 in 1945-46, 36,279 in 1946-47; living expenses 42,110 and $64,281
Soirée d'étudiants chez les Wallen : idé: Wallen student evening: idea to reform the work program (deficit of $12,000); questionnaire; petition for a community meeting signed by 34 students and 11 teachers (including Jalowetz and Lowinsky)
Réunion du corps enseignant : Wallen pré: Faculty meeting: Wallen presents its method (box with suggestions 36 hours before, seven groups of twelve, three twenty-minute questions, coffee and cake, general list); objections (Albers), then “vote of confidence”
Mort de Heinrich Jalowetz d'une crise ca: Death of Heinrich Jalowetz from a heart attack after a Beethoven sonata recital sitting on the porch; Johanna Jalowetz and Lockwood watch by listening to the Passion according to St Matthew, the Quintette with clarinet of Brahms, Mozart, Bach's Cello Suites
Second trimestre 1945-46 : le compositeu: Second quarter 1945-46: the black composer Mark Fax succeeds Baker; no incident of the year despite the visitors and concerts of Vesta Martin and Mark Fax
Arthur Penn (24 ans, ancien du Neighborh: Arthur Penn (24 years old, alumni of the Philadelphia Neighborhood Playhouse, theatre in the armies), on the stories of his brother Irving Penn on the Bauhaus, made a two-week visit and then enrolled as a student
« Report of Faculty Committee » (Wallen,: “Report of Faculty Committee” (Wallen, Levi, Rondthaler): Community Council of eight members (three teachers, three students, one representative of wives and employees, one of the community), joint disciplinary committee with power of exclusion, majority vote in the teaching profession due to lack of consensus, two-thirds referendum; adoption through community and faculty meetings
Grâce au GI Bill, 75 étudiants au printe: Thanks to the GI Bill, 75 students in the spring of 1946 on premises for up to 60
Albers évoque devant un étudiant le « bi: Albers speaks to a student about Wallen's “bid for power” and urges his own counsel to support his candidates in the Community Council elections
Photo 16 : institut d'été 1946 — Leo Ami: Photo 16: Summer Institute 1946 — Leo Amino, Jacob Lawrence, Leo Lionni, Ted and Bobbie Dreier, Beaumont Newhall, Gwendolyn Lawrence, Ise Gropius, Varda, Nan Newhall, Walter Gropius, Molly Gregory, Josef and Anni Albers
Wallen élu président du nouveau Communit: Wallen elected President of the new Community Council
Été 1946 : Institut de musique suspendu: Summer 1946: Institute of suspended music (departure of Fritz Cohen); Institute of Art: Jean Varda, Leo Amino, Jacob Lawrence, Concetta Scaravaglione, Balcomb Greene, Will Burtin, Leo Lionni, Beaumont Newhall, briefly Gropius
Arrivée de Karl Niebyl (économiste marxi: Arrival of Karl Niebyl (Marxist economist born in Prague, thesis burned by the Nazis, passed by Tulane, Carleton, Wisconsin) with three disciples; encourages engagement at the Southern Negro Youth Congress
Affaire du télégramme « 47 » ouvert par: Case of telegram “47” opened by mistake (47 votes the day before in community meeting): interrogation of a student; The telegram came from a Republican friend.
Groupe d'étude Wallen (15 à 20 personnes: Wallen Study Group (15-20 people, mostly students) on small communities; joint work weekends (barrage on the Eden Lake Feed Stream); prospecting of sites (Maine, Utah, Oregon); Rondthaler, Liz Gellhorn and Dave Resnik give up
1946-47 : 90 étudiants, plus de 50 % d'h: 1946-47: 90 students, more than 50% men (end of the “école de filles” character of the wartime); rejected candidates
Rondthaler obtient trois bâtiments des s: Rondthaler obtains three surplus military buildings: student studies, classrooms and reserve, and the first well-lit library (for Nell Rice, librarian); then government donations (printing press, furniture, typing, dishwasher, chopper, one hundred swivel chairs, sewer drain, pants press)
Deux couples quakers, les Clifford Mole: Two quakers, the Clifford Mole and the Raymond Trayer, take the farm; Farm expansion by students and teachers
Pas de déficit en 1946-47 et même une ré: No deficit in 1946-47 and even a reserve of $618.41; 1947-48: estimated income 115,239; expenditure 119,402 dollars; Rondthaler underexpenditure seven months; Recipient year through donations and summer institutes
Charlotte (« Bimbus ») Schlesinger engag: Charlotte (“Bimbus”) Schlesinger engaged in music; Johanna Jalowetz teaches singing and binding
Josef et Anni Albers en congé d'un an au: Josef and Anni Albers on one-year leave in Mexico; Ilya Bolotowsky (cited in its retrospective by J. B. Neumann, New Art Circle) replaces them; Trude Guermonprez, eldest daughter of the Jalowetz, teaches weaving in place of Anni Albers (1947) and remains assistant the following year
Ilya Bolotowsky enseigne la peinture (pe: Ilya Bolotowsky teaches painting (permissive, all styles), stays until spring 1948; turned into South Caroline Studebaker to buy alcohol (dry county)
Réunion de la communauté contre le dorto: Community meeting against TAC dormitory (“a barracks or a beach house”); preference for small dormitories of 10 to 14 people; student plans; Board pays TAC but gives up the project
Résolution des étudiants : admettre auta: Student resolution: admit as many black students as possible, including men; fundraising during Christmas holidays; the teaching body accepts unanimously black men
Trimestre d'hiver 1947 : cinq étudiants: Winter Quarter 1947: five black students, including two veterans; declared end of phase “expérimentale”, public declaration: “admission will be open to all students of all races”
Enquête auprès des anciens étudiants (ad: Survey of former students (admission to graduate school); Bulletin vol. 6 No. 1 (January 1948)
Edward Lowinsky part en Italie avec une: Edward Lowinsky goes to Italy with a Guggenheim scholarship, then to Queens College
Un groupe du Fellowship of Reconciliatio: A Fellowship of Reconciliation group, including Bayard Rustin, spends one night at the college on his trip to the South to test segregation (Journey of Reconciliation); BMC “the only known haven” of the region for interracial groups
« Re: Wallen Proposal » de Mary Caroline: “Re: Wallen Proposal” of Mary Caroline Richards (five pages); Permissive Board response; Albers opposition; Wallen keeps his resignation

Frank Rice, fils de John Andrew Rice, re: Frank Rice, son of John Andrew Rice, joins the teaching staff

Kenneth Noland suit un seul trimestre av: Kenneth Noland follows a single term with Albers and then works with Ilya Bolotowsky (replacing Albers for one year off in the late 1940s)

Cours de théâtre de Penn deux fois par s: Penn theatre course twice a week: 20-30 participants including Levi, M.C. Richards and Wallen; An Actor Preparations, improvisations; stage built at the end of the dining room (Penn reseals the old electrical board)

Sept ou huit étudiants (Paul Williams, A: Seven or eight students (Paul Williams, Al Lanier, Si Silmman) built the “Minimum House” for about a year (just over $1,000, paid by the mother of Paul Williams); the tombstone of Jalowetz mistakenly integrated to the bottom wall
Programme de l'automne 1947 : Levi (« Lo: Fall 1947 program: Levi (“Logic”, “The Individual in Society”), M. C. Richards (poetry, fiction), Rondthaler (latin, “History of the English Language”), Frank Rice (German, arrived in summer 1947), Wallen (“Group Process”), Max Dehn (“Problems of Philosophy”); Tasker Howard Jr., former NLRB student (economy); Natasha Goldowski (Physics, Chemistry; Old Manhattan Project) and his mother “Madame” (French, Russian)

Charles Bloomstein, expert-comptable, re: Charles Bloomstein, accountant, joins staff (college books, farm accounts, shop, workshops)
Retour des Albers du Mexique, « a few mo: Return of Mexico Albers, “a few months” prior to visit of Cage and Cunningham
Retour des Albers du Mexique « in the ea: Return of Albers from Mexico “in the early spring of 1948”; Albers disapproves of courses given by students and the weight of social sciences
Élèves de Bolotowsky contre Albers (« il: Students of Bolotowsky vs. Albers (“illusionnisme” material exercises); according to Bolotowsky, Albers makes the floor of the exhibition room too varnish to dry before varnishing

Nouveau versement sur la première hypoth: Repayment on first mortgage; a debt of $10,000 is first ranked ($1,000 per year over 10 years); Second $16,500 mortgage held by the Dreier family; loan of $9,500 from Stephen Forbes
Fondation de la communauté de l'Oregon p: Foundation of the Oregon community by the Wallenites (“an outgrowth of Black Mountain”); dissolved after three years; five-day annual meeting at Thanksgiving
Session d'été 1948 : 74 étudiants (moiti: Summer session 1948: 74 students (new half); guests: Willem and Elaine of Kooning, Richard and Louise Lippold (arrived in a hearse), Buckminster Fuller (invited by Albers), Peter Grippe, Richard Lischer (carpentry), Winslow Ames (stamp history, July), Beaumont Newhall (3rd summer, History of Photography), Charles Burchard (architecture, August), Erwin Bodky (“Sonatas of Beethoven”), Edgar Kaufmann Jr. (industrial design), Isaac Rosenfeld (Tolstoy, Writing), John Cage, Merce Cunningham; Josef Albers, Anni Albers, Trude Guermonprez
Cours d'architecture et d'ingénierie ind: Buckminster Fuller course in architecture and industrial engineering; four- to five-hour lectures with intermission and tables of geometric figures; friendship Fuller–of Kooning (courses to Asheville)
Unique concert solo de Merce Cunningham: Merce Cunningham's unique solo concert for the community, assisted by Louise Lippold (former student) and Sara Hamill (student); Cunningham course
« Amateur Festival » de Satie par Cage :: “Amateur Festival” of Satie by Cage: 25 concerts of half an hour, three nights a week after dinner, in the dining room or piano of its open windows cottage; plus a concert of his own works; Albers requires a ten minute talk before each concert
Mary Caroline Richards traduit Le Piège: Mary Caroline Richards translates Satie Medusa Trap from Rondthaler to Ocracoke, and returns towards the end of summer
Les Levi partent chez les Rondthaler à O: Levis leave for Rondthaler in Ocracoke, before Europe
Selon Bolotowsky, Levi lui propose de re: According to Bolotowsky, Levi offers to stay for “dump Albers”; he refuses; Bolotowsky leaves college
Dreier assure temporairement le rectorat: Dreier provides temporary rectorate after Levi's resignation
Au déjeuner, Levi propose comme recteur: At lunch, Levi offers as rector an “duel” in the kitchen (cold schnitzels against pancakes Suzette); food battle, “some thirty people got themselves pretty messed up”
À mi-parcours du festival, longue causer: Midway through the festival, long talk by Cage against Beethoven (“Beethoven was in error”); Erwin Bodky responds by a concert of Beethoven's last quartets preceded by a talk
Fuller tente d'ériger son premier grand: Fuller tries to erect its first large geodetic dome (aluminium venetian blinds, 15 m planned) in the rain: the “Supine Dome” does not stand
Répétitions ouvertes du Piège de Méduse: Open rehearsals of the Piège de Méduse; Arthur Penn called to stage; exercises for “make a damn fool of myself” with Fuller
Représentation du Piège de Méduse (The R: Representation of the Medusa Trap (The Ruse of Medusa) by Satie, Trad. Mr. C. Richards: Buckminster Fuller (Baron Medusa), Elaine of Kooning, Merce Cunningham (the mechanical monkey, tail drawn by Lippold), Isaac Rosenfeld, Alvin Charles Few (neve of cook Malrey Few); Kooning Willem sets; Cage on piano; Arthur Penn staging; Levi returns for the occasion
Les Levi partent pour leur année en Euro: Levis leave for their year in Europe
Effectif tombé de 90 à 50 étudiants à l': Dropped from 90 to 50 students in the fall of 1948; resignations displayed on the table; teaching staff: Anni and Josef Albers, Erwin Bodky, Trude Guermonprez, Johanna Jalowetz, Charlotte Schlesinger, Natasha Goldowski, Anna Goldowski, Frank Rice
Edward Dahlberg arrives to replace Mr. C. Richards (literature, writing); individual interviews (boys in his office, girls walking in the woods)
Premier séjour de Robert Rauschenberg, v: First stay of Robert Rauschenberg, come with Susan Weil; Albers finds it frivolous (“had nothing to teach him”)
Premier cours d'Olson à Black Mountain ;: First course from Olson to Black Mountain; a student Judge “basically a charlatan” (letter from Mel Mitchell Kelly to “Andy”, 20 Nov. 1949)
Séminaire non crédité de Natasha Goldows: Natasha Goldowski uncredited seminar on cybernetics based on the tests of Norbert Wiener's first book; Olson: a poet was missing
Charles Olson, enseignant invité : séjou: Charles Olson, guest teacher: monthly stays (often a week); seminars “Writing” and “Reading”, evening lectures (non-homeric myth, Melville), poetry readings, tarot; dance-mime production of Llanto por Ignacio Sánchez Mejías de García Lorca
Albers et Dreier en tournée dans le Nord: Albers and Dreier on tour in the North to solicit donations; Stephen Forbes refuses (“leaned slightly toward the Levi position”)
Première visite de N. O. Pittenger à la: First visit of N. O. Pittenger at the end of January, at the time of the crisis; he refuses to commit until the question of annuities (pension Albers–Jalowetz–Straus, vouchers in the name of Albers) is clarified
Le professeur Cole, auditeur de longue d: Professor Cole, a long-standing auditor, establishes the legality of the pension plan; 80% of the funds protected; Pittenger accepts an advisory role; Final emissions
Départ de Josef et Anni Albers, Trude Gu: Departure of Josef and Anni Albers, Trude Guermonprez and Charlotte Schlesinger after the end of their courses; Nell Rice remains alone in the 1933 group
Juste avant la session d'été, visites de: Just before the summer session, visits by Langston Hughes and Bortai Bunting, daughter of Basil Bunting
Session d'été 1949 dirigée par Fuller (p: Summer 1949 session led by Fuller (more than 50 students): John Walley and Emerson Woelffer (Institute of Design, Drawing, Painting, Sculpture), Diana Woelffer and Jane Walley (ceramic, Jewellery, Photography), nine design engineers from the Institute of Design; Marli Ehrman (weaving), Betty and Pete Jennerjahn (dance, printing), Nataraj Vashi and Pia-Veena (dance and Hindu philosophy), James Albert Pait, Nathan Rosen, John Scholtz (symposiums on infinity); Erwin Bodky (music)
Le dôme de Fuller (hémisphère de 4,3 m e: The dome of Fuller ( 4.3 m hemisphere in aviation aluminum tubes and Vinylite, built at the Institute of Design) stands; engineering tests; he collapsed in September
Grande fête de Fuller pour la communauté: Fuller's great celebration for the community: a student reads aloud one of his two hundred-page poems, read to the end
Festival Bach de trois jours dirigé par: Three-day Bach Festival directed by Erwin Bodky (who leaves the faculty in autumn)
Les Rondthaler reviennent quelques semai: The Ronthaler are back for a few weeks; appeal of funds to elders; Forbes maintains the mortgage and releases the gravel ground; the Board suspends the monthly rents of the Albers for the summer
Soirée de Charles Olson « Wagadu, after: Charles Olson “Wagadu, after Frobenius” Evening: poetry, mime, music, color, dance (“jointure of speech-sound-motion”); his plan to bring his troupe of Washington (Odyssey) refused for lack of funds
Le corps enseignant donne à Pittenger «: The teaching staff gives Pittenger “all administrative prerogatives”: he becomes rector while waiting for a holder
Rentrée 1949 (~45 étudiants) : retour de: Return 1949 (~45 students): return of Mr. C. Richards and Bill Levi, full-time Max Dehn, David Corkran (history); Hazel Larsen (photography), Jennerjahn (“Color”, “Modern Dance”), Joe Fiore (drawing, painting), Johanna Jalowetz; recruited quakers: John McCandless (printing), Don Warrington (treasurer), Vollmer and Louise Hetherington (music), Robert C. Turner (ceramic, oven-built); Paul Leser and Flola Shepard from Olivet
Olson commence les Maximus Poems (dix dé: Olson starts Maximus Poems (ten already written when Williams decides to publish them)
Creeley, à Littleton (New Hampshire), ra: Creeley, Littleton, New Hampshire, misses a review; by Cid Corman (program “This Is Poetry”, Boston), receives poems from Olson and replies that it seems “looking for a language”: beginning of their correspondence, intense during the stay of Olson at Yucatán (1950-51)
Réunion de deux jours chez Stephen Forbe: Two-day meeting at Stephen Forbes: six former students (including Morton Steinau and Tasker Howard), Pittenger and Corkran propose an Board of Overseass (choice and revocation of the Rector, salaries, budget, recruitment, fundraising)
Visite de Stephen Forbes au college en v: Visit of Stephen Forbes to the college on holiday: leans for the idea of Levi (add five or six non-residents to the Board); offers up to $6,000 for a new science building; Find a Rector
Joel Oppenheimer à Black Mountain (1950-: Joel Oppenheimer to Black Mountain (1950-1953): painting, printing, poetry with M. C. Richards, relaxation exercises with Paul Goodman (summer 1950), then two years in the Olson workshop
Arrivée de Joel Oppenheimer (20 ans, ren: Arrival of Joel Oppenheimer (20 years old, dismissed from Cornell and University of Chicago)
Session d'été 1950 (huit semaines) : Pau: Summer session 1950 (eight weeks): Paul Goodman (writing), Clement Greenberg (history and art critic), Theodoros Stamos (painting), Katherine Litz (dance), Leo Amino (sculpture), Robert Klein (theatre)
« Homosexual summer » : réunions d'étudi: “Homosexual summer”: Student meetings on the “question Goodman” ( favorable majority); opposition of Quakers and Dehn; Goodman, accused of urinating behind a tree during a softball game
En pleine réunion, Ray Trayer frappe Bil: In the middle of the meeting, Ray Trayer hits Bill Levi (defence of Goodman, remark on the farm); Joel Oppenheimer jumps on the back of Trayer (“The Wild Bull of the Campus”); Johanna Jalowetz encourages it
Le corps enseignant vote nettement contr: The teaching staff voted strongly against maintaining Goodman for the year
Corkran décide de partir ; avec lui Tray: Corkran decides to leave; with him Trayer, Quakers and Goldowski abandon (Goldowski marries an older student)
Corkran à Forbes (puis 27 mars 1951) : «: Corkran to Forbes (then March 27, 1951): “a situation to me personally repugnant and institutionally impossible”; departure of Corkran and Quakers
Bill Levi quitte la communauté (son mari: Bill Levi leaves the community (his marriage was defeated)
Après le départ de Bill Levi (déc. 1950): After the departure of Bill Levi (Dec. 1950), Mary Caroline Richards remains and makes the separation final; Wes Huss invites Levi to dinner with Natasha Goldowski before departure
Séparation de Bill Levi et Mary Caroline: Separation of Bill Levi and Mary Caroline Richards
Photos de Jonathan Williams : Charles Ol: Photos of Jonathan Williams : Charles Olson writing Maximus (1951); Francine of Plessix and Joel Oppenheimer (summer 1951)
Visite de Boris Aronson, décorateur, ave: Visit of Boris Aronson, decorator, with his wife Lisa (daughter of the Jalowetz): lectures by Olson “the most exciting thing you ever experienced”
Atelier d'écriture d'Olson dans la salle: Olson writing workshop in the Studies Building magazine room (smoke, cashmere sweater on the head): you must bring a text to enter; text readings sent by Creeley (“Mr. Blue”) or Duncan; “new sciences of man” diagrams (Mark Hedden log); “Gothic seizure” of Jack Rice; Paul Leser invited when it comes to African anthropology
Départs du printemps 1951 : les Jennerja: Spring 1951 departures: Jennerjahn (France, GI Bill), Robert Turner (pottery in the state of New York), Trayer (Earlham), Paul Leser (Hartford Seminary); resignation of 24 April 1951: “I am in love with [Black Mountain]”), Natasha Goldowski (one year in Paris)
Seuls deux recrutements acceptés : Victo: Only two accepted recruitments: Victor Sprague (biology) and John Adams (anthropology)
Premier numéro d'Origin de Cid Corman: First issue of Cid Corman's Origin
Charles Olson revient s'installer à Blac: Charles Olson returns to Black Mountain, from Lerma (Yucatán), with y & x and Call Me Ishmael; Ed Dorn prints on the A Letter for Melville college press
Session d'été 1951 (~50 étudiants, équil: Summer session 1951 (~50 students, financial balance): photography workshop (Hazel-Frieda Larsen, Harry Callahan, Arthur Siegel, Aaron Siskind); Katherine Litz; first stays of David Tudor and Lou Harrison; Ben Shahn (“Jolly Tales from the Hassidim”) and Robert Motherwell do not agree
Comédie musicale Flabbergasted de l'étud: Flabbergasted musical comedy of student Jay Watt, dances of Katherine Litz (also a dance inspired by the Mayan glyphs of Olson); “Light-Sound-Movement Workshop” : Nick Cernovich “after the Noh tradition”
Francine du Plessix (Gray) passe les été: Francine of Plessix (Gray) spends summers 1951 and 1952 to Black Mountain, first for painting, then in the writing course of Olson (Dostoevski, Notes of an Underground; newspaper habit; “Stop all this third person writing”)
David Tudor joue la Deuxième Sonate de B: David Tudor plays the Second Boulez Sonata; Olson: “the only piece of music since Bach”
Jonathan Williams à San Francisco (Rexro: Jonathan Williams in San Francisco (Rexroth, Duncan, Henry Miller): Jargon No. 1, Broadside from one of his poems engraved by David Ruff
Jonathan Williams à Black Mountain : pho: Jonathan Williams to Black Mountain: photography at the Rolleiflex with Aaron Siskind, writing course of Olson one night per week (one session from 7 p.m. to 11 p.m. extended at Ma Peak's tavern then all night and the next); two months of antagonism with Olson
The Black Mountain Review, vol. 1, no 1: The Black Mountain Review, vol. 1, No. 1 (only issue), college review: ed. M. C. Richards, Joel Oppenheimer, Mary Fitton, Alex Kemeny, Hazel Larsen; No. by Nick Cernovich, Goldowski on “High Speed Computing Machines”, poems by Russell Edson and Oppenheimer, “Father” by Fielding Dawson; a second number composed but never printed
Jargon nos 2 à 4 imprimés à Black Mounta: Jargon Nos. 2 to 4 printed at Black Mountain: No. 2 (Oppenheimer poem, Rauschenberg drawing, 150 ex., ~50 dollars), No. 3 (“Red/Gray”, six Williams poems), No. 4 (Victor Kalos poems, Dan Rice drawings)
Programme d'« institutes » d'Olson : cin: Olson “institutes” program: five eight-week institutes (crafts; theatre — Boris Aronson projected; “new sciences of man” — Christopher Hawkes approached; natural sciences; arts in summer); Catalogue 1952-53 inflated (Goldowski, briefly returned, nine prices ; Huss eight; Sprague ten; Doyle Jones “Timber Operations”)
Ben Shahn, en conférence au Philadelphia: Ben Shahn, a lecture at the Philadelphia Museum, talks about Black Mountain; Michael Rumaker hears it
Jonathan Williams incorporé dans l'armée: Jonathan Williams joined the army in January 1952 (two years, especially in Stuttgart: Rainer Maria Gerhardt, the Cantz printer); inheritance of $1,500 of Charles Neal dedicated to Maximus Poems of Olson
Session d'été 1952 (~70 personnes) : Cha: Summer session 1952 (~70 people): Charles Olson, Franz Kline, John Cage, Merce Cunningham, David Tudor, Robert Rauschenberg (revenue, married to Sue Weil), Stefan Wolpe and Hilda Morley (arrived at the beginning of the session); Katherine Litz
Stefan Wolpe remplace Lou Harrison (Gugg: Stefan Wolpe replaces Lou Harrison (Guggenheim 1952-53) in composition; Hilda Morley teaches literature and Hebrew; Wolpe remains after 1953 (Cage talks about “usurpation”)
Cage annonce un cours de composition où: Cage announces a compositional course where students would be its apprentices for the Williams Mix (funded by Paul and Vera Williams): none enrolled; conversations and strippoker games
Cunningham souffre de l'appendicite (rég: Cunningham suffers from appendicitis (regime, ice pocket); Olson may be taking her dance class that summer (“like a light walrus”)
Karen Karnes et David Weinrib arrivent c: Karen Karnes and David Weinrib arrive as resident potters ($80 per month) in the workshop built by Robert Turner; “potters-in-residence” excluding teaching staff first year
Creeley déjà invité à enseigner en 1952: Creeley already invited to teach in 1952 and announced in the brochure of the summer session (writing course)
Événement « mixed media » de Cage dans l: “mixed media” event of Cage in the dining room (Theatre Piece No. 1): Cage on a scale or a lutrin (Zen, Meister Eckhart ?), poems of Olson and M. C. Richards, paintings and gramophone of Rauschenberg, David Tudor on a prepared piano, Merce Cunningham dancing in the alleys pursued by a dog, films and slides, coffee served in white cups; until 10:30 p.m. Stefan Wolpe goes out protesting; Johanna Jalowetz: “Deep in the middle ages”; Franz Kline in the public
Lecture intégrale de nuit par Cage du Hu: Full night reading by Cage of Huang Po Doctrine of Universal Mind (20-30 listeners); readings by Artaud with David Tudor and M. C. Richards
« Institute of the New Sciences of Man »: “Institute of the New Sciences of Man”: three-week archaeology and mythology seminar with Olson, Robert Braidwood (Jarmo) and Marie-Louise von Franz (near Jung); Christopher Hawkes is not coming
Fin du troupeau de bovins : vache morte,: End of cattle herd: dead cow, mammalites, manure, escaped herd (Olson moguling in meadows), auction at the time of a fall in prices
Récolte de tabac décevante ; Jack Rice (: Disappointing tobacco harvest; Jack Rice (Dan's brother) resigns after an argument with Huss (Olson carries an “I am exonerated” sign)
Mort de Max Dehn d'une crise cardiaque p: Death of Max Dehn from a heart attack shortly after the destruction of the dogwood forest; buried in the woods of the college
Arrivée de Michael Rumaker avec une bour: Arrival of Michael Rumaker with a scholarship (like Ed Dorn): farm (silo), then cook seven days a week; three years
Olson démolit en classe la nouvelle de R: Olson demolishes in class the news of Rumaker on the south of Philadelphia; soon after, “The Truck”, its first published news, well received
Olson, à la dernière table non débarrass: Olson, at last table not cleared: “I’m more important than any fucking dishwasher!”
Le Community Council « reinvigorated » (: The Community Council “reinvigorated” (about five months: dog dumps at Studies Building, Fielding Dawson and heating, Tinkerbelle the dog of Paul Goodman guarded by Tim La Farge, recorders, cowboy students at the cinema) resigns in block
Fin 1953, Creeley accepte de diriger une: At the end of 1953, Creeley agreed to conduct a new Black Mountain Review from Majorca (“with Olson as mentor”); the college finances 400 to 500 dollars per issue (400-500 ex.), printed in Spain by Mossén Alcovar
Arthur Penn commence à réaliser pour la: Arthur Penn starts making for TV
Les Creeley quittent Aix-en-Provence (vo: The Creeleys left Aix-en-Provence (near Mitchell Goodman and Denise Levertov) for Majorca: Roebuck Press with Martin and Janet Seymour-Smith, then Various Press (in 1954: Mayan Letters and In Cold Hell, in Olson's Thicket, Blackburn, Layton, Eigner, Duncan, Caesars Gate)
Jonathan Williams rencontre Creeley lors: Jonathan Williams meets Creeley during a visit to Mallorca
Dernière session d'été : Esteban Vicente: Last summer session: Esteban Vicente (painting), David Tudor (Beethoven to warm up, we come to listen), Merce Cunningham without Cage with his company — Carolyn Brown, Viola Farber, Marianne Preger (Simon), Anita Dencks, Jo Anne Melsher, Remy Charlip, Paul Taylor; Franz Kline and Jack Tworkov; second ceramic institute (Karnes, Weinrib, Daniel Rhodes, Warren MacKenzie, Peter Voulkos)
Six semaines de Cunningham : cours le ma: Six weeks of Cunningham: lessons in the morning, rehearsals in the afternoon and evening in the dining room; Anita Dencks catches mumps after two weeks; beginner students (Harvey Lichtenstein, James Leo Herlihy — was uncertain); Remy Charlip composes her first dance
Cunningham crée quatre danses — « Septet: Cunningham creates four dances — “Septet”, “Banjo” (Gottschalk, Tudor on piano), “Dime a Dance” (Tudor), “Untitled Solo” (Christian Wolff) — and takes over “Suite by Chance”; three shows for the community
Concert de musique de Stefan Wolpe prépa: Stefan Wolpe music concert prepared by David Tudor
Passage au système trimestriel ; frais r: Transfer to the quarterly system; reduced costs from $1,600 to $850; campus low (dining room–Studies Building) closed then rented: end of twenty years of meals in common; estimated budget of $25,000 per year
Démissions de Malrey Few (cuisinier de l: Resignations of Malrey Few (long-time cook), Flola Shepard and Len Billing; end of GI Bill; late 1953, 24 students and more cash salaries for months; Johanna Jalowetz joins her daughters after selling part of the collection of Jalowetz (partitions by Schönberg)
Hiver 1954-55, le plus bas : une tentati: Winter 1954-55, the lowest: a suicide attempt, a fire that destroys almost all Joe Fiore's paintings, no money for coal; nine students and half a dozen teachers
Doyle Jones quitte brusquement la ferme: Doyle Jones suddenly leaves the farm; two students succeed him; in 1955 the farm stopped operating
Jonathan Williams, revenu de l'armée (fa: Jonathan Williams, a return from the army (family in Highlands), goes and comes to Black Mountain until 1956; publishes Anecdotes of the Late War and Maximus 11/22 by Olson (350 e.g. in 1956, 25 subscribers at $25)
Départ de Flola Shepard : fin de tout en: Flola Shepard's departure: the end of all social engagement; two black students came by car from Asheville to take some courses
Doyle Jones quitte la ferme, vaches vend: Doyle Jones leaves the farm, cows sold; end of free food (heat plates, small refrigerators); 2 dollars a week (Eric Weinberger); Black Mountain A&P food flights; Tord-boyaux bought by Doyle at $5 a gallon
Creeley arrive à Black Mountain à 8 heur: Creeley arrives at Black Mountain at 8 am after a night drive from New York in pick-up from 1940; Olson, naked in a napkin, receives it and makes it teach the same evening
Premier cours de Creeley dans la grande: First Creeley course in the Studies Building large conference room (six students, Karen Karnes asks him to speak louder); then small room: Hart Crane, W. C. Williams, Miles Davis, Charlie Parker, Bud Powell
Déclaration sur « the situation of the C: Statement on “the situation of the College” to Elders, Friends and Foundations (“expansion” Projects, Administrative Secretary)
The Black Mountain Review no 1 (64 p.) :: The Black Mountain Review No. 1 (64 p.): “On First Looking Out of La Cosa’s Eyes” and “Against Wisdom As Such” by Olson, poems by Creeley, Blackburn, Layton, Eigner, eight reproductions by René Laubies; Associate Editors Blackburn, Layton, Olson, Rexroth (who withdrew due to articles by Seymour-Smith on Roethke and Dylan Thomas)
Forbes accepte de reporter un billet hyp: Forbes agrees to postpone a expired mortgage note (again in April 1955)
The Black Mountain Review no 3 : Duncan,: The Black Mountain Review No. 3: Duncan, “Letters for Denise Levertov: An A Muse Ment” (Levertov sees a parody, Olson an attack); Note by Creeley on Rexroth's withdrawal
Triangle amoureux Creeley–Dan Rice–une é: Love Triangle Creeley–Dan Rice–a student; Jargon publishes All That Is Lovely in Men (poems of Creeley, drawings of Dan Rice); Jargon #7: The Immoral Creeley Proposal (Laubiès drawings; 18 ex. sold out of 200)
Creeley boit l'après-midi au Ma Peak's t: Creeley drinks in the afternoon at Ma Peak's tavern; Grey Stone picks him up in pick-up on class nights (“Now, teach”)
Le college accepte un fils déficient men: The college accepts a mentally impaired son of a rich Southerner who announces his decision by flying over the college and beating wings; We're looking for the plane three or four days: it never comes
Un habitant des collines vient provoquer: An inhabitant of the hills causes Olson (“the giant that walks the roads at night”): Olson breaks his jaw
Au retour du Ma Peak's tavern, Tom Field: Upon the return of the Ma Peak's tavern, Tom Field, harassed by Creeley, throws the car against the fireplace of a campus cottage (Rumaker on the steps): Field broken leg, Dan Rice back (corset six months), Creeley shoulder unloaded (15 dollars insurance)
Juste avant Noël 1954, la communauté sus: Just before Christmas 1954, the community suspended all courses for three months; Creeley already gone (back to summer); half of the group is leaving; 8 to 10 people remain; final closing rumor
Photos de Jonathan Williams : Robert Cre: Photos of Jonathan Williams : Robert Creeley (“Portrait as a Spanish Assassin”), Dan Rice and Creeley
Pendant la suspension, tournée de collec: During the suspension, collection tour from former supporters; Nell Rice mission to Stephen Forbes leads to an input procedure
Arrivée de Don Mixon comme étudiant: Arrival of Don Mixon as a student
Olson se sépare de Connie : il a un fils: Olson separates from Connie: he has a son (Charles Peter) with student Betty Kaiser
Karen Karnes et David Weinrib rejoignent: Karen Karnes and David Weinrib join the Stony Point (Rockland County) colony of Paul Williams, where Cage, Cunningham, M.C. Richards and David Tudor will come
Premier séjour de Robert Duncan à Black: First stay from Robert Duncan to Black Mountain
Nell Rice, Hazel Larsen et Natasha Goldo: Nell Rice, Hazel Larsen and Natasha Goldowski write to the 19 former teachers creditors of arrears for trial; most refuse
Robert Hellman (« The Quay », BMR no 1): Robert Hellman (“The Quay”, BMR No. 1) teaches languages about six months from the summer of 1955; Tony Landreau (weaving, Dorothy Liebes student) restarts the Studies Building basement trades; short come from Martin Sprengling (Oriental Institute)
The Black Mountain Review, été 1955 : «: The Black Mountain Review, summer 1955: “Sound of Talking” by James Purdy, perhaps his first American publication
Michael Rumaker « diplômé » : programme: Michael Rumaker “diplômé”: Olson program (the Greeks, Shakespeare, the novel), Robert Duncan external examiner; party and diploma calligraphed by Joe Fiore (accepted in 1968 by New School and Columbia)
Le cours d'Olson devient « The Present »: The Olson course becomes “The Present” (pre-reading of the New York Times and Asheville Citizen-Times); Duncan teaches, including a course in Persian history; Dan Rice learns trumpet and Spanish (to John and Elaine Chamberlain)
