Where their German equivalents would take the waters to Baden-Baden or play baccarat, Ted and Bobbie Dreier go on a backpack hike and join the road maintenance team. Anni and Josef adapt quickly, Anni especially. ion column bug; backpack instead of cures; road crew instead of baccarat
Les étudiants, entraînés par la table al: The students, trained by the German Emmy Zastrow table, repeated welcoming phrases that they forget by climbing the steps; Anni discovers the wooden doric columns with a buggy photo; during the ceremony, Albers says “I want to open eyes”; a woman asks her age, “quarante-cinq”, and declares that he will never learn English Words: “I want to open eyes” / “Then you will never learn English, it's too late” Atmosphere: warm and disconcerting, collision of two worlds Issue: the arrival of Europeans in the rural South; the initial linguistic injury
En visite à Thanksgiving 1933, Wunsch tr: On a visit to Thanksgiving 1933, Wunsch finds students and teachers hate Rollins, speaking day and night; discouraged, he delays his arrival; At Thanksgiving 1934, he found the college standing, engaged in a positive program, Rollins forgotten Words: “J'ai découvert le collège sur ses pieds… activement engagé dans un programme positif. Rollins semblait oublié. J'étais enthousiaste.” Atmosphere: De disappointment with enthusiasm in one year Issue: Can the college define itself differently than against Rollins
Après l'accostage du S.S. Europa (10 heu: After the landing of the S.S. Europa (10 hours late, hurricane), the Albers dine with Ted Dreier's parents, meet Aint Kate and Duchamp, visit his Brancusi exhibition, meet Grosz, their benefactors and the former Bauhäusler Drewes. Words: Albers on Duchamp: “a great fellow”; on Grosz: “sehr sympathisch”. Atmosphere: New York Warming, Thanksgiving Weekend, Hand-Wide World of Art Issue: The Old World (Duchamp, Grosz, Drewes) welcomes Bauhaus survivors.
Le premier jour, la secrétaire du collèg: On the first day, the secretary of the college, “une fille très saine et appétissante”, greets the couple on the porch, barefoot in sandals. Words: Anni, inside: “Well maybe this is a true story” (Maybe it's a real story). Atmosphere: The summum of the American informal seen by a Berliner; Southern Light, Blue Ridge View Issue: Anni measures in a body detail that proclaimed freedom is real.
Trois étudiants proposent de créer une f: Three students propose to create a farm to save and build the community; long conversation, then vote unanimously. Atmosphere: Long and lively debate before unanimity. Issue: Institutional birth of the farm, symbol of the community project.
Les reporters mitraillent le professeur: The reporters are firing the refugee professor; someone shouts to photograph the woman too; When Anni Loved Words: Atmosphere reporters cry: flashes, spontaneous American camaraderie Issue: home country of adoption
À leur arrivée, les Albers découvrent un: When they arrive, the Albers discover an opinion fixed by a punaise on an ionic column Atmosphere: cultural shock: in Germany the columns are marble Issue: America without aristocracy: first step of adaptation
Photographes mitraillent Josef ; un cri: Photographers machine-gun Josef; a cry: “prenons aussi la femme”; Anni delighted sees American kindness there; Johnson waiting at the landing place Words: “Let's get the wife, too” — “Prenons aussi la femme” Atmosphere: flashes, confused joy, seal coat, top shape Issue: Anni accepts the role of woman of the famous while keeping her reserved dignity
Minutes dactylographiées des réunions de: Typed minutes of the faculty meetings of 7 November and 7 December 1933; For the first years, these reports, written by Mangold, do not say “rien du tout, sauf qui était présent et quelles actions ont été prises”.
Pour entrer dans l'éthos du XVIIIe siècl: To enter the ethos of the eighteenth century, the members mounted the room of Congreve. A scene was built by closing part of the dining room by curtains; rehearsals from October. At Christmas, Rice, who was supposed to play a role like all members, still didn't know his lines and refused to learn them, “catégorique et provoquant”; Peggy Loram “ne pouvait pas survivre” at extended coaching; the play was played in front of half of the college that did not participate, Rice carrying a text of blower rolled like toilet paper. Curtains in the dining room; quick “comme du papier toilette” roll script; prayers for memory of Rice. Consequences: Vibrant success, unbridled party after the curtain; The community saw the illustration of two convictions: the falseness of the curricular/extracurricular distinction and the central place of art.
À la même réunion, la faculté vote pour: At the same meeting, the faculty votes to encourage candidates to submit personal works (poem, new, painting); On a motion of Peggy Loram, “étudiants spéciaux”s can register for any course with the agreement of the teacher, without preconditions. Atypical Form Questions: “Si vous ne comptez pas être diplômé, quel est votre plan ?”; “Si vos notes de secondaire sont mauvaises, comment l'expliquez-vous ?”
Plusieurs élèves tombent aussitôt en ret: Several students immediately fall behind in school fees; Dreier reports to Board that it is unlikely to recover everything. fee set at $340 + $340 for room and board; Cumulative $1,200 in the third year Consequences:
Warburg, trustee du Museum of Modern Art: Warburg, trustee of the Museum of Modern Art, states that Albers could fundamentally change the teaching methods of art in this country; his main interest is to draw the creative possibilities of his students through experimental technical exercises.
Lors de la cérémonie d'accueil, interrog: During the welcoming ceremony, questioned about what he hoped to achieve in the United States, Albers, gathering his meagre English, answered simply: “I want to open eyes”. The article presents it as “internationalement connu pour sa méthode inhabituelle d'enseignement de l'art”. Consequences: Formula that summarizes his pedagogy: open the vision, form an audience for abstraction
Répétitions depuis octobre ; à Noël Rice: Repeated since October; At Noël Rice always ignores his lines and refuses, categorically and provokingly, to learn them; Loram at the edge of collapse; Last connections, prayers for memory of Rice, representation in front of half of the college; Rice follows the scene with its text of blower rolled like toilet paper; triumph and unbridled celebration. Atmosphere: Collective farce, comic suspense, final euphoria. Issue: Does the founder refuse to learn or test the community? Art in the center against the vanity of the role.
Le couple fraîchement débarqué d'Allemag: The newly landed couple from Germany are welcomed; Josef is asked what it hopes to achieve in the United States; he gathers his little English and simply answers “I want to open eyes” Words: “I want to open eyes” — I want to open my eyes Atmosphere: Emotion of a providential exile, tension of recent immigrants Issue: What the Bauhaus brings to America, condensed in one sentence
La designer cubaine Clara Porset, formée: La Cuban designer Clara Porset, trained in New York and Paris in the 1920s and interested in the Bauhaus approach, went from Havana to Black Mountain to discover the teaching of Josef, and was conquered; She immediately invited the couple to Cuba. Porset quote: “Albers enseigne avec la prodigalité de qui possède un trésor inépuisable” (article in Ahora, late December 1934-early January 1935) Consequences: First Latin voyage of the couple, December 1934
Josef Albers photographie plusieurs port: Josef Albers photographed several portraits of Clara Porset during a visit to La Havana. Several photographs kept Consequences: Beginning of the relationship with Porset
Josef érige les cours d'art au centre du: Josef places art courses at the centre of the curriculum. Anni returns to weaving and, in the autumn, enters the claustre and develops a new complex theoretical and didactic program for the weaving workshop.
La designer et architecte cubaine, formé: La Cuban designer and architect, trained in New York and Paris in the 1920s, sought to know the Bauhaus approach to design and contacted Josef shortly after his arrival in the United States; She goes from Havana to Black Mountain to experience her first-hand teaching and is not disappointed. Consequences: She immediately invites Josef and Anni to Cuba
Josef place les cours d'art au centre de: Josef places art classes at the centre of education at BMC; Anni becomes a faculty again in the fall and develops a theoretical and didactic program for the weaving workshop. Invited by Cuban designer Clara Porset (arrival to BMC in September), Josef gives a three-day lecture cycle at the Havana Lyceum (ex women's club of 1928, later merged with the Lawn Tennis Club). The Albers drive Dreier with Ted and Bobbie. trip 1934-12-28 – 1935-01-16; letter to Gropius of January 22, 1935: coffee, beans, black cigarettes, real rum
« L'année dernière » (par rapport à 1935: “L'année dernière” (compared to 1935), students take over farm management on their own; During the summer, some by rotation stay on site to prepare the harvests, which the whole college harvests in the fall, without conflict with the academic calendar. Summer guard bearings; collective fall harvest; economic benefit for college Consequences: Model of collective tasks replacing artificial sport from other schools
Rice regrette rapidement d'avoir fait de: Rice quickly regrets having made Georgia the rector: he thinks Georgia does not understand the wish that “le chef ne soit pas réellement chef” and would like to invest the function of more authority. Georgia gladly gives the office to Rice after a year, to the slight astonishment of Rice, in which this ease shakes his subconscious belief in demonology. It remains to be seen whether Rice will stick to the idea of a purely protocol rectorate.
Dès le printemps de la première année, d: As early as the spring of the first year, formal amendments to the statutes gave every member of the college the right to inspect all the registers of the corporation, recognized the student body's right to adopt a constitution for its own government, guaranteed student representatives to attend and speak at the ordinary meetings of the faculty, and gave the Student Moderator an effective seat at the Board of Fellows. Dreier had publicly announced that no significant decisions would be made about the students without consulting them. Consequences: Student representation superior to most colleges, but not equal: Rice admits that some (fellows) are “plus égaux que d'autres”
Après une visite en 1934 à la Lincoln Sc: After a visit to Lincoln School in 1934, a bastion of progressive education, Rice judges the place almost lifeless, “courant sur quelque chose qui s'est passé il y a longtemps”; The overwhelming observation: progressive education when it is stupid is “bien plus bête que l'autre sorte”. Consequences: strengthens the educational anti-dogmatism of BMC
Chaque été, la Blue Ridge Assembly de l': Every summer, the Blue Ridge Assembly of the Protestant Church takes over its buildings for its conferences; Some members of the college stay there to manage day-to-day business. La, second year, is Fred Mangold (modern language instructor) and his wife Isabel. Mangold describes an “neuf cents crétins végétariens, tous adventistes du septième jour” convention; a Christian dies from an afternoon of sun baseball followed by a dip in the lake; castration of the farmer's pig; YMCA secretaries who laugh Consequences: Ironic bulletins sent to dispersed members of the college
Long passage du journal écrit à la fin d: Long passage from the newspaper written at the end of the first year: John was in love with “Paul” despite him, despite his attachment to someone else at New York; he confessed his affection, which embarrassed and shocked Paul by his lack of reserve; Then “Ann” and Paul began to weave a canvas around them.
Fin de la première année du collège : Jo: End of the first year of the college: John, a lover of “Paul” despite himself (dedicated to someone else at New York), declares his affection; Paul is embarrassed, shocked by the lack of reserve; “Ann” and Paul then bind together, John avoids Paul, Ann the rail of “self-dramatization”; the episode is visible from the whole community in this closed universe. John polished if it crosses Paul; “sel sur une plaie”; Work more depressing than ever Consequences: decrease of John in group esteem
Rice fait parler John de ce qui le boule: Rice makes John speak of what upsets him, sees the situation as it is, and then exposes to him the seriousness of the understatements and criticisms aroused, destroying John's regained confidence. Rice “brise” John's new confidence Consequences: John hangs on to his friends “du Nord” and the feeling of having tried everything for the college
Deuxième année : des étudiants ouvrent u: Second year: students open a cooperative shop briefly every day; the college creates its printing house; library shelving, weaving and furniture; a “Cottage School” for young children (the oldest schooled in the village) is held by students, frequented for a time by children of the city. sale of cigarettes, paper, chocolate bars, instant cocoa; Chronic imbalance cases; departure of children from the city when “l'évolution” is discussed Consequences: self-sufficiency attempts
Wunsch refusant le gîte et le couvert (i: Wunsch refusing lodging and cover (he must support his mother and sister), students collect a thousand dollars for his salary; a part of the teaching staff, living with money, designs resentment; Inconclusive general meeting. $1,000; Rice adjourns the meeting: “there's no consensus here”; advises students to persuade opponents. Consequences: Wunsch finally receives its invitation.
Premier jour : Dewey déçoit légèrement l: Day one: Dewey slightly disappoints the community because it “ne s'enthousiasme pas visiblement” like previous visitors; he quietly observes, gently discourages being treated in the Grand Philosopher, attends every day during Rice, walks quietly and drinks beer with the students in the evening. Another visit during 1934-35 accompanied him by Albert Barnes, an art collector. Every evening before dinner, whiskey with Dewey and two or three people, offered by Barnes (one full box of “whisky divin” according to Rice) Consequences: After his second visit, Dewey agreed to sit on the College Advisory Board
Avant que le collège n'ait six mois, Wil: Before the college was six months old, Wilder, invited by John Evarts he knew at Yale, conquered the college: dinners with students, endless questions, anecdotes about the famous (Elinor Wylie, Spengler, the Lunt, Woolcott, Ruth Gordon, Katharine Hepburn), evenings to read his plays in one act in front of the large fireplace of the hall of Lee Hall, an evening at the cottage of the Dreier with the Albers and Evarts (alternative German and English conversation), a public lecture, and a final interview with Rice. He buys a wood engraving of Albers for 10 dollars (special price) and Albers adds a second as a gift; he leaves $25 to the library fund; 250 guests outside the conference Consequences: Wilder promises to try to come back in spring (Rice had offered him a semester of teaching per year); compliments the emotional climate but suggests more human diversity and “un peu plus de discipline intellectuelle”
En sa qualité de recteur, Georgia rappel: As Rector, Georgia reminds the community that it will be judged by the quality of the intellectual work accomplished; the past year has produced it, but far from what the group is capable of; Without significant progress, the college would lose much of its raison d'être. Consequences: Affirmation of the centrality of academic work
Le Bulletin n° 2 (1934), traduit de l'al: Bulletin No. 2 (1934), translated from German by Ted Dreier, who returned with Albers “chaque nuance de sens de chaque phrase chaque soir pendant un mois”. a month of translation evenings Consequences: major text on Albers pedagogy
Albers livre un texte élaborant ses exer: Albers delivers a text developing its material exercises and their raison d'être: optical and tactile perception, primary need to touch materials. Consequences: Founded BMC theory of subject studies.
Albers publie dans le Black Mountain Col: Albers publishes in Black Mountain College Bulletin an essay explaining the logic of his pedagogy of drawing: drawing as a visual language, exclusion from drawing of expression at the beginning, elementary teaching as strictly objective craftsmanship. Consequences: this text sets the basic themes of its drawing course
Dans les premières années du cours de co: In the early years of the color course at Black Mountain, Albers devotes the first sessions to known color systems; later (to Yale), he reserved them at the last week of the course, island of theory in a course that celebrates empirical observation. The Goethe triangle, the Schopenhauer wheel, the Runge globe, the systems of Albert Munsell and Wilhelm Ostwald.
Dans l'année suivant son arrivée, Albers: In the year following its arrival, Albers publishes a statement: after the fundamental studies (drawing, design, color) that occupy half a year, not eager to paint; studies after nature or model concern the relationship between colour, shape and space. Cite Rembrandt who, at the age of 30, would have felt the need for twenty years of study for a color-space problem. Consequences: Displays the fears of a teacher who has to build a course by training himself.
Approché au nom d'Albers par Edward Warb: Approached in the name of Albers by Edward Warburg of MoMA, Sawyer, director of the gallery, agrees to show a group of prints of Albers. Consequences: First New England recognition of Albers; Sawyer will recruit him later to Yale
Albers publie son texte sur l'enseigneme: Albers publishes its text on artistic education in the College Bulletin; He tells an anecdote about Rembrandt.
Un étudiant du cours de couleur à Black: A student from the colour class at Black Mountain poses in front of a blackboard with a chromatic wheel; photograph kept at the North Carolina State Archives. blackboard chromatic wheel
Tous les jours structurés par les corvée: Every day organized by the chores except Saturday, dedicated to the Japanese school where children discover calligraphy. At eight years old, Asawa describes the brush gesture as a dance. "It was like a dance. Lift your feet up and lift your hands."
Le sceau circulaire à motifs concentriqu: The circular seal with concentric motifs symbolizes, according to Albers, “coming together, standing together, working together” (assemble, hold together, work together). It closely resembles Gropius Bauhaus's curriculum diagram, but without a prescriptive program. round medallion, concentric drawing Consequences: Emblem of the mutual relationship between individual and community
Les Albers traversent la Floride avec le: The Albers cross Florida with their new friends Theodore and Barbara Dreier (among the founders of Black Mountain and roommates of Albers), en route to a conference in Havana; Anni had the idea of a trip to Mexico the following year. Consequences: The first Mexican voyage project
La veille de partir à la convention nati: La makes sure to go to the national convention of factors in Cleveland, for which he had long been preparing, the father asks to borrow his son's suitcase, “plus grande et plus neuve que la sienne”; Olson, about 24, refuses without reason. Consequences: The father goes mad; shortly after he was hospitalized and died in August 1935 (heart); To the end he refused to speak to his son or to recognize his presence during his visits.
Albers publie à Asheville en 1934 des bo: Albers published in Asheville in 1934 engraved wood and linogravures, probably prepared by drawings that did not seem to have survived.
À la deuxième année du collège, Rice dev: In the second year of the college, Rice became rector and Georgia was secretary.
Albers se désespère du manque de formali: Albers despaired of the lack of formalism of faculty meetings and the Council of Fellows: he wanted a strict agenda known in advance; Rice allowed the faculty to enter, sit down and talk about what was coming. Albers judged Rice “totalement indiscipliné”. Consequences: lasting style tension between the two men
Un fermier employé aide à produire envir: An employed farmer helps produce about half of the vegetables consumed in the refectory. Pigeon breeding trials, apple harvest, coal transport from Black Mountain station by the college pick-up, campus shop attempt. 50% of vegetables; coal discharged by hand
Il lance ses premières compositions abst: He launches his first abstract compositions; He will then destroy most of them by covering them, saving only those in accordance with his strict requirement of the new masterpiece. destruction by painting above
De Kooning se lance dans ses premières c: De Kooning starts its first abstract compositions and then destroys most of them by covering them with paint; Only those who meet his demand for a new masterpiece escape his ruthless self-criticism. Consequences: Reputation of an artist unable to finish his paintings.
Become a member of the Artists' Union.
À la demande de l'architecte Philip John: At the request of architect Philip Johnson, Josef Albers designs the cover of the MoMA's Machine Art exhibition catalogue, with a dramatic photo of an industrial ball bearing. The printer's first tests do not respect his margins; Albers rejects them and requires that its designer name be removed if the defect is not corrected. required margin between the edge of the paper and the image: exactly three millimetres; image: shiny industrial ball bearing Consequences: Johnson responds contrite and promises to reduce the margin to three millimetres according to the original drawing
Aidé de Maxwell Fry, les Gropius s'insta: With Maxwell Fry's help, the Gropius moved to England. Many believe that he was fleeing as much to drive Ise away from Herbert Bayer as to flee the Nazis — as he did when he left the Bauhaus six years earlier.
La rougeole contractée en 1934 entraîne: La measles contracted in 1934 causes scleroderma, a disease of mucous membranes that slowly kills it without preventing an extraordinary late work where war and death replace birth and the splendors of nature. Consequences: Death in July 1940, less than a year after its 60th birthday
Mies est « provoqué » (mot de Johnson) p: Mies is “provoqué” (word of Johnson) by the reproduction of his furniture without credit; Johnson blamed House & Garden magazine, which did not use the information provided, and refused to take credit, citing furniture also made for his friend Edward M. Warburg. Magazine House & Garden ; development of Johnson that it includes a Brno chair in an exhibition of the Modern “proudly attributed” in Mies Consequences: Initiation of the late antipathy of Johnson towards Mies.
Quatre ans après son arrivée aux États-U: Four years after his arrival in the United States, Hofmann opened a school in New York that attracted students from all over the country; he spends two exhausting days a week (morning, afternoon and evening classes) between classes and critics.
Quatre ans après son départ d'Allemagne,: Four years after leaving Germany, Hofmann opened a school in New York that attracted students from all over the country; He teaches two challenging days a week (morning, afternoon and evening classes). Two days a week; lessons morning, afternoon and evening; sometimes seventy people in class during demonstrations. Consequences: Hofmann becomes one of the most influential art teachers of his generation.
Entre janvier et début avril 1934, corre: Between January and early April 1934, correspondence was provided between Mrs. Joseph Swan (former Bennington trustee and Johnson relationship), Johnson, Albers and President Robert Leigh, for an appointment of Albers to Bennington for 1934-35. Albers BMC contract expiring June 12, 1934; uncertainty about BMC's solvency; desire to be closer to New York Consequences: Bennington's final refusal; Albers remains at Black Mountain until 1949
John communique sa forte affection à Pau: John communicates its strong affection to Paul; discomfort, shock; Ann and Paul close on themselves; Paul becomes remote; John avoids Paul but remains polished; Ann spades John sarcasm; all in front of the eyes of the whole college Words: Ann mocks John's self-dramatization Atmosphere: claustrophobe — “notre petit univers, impossible de s'éviter l'un l'autre”; salt on a wound Issue: love forbidden in a glass village
Rice aborde le travail de John, le fait: Rice addresses the work of John, makes it speak, sees it clear in the situation, and then exposes to it the gravity of the underlyings and criticisms of the group Words: Rice insists on the “gravité des sous-entendus” Atmosphere: briefly liberating and then destroying Issue: the founder, ally and censor
Les étudiants ont ramassé 1000 dollars ;: Students picked up $1000; Inconclusive meeting; Rice adjourns due to lack of consensus; Distraught students come to see him; he sends them back to the opponents to persuade. Words: Rice: “there's no consensus here”; “If I was running the show—but I'm not running this show, because it's yours”. Atmosphere: FCC underpaid against the thousand dollars. Issue: Who governs: the community or its leaders.
Conversation alternant allemand et angla: German and English alternating conversation: Wilder's ecolage in China, Mary Pickford's play project with him, Goethe's color theory, Wilder's trick to hold phone numbers by their melody, Kandinsky's art, Gene Tunney. Then Wilder buys a $10 Albers engraving, Albers offers a second. Words: Albers on Wilder: “Ein fabelhafter Kerl! So lebendig—so kraftvoll und tuend—er ist ein richtiger moderner Mensch!!” Atmosphere: Warm, brilliant, bilingual Issue: La meets the New York literary world and refugees from the Bauhaus
Wilder prononce une conférence sur les «: Wilder delivers a lecture on “rapports de la littérature et de la vie” in front of the whole college and 250 guests; It flatters local pride (experimental colleges) and national pride (America holds the new subject: the multitude), without guaranteeing a Renaissance; After which an “matrone d'Asheville au joli minou effronté” invites him to spend the Saturday at his home in Biltmore Forest. Words: America has “les mains sur un nouveau sujet — la multitude — mais on ne peut être sûr qu'elle tourne le coin vers une grande Renaissance” Atmosphere: General public, worldly
Avant de partir, Wilder confie à Rice so: Before leaving, Wilder gave Rice his enthusiasm for the emotional climate (“une atmosphère mystérieusement heureuse”) but expressed reservations: too few people and people's types, and “un peu plus de discipline intellectuelle” would not harm. Rice offers one semester of teaching per year; Wilder diplomatically replied that he would try to come back in the spring and left $25 for the library. Words: “Une atmosphère mystérieusement heureuse”; “un peu plus de discipline intellectuelle” Atmosphere: Frank, courteous Issue: La first lucid external evaluation of the project
Les épreuves arrivent du printer ; la ma: The tests come from the printer; the margin around the ball bearing is too wide; Albers refuses, requires that its name be removed if the defect is not corrected; Johnson responds with a contrite letter promising three exact millimeters. Words: Albers requires correction if not removal of its name; Johnson apologizes and confirms the three-millimetre margin. Atmosphere: perfectionist tension, wounded dignity Issue: Bauhaus rigor transplanted into America, up to millimetre
Leigh encourage Albers à continuer à BMC: Leigh encourages Albers to continue at BMC, arguing that someone needs different technical training; Albers, believing in a misunderstanding due to his English, responds in German “par souci de directness and simplicity”, offers a visit to Bennington from 8 to 15 April, details his studies in the great German art schools before 1920 and recalls that he also practises oil painting. Leigh definitely refuses: the department already has an “d'arrière-plan allemand” member, and you need someone from “plus essentiellement américain” who knows “the background of our girls”. Letter in German; proposed visit 8-15 April; Leigh quote on the “expérience américaine” Consequences: Albers remains at Black Mountain; possible devastation of Albers; hypothesis of a Eurocentrism of Albers towards women noted by Mrs. Leigh
Albers écrit à Kandinsky que le flux con: Albers writes to Kandinsky that the constant flow of visitors almost always attends his courses and above all praises his English, yet perfectible.
Avant fin juillet 1934, Albers se présen: Before the end of July 1934, Albers showed up at the MoMA with its recently engraved wood, hoping to help expose them, perhaps to the museum itself. Engraved wood wallet brought in person Consequences: Warburg immediately wrote to Agnes Mongan (Fogg, Harvard) and Charles Sawyer (Addison Gallery); only the Addison accepts
Albers, un an après son arrivée, se prés: Albers, one year after its arrival, presents itself with its engraved wooden wallet, hoping for an exhibition at the museum; Warburg immediately wrote to Mongan and Sawyer, pressing the step. Words: Warburg: “plusieurs musées ont déjà demandé cette exposition”, respond as soon as possible Atmosphere: Zeal of the emigrant, rapid generosity of the patron Issue: Make the artist exist (not just the professor) in America
Le courrier met environ deux semaines pa: The mail takes about two weeks by boat. Mies responded to Johnson's letter of November 2 in a dry reply: he refused to accept an exhibition of “élèves” that he had not trained and demanded the strictest standards. Johnson, upset, replies that he leaves the Modern and threatens that there will be no more architectural exhibitions in America — false prediction. Letter from Johnson dated 2 November; Mies' reply dated 23 November; Two weeks of postal transit Consequences: Temporary withdrawal; post-war Johnson becomes one of Mies' greatest supporters.
Éditorial de tête de Walter Locke (ami d: Walter Locke's leading editorial (friend of Rice) in Dayton Daily News, Ohio, November 16, 1934; article by Grace Alexandra Young, “Art as a Fourth R”, in Arts and Decorations, January 1935.
Première entrée des Albers en Amérique l: The Albers first entered Latin America, Cuba in winter 1934, shortly after their arrival in the United States in late 1933. Consequences: Opening of a series of more than fourteen trips
Les Albers et leurs amis Ted et Bobbie D: The Albers and their friends Ted and Bobbie Dreier travel by car and ferry from Miami to Havana; Josef gave three lectures at the Lyceum Club. They fell under the charm of the Latin world. Palmeras, tropical fruits and flowers, Spanish New Year wine, very strong coffee, black tobacco, rum; Letter from Josef to Kandinsky of 4 February 1935 Consequences: Beginning of the lasting link of Albers with Latin America
Invités par Clara Porset, Anni et Josef: Invited by Clara Porset, Anni and Josef leave with their friends Ted and Bobbie Dreier by car and ferry from Miami to Havana; Josef gives three lectures at the Lyceum Club. heat and sun of Cuba, palm trees, abundant tropical fruits and flowers, Spanish wine on New Year's Eve, very strong coffee, black cigarettes, rum Consequences: First taste of the Latin world, beginning of two decades of Latin American travel
Arrivée en voiture et ferry depuis Miami: Arrival by car and ferry from Miami with the Dreier; reception of Porset; Josef gives three lectures; dazzling discovery of Cuba, from New Year's Eve to Spanish wine Words: Josef to Kandinsky: all “différent de l'Amérique du Nord... excellent tout” Atmosphere: Heat, sun, palm trees, rum and strong coffee Issue: First contact with the Latin world, lightning
Invité par la designer cubaine Clara Por: Invited by Cuban designer Clara Porset, who had visited Black Mountain in September, Josef gave a three-day lecture cycle at the Havana Lyceum (founded in 1928 as a women's social club, later merged with the Lawn Tennis Club). The Albers travel with Ted and Bobbie Dreier in the Dreier car. Dreier car; Lyceum founded in 1928 Consequences: Start of the Latin American Travel Series
Peu avant la visite de sa mère venue des: Shortly before his mother's visit from the Netherlands, Kooning rents a temporary space where he and Diaz pass as husband and wife; his mother pierces the deception, learns Diaz's abortion and discovers the existence of Juliet Browner Consequences: Reveals the dominant personality of the mother, who threatened to commit suicide if her son upset her
Anni rapportera en 1970 que la collectio: Anni will report in 1970 that the collection began by chance in 1935; They will call the “ídolos” figures, a quasi-religious term also used by Rivera. Hundreds of figures and objects, later bequeathed to the Peabody Museum of Yale; Never exhibited at home, kept in cabinets and boxes Consequences : Collection bequeathed to the Peabody Museum
Josef Albers photographie le site de Mon: Josef Albers photographes the Monte Albán site, including the pelote playground; montages of 40 and 39 contacts kept at the Foundation. mounting 'Alban mount '35' 40 contacts on cardboard, 20.6 x 50.8 cm
La collection de figures et objets préhi: La collection of prehispanic figures and objects, that Josef and Anni invest of quasi religious significance by calling them idolos, began without ceremony in 1935. A selection of the smallest pieces will be published in 1970 with an introduction by Anni; The ensemble will eventually go to the Peabody Museum of Yale. hundreds of pieces; rows in closets and drawers, never exposed; 1970 publication Consequences: Talismans deprived of true creativity, never shown in the house.
Adamic visite le collège pendant trois m: Adamic visited the college for three months in 1935, impressed by the educational and community character, especially as expressed in the ideas of the founder John Andrew Rice; he holds the conversations returned in his chapter “The Long Road”. Consequences: Publication of “The Long Road” in My America (Harper, 1938), 615-45; article “Education on a Mountain”, Harper's, April 1936
Rice expose à Adamic sa philosophie éduc: Rice exposes Adamic's educational philosophy: method against content, process against results, formation of imagination, art as the beginning of education. Consequences: These “restèrent viables et affectives pendant toute la vie du collège” ideas according to the editor
Sly arrive en 1935 : environ 53 étudiant: Sly arrived in 1935: about 53 students, teaching staff grown with 18-20 members; enough musicians (students, teachers and wives) for overall music. 53 students; 18-20 teachers Consequences: Extension of musical activities: ensemble, madrigaux, limited tours (state teachers' college nearby)
Sly arrive au collège : environ 53 étudi: Sly arrives at the college: about 53 students, teaching staff increased to 18-20 people 53 students, 18-20 teachers Consequences: booming musical activities, overall music possible
Inauguration du cottage musical (quelque: Inauguration of the musical cottage (a few upright pianos, a few fireplaces) celebrated with hot dogs and Coca, or autumn cider; Albers came; Each of them had his own sausage on a loose hanger, but Albers folded his own in S and put his sausage above the fire; He was made to notice the advantage of the sting, he replied to love the shape very much in S; his sausage fell into hot-dog fire, Coke or cider, bent in S, fireplaces, upright pianos
Norman et Nan se marient en 1935 alors q: Norman and Nan married in 1935 while in college. Consequences: four children; more than 20 charities councils served to both
Le psychanalyste Fritz Moellenhoff, qui: The psychoanalyst Fritz Moellenhoff, who has known Albers since 1920 in Germany, comes with his wife Anna (also a doctor) to Black Mountain in 1935, at the suggestion of Albers.
Le psychanalyste allemand Fritz Moellenh: The German psychoanalyst Fritz Moellenhoff and his wife doctor Anna arrive under the auspices of Albers and remain for several years. Implications: Clinical Perspective on the Student Population
Productions publiques : Gloria Mundi, Th: Public productions : Gloria Mundi, The Twelve-Pound Look, The Wild Duck, Fixin's by Paul Green. Class productions without outdoor audience: The Bear, Death Says It Isn't So by Heywood Broun, an original play I Died Eight Years Ago, two plays in one act by Lord Dunsany, the prologue by Androcles and the Lion, passages by Saint Joan and Macbeth.
Pendant ses vacances, Wunsch décide que: During his vacation, Wunsch decides that the reality of Black Mountain lies in human relations; his energy will go to help people find themselves: “Je commençais à voir le drame comme une thérapie.” Consequences: Psychodramatic view useful to some students; despised by Albers as an excuse for mediocrity under cover of “auto-expression”.
Vers le milieu des années trente, la vil: By the mid thirties, the city voted for prohibition; Roy, owner of a small beer bar near the train station, learns that student Stephen Forbes comes from a wealthy New England family and offers to build a café just outside the city. Forbes agrees to finance anonymously, but students end up discovering the investment and even its amount — without Forbes understanding how. A small beer bar named Roy's, close to the station; Forbes thought he was funding anonymously Consequences: Birth of the Roy's, favorite conversation den at the college
La troisième année, le président de Benn: La third year, the president of Bennington College and his wife spend two days in college; Rice, who blames them for the “snob” attitude of Bennington's media at the start of Black Mountain, remains “frigide” towards this couple he judges “complaisant”. Two-day stay, third year of the college Consequences: Visit without success
Fred Mangold, ami personnel d'Adams, le: Fred Mangold, Adams's personal friend, persuaded him to visit Black Mountain in 1935, with the possible idea of joining the faculty to strengthen science. After a week, Adams concludes that the college really applies the principle that learning starts only when the student wants to learn, but that the existing scientific courses (Georgia in chemistry, Dreier in physics, Anna Moellenhoff in biology) are little followed because the students do not see the need; No staff member takes a science course while many follow drawing, music, literature, history and languages. He advises not to expand the sciences. one week stay Consequences: no scientific expansion recommended
Mangold répond que la science est néglig: Mangold replied that science was neglected for lack of good teachers, except Ms. Moellenhoff, who had eight “simplement fous” students of the subject since the opening of her biology course. Adams replies that biology, the science of the living body, naturally seduces more than other sciences, and that if Black Mountain wants to teach only what students want to learn, it must not introduce subjects simply because society has certified them important. eight “goofy” biology students
Deux ans après l'épisode de l'étudiant n: Two years after the black student's episode, heating broke down in the cottage where the black staff lived. Anna Moellenhoff insisted that they be given two large rooms in Lee Hall, many with bad colds. The blacks refused: Rubye Lipsey explained that it would provoke too much hostility in the village. two large rooms offered in Lee Hall
Albers conçoit un logo balayant l'hérald: Albers designs a logo sweeping the traditional heraldic, symbol of clarity, sobriety and modernity: a simple ring, with the full address of the college, without monogram or motto. a simple ring, complete printed address Consequences: flyer of 1935 broadcasting the logo
Première visite au Mexique, suivie de qu: First visit to Mexico, followed by fourteen trips to Latin and South America fourteen trips in total Consequences: Birth of documentary photographs of ancient architecture and native weaves
Après la période de gravure à Berlin pui: After the period of engraving in Berlin and then in North Caroline, Albers began painting in 1935. Consequences: Open the way to the painted series of the 1930s-40s
Après sa première visite, Dewey écrit à: After his first visit, Dewey writes to Rice that the work of the college is imperative for democracy and that there is “aux racines mêmes” (grass roots) of a democratic life. Dewey will visit the college several times, join the advisory board and give hundreds of books to the library. Consequences: Legitimation of the college by the major figure of progressive education.
Wunsch rejoint le collège comme instruct: Wunsch joins college as an English and Dramatic Instructor, after being a colleague of Rice at Rollins College in Florida. title: instructor in English and Dramatics Consequences: Transformation of Rice's informal seminar into structured creative writing
Albers publie dans Progressive Education: Albers publishes in Progressive Education (Vol. 12, p. 391) an article in English, written in his early years at Black Mountain, stating that the rules are born from experience and come after.
Début de voyages fréquents au Mexique où: Start frequent trips to Mexico where the two artists discover the ancient arts of South America, which deeply mark their works. Consequences: Pre-Columbian influences in both corpus.
Peu après l'achat, Anni montre sa pièce: Shortly after the purchase, Anni shows his piece to the renowned archaeologist George C. Vaillant, who confirms that it is an authentic Mexican treasure; So the couple is passionate about Mexican culture. Consequences: Thirteen other trips to Mexico
Dans les années 1930, l'historien d'art: In the 1930s, art historian Meyer Schapiro blamed Fuller's shelters for their naivety: believing that better housing controlled by capitalist societies would transform the structure of capitalism is a decoy, for these firmms are involved in overproduction, competition, speculative layoffs. Consequences: Sustainable Review of the “révolution par le design”
Conférence d'Albers sur l'art abstrait à: Albers Lecture on Abstract Art at Asheville.
Au milieu des années 1930, peu après son: In the mid-1930s, shortly after his arrival in America, Albers designed a synthetic fibre upholstery fabric for Rena Rosenthal's shop, then a cellulosic cotton screen fabric cut and radiates, in unusual pastels, allowing to see outside without being seen. Cellulosic cotton cut, rayon, horizontal stripes of pastels
Allan Sly et Dante Fiorillo rejoignent l: Allan Sly and Dante Fiorillo join the music faculty; Fiorillo is named composer in residence, supported by a Guggenheim scholarship.
Venue de Bennington en 1935, visant une: Coming from Bennington in 1935, aiming for a dominant art: half of his courses in drawing, colour and art studies, the other in German, French literature, music, world economy and Plato with Rice. In the higher division, it reduces from six to five courses per semester for its final draft and review reviews. six and then five courses per semester
Séjour de près de deux mois suggéré par: Nearly two months' stay suggested by Henry Allen Moe. Adamic is delighted by the place and people, especially by Rice; both link immediate friendship and Rice develops his ideas and experiences for the article Adamic decides to write for Harper's. Duration: almost two months Consequences: Article “Education on a Mountain”
De Kooning est accepté dans le Federal A: De Kooning is accepted in the Federal Art Project launched by Roosevelt to provide orders to artists hit by the Depression. The program will produce more than 2,500 frescoes, 18,000 sculptures and hundreds of thousands of prints, paintings and photographs across America. 2,500 frescoes; 18,000 sculptures; salary judged “plutôt correct” allowing to live modestly but well during the Depression Consequences: First time that Kooning can devote itself entirely to its art; the decisive experience.
Lancement du Federal Art Project du WPA: Launch of the WPA Federal Art Project in 1935 to alleviate poverty; Burckhardt remembers that “Bill” was registered there a year or more — the “$23.50 Club”, the name of the weekly allowance. $23.50 per week
Rudy Burckhardt et Edwin Denby (poète et: Rudy Burckhardt and Edwin Denby (dance critic and poet) are the level neighbours of Kooning West Street 21st and become his first convinced collectors.
Photographie d'Anni Albers dans la voitu: Photograph of Anni Albers in the Dreier car, taken by Josef Albers (illustration legend).
Au milieu des années 1930, Josef Albers: In the mid-1930s, Josef Albers was part of a group of artists protesting against the lack of attention to purely abstract artists; He thinks Barr never forgave him. Consequences: Alfred Barr's lasting resentment towards Josef Albers
Premier revenu stable via le Federal Art: First stable income via the Federal Art Project; astonishes colleagues by their share of their salary devoted to materials and art books. Whole tubes pressed on the pallet for one hour of work; reworked paintings of years, shaved at the end of the day
Exposition des gravures d'Albers pendant: Exhibition of Albers engravings during January 1935; Sawyer had probably seen the prints in the Warburg office in early September 1934. First Addison exhibition dedicated to a single European modernist artist. Fifteen works shown according to the checklist, on a larger ensemble; Boston and local newspapers have published shorts but no reviews Consequences: Sawyer will continue to support Albers exhibition opportunities the following years
Inauguration du cottage musical autour d: Inauguration of the musical cottage around the fire; each bites its sausage on a unfolded hanger; Albers folds his S and deposits his S; the advantage of the tip is explained; he refuses; The sausage falls into the fire Words: “I like very much the S-form” — I like the shape in S Atmosphere: heat of fire, smell of sausages, Coke or autumn cider Issue: the stubborn genius of Albers up to a makeshift grill
Adamic, en quête de pastoralisme pour fu: Adamic, seeking pastoralism to escape New York, receives guest room and invitation to dinner; the table brings together faculty and students who use each other; the conversation continues very late in the night; two and a half months left instead of a few days Words: Table conversation without content reported, but that lasted past midnight Atmosphere: Community warmth, intellectual effervescence night Issue: The visitor is in a hurry for a long time: birth of the narrative that will launch the myth
Première visite du philosophe ; il obser: First visit of the philosopher; he observes the community and then writes a letter of support to Rice. Words: “existe aux racines mêmes d'une vie démocratique” College; His work is imperative whatever happens from the present crisis. Issue: La bail of the greatest American teacher.
Pendant que Josef et les Dreier visitent: While Josef and Dreier visit the interior of a church, Anni waits in the car; a little boy approaches with a kid under his arm and proposes to sell the beast or a small figurine head wrapped in a handkerchief; Anni buys the head for a few pesos. Words: The boy proposes the kid or the figurine; Anni will say later: she would not have imagined that such a piece would still be available Atmosphere: Heat of the Mexican road, chance, enchantment Issue: Fortuitous birth of a collection that will unite the couple for fifty years
Trois mois après son arrivée, épuisé et: Three months after his arrival, exhausted and doubting, Wunsch requests a private interview; Rice takes him to his room, listens to him, suggests that he is tired and judges only by tangible results, and proposes a vacation. Rice suggests a trip to Kentucky Derby. Consequences: Wunsch goes on vacation and redefines its role.
Wunsch attend peut-être le marteau-pilon: Wunsch may be waiting for the drummer; Rice takes him to his room, listens to him, finds him tired, suggests a vacation — a trip to Kentucky Derby for example. Words: Rice judges that Wunsch only evaluates its work by its tangible results. Atmosphere: Warm, quiet, with the fantasy of Rice. Issue: Wunsch expected to be crushed; He's being treated.
Mangold, chargé des sessions d'été, se p: Mangold, in charge of the summer sessions, complains of the “nincompoops” (letter to Rice of 9 July 1935), predicts the death of the college (19 June 1935), speaks of castration (to Bailey, 28 August 1935), then Mexico on 26 June 1936 warns his successor: pray that no Adventist profane the woods “d'orgies végétariennes”; last year's harvest was “abomination, à part quelques barbares lubriques qui donnaient une note pittoresque — la nouveauté résidait dans les barbes”.
Article développant un espace-temps plié: Article developing a space-time folded in parallel layers connected by a bridge, using only the general relativity and Maxwell equations — first description of a worm hole. Physical Review 48 (1), p. 73 Consequences: Concept taken from Wheeler and Fuller (1962, instability), Hjellming (1971), Thorne and Morris (1988).
Rejoint le Federal Art Project ; murale: Joins the Federal Art Project; mural for the Williamburg Federal Housing Project never completed; leaves WPA after one year for lack of American citizenship
Knickerbocker, la trentaine avancée, arr: Knickerbocker, the advanced thirty, arrives highly recommended by his Harvard teachers, where he completes a PhD in psychology specialized in child problems; he and his wife run a small school for disturbed children. Two of the three recommended professors highlight his “unusual independence”. Consequences: He expresses his doubts about the class tactics of Rice, which he believes produce fear and break people without rebuilding them.
Katherine Dreier (qui avait visité le Ba: Katherine Dreier (who had visited the Bauhaus Berlin in 1933 and knew Albers through his nephew Theodore and his wife Bobbie) brings an exhibition of his collection to BMC. Works by Archipenko, Burliuk, Campendonk, Gleizes, Kandinsky, Klee, Léger, Miró, Mondrian, Schwitters; students chose 30-40 paintings in the reserve to hang them in their rooms Consequences: Unique experience: living with works, seeing them under all lights
Dreier ouvre sa réserve aux résidents ;: Dreier opens its reserve to residents; Each one chooses works from thirty or forty, hangs them in his room, lives them daily. Words: Bobbie Dreier: one could watch them “sous toutes les lumières”, not just pass before as in an exhibition; “J'ai choisi moi-même” Atmosphere: Rare intimacy with modern masterpieces at the bottom of the North Caroline Mountains Issue: European Modernism Enters American Domestic Life
En visitant sites et musées, les Albers: By visiting sites and museums, Albers examine fragments of ceramic — delicately shaped heads, often broken figures — found by the peasants while ploughing; they start to buy and collect, up to more than a thousand Atmosphere objects: Unbelievable wonder: centuries old pieces in their hands Issue: Birth of a collection and a source of permanent inspiration
Après deux mois elle sent que « quelque: After two months she feels that “quelque chose manquait”: boys; She hates being blown from one subject to another. Consequences: An incidental meeting with a former comrade who suggests Leonardo da Vinci Art School.
Admise sur dessins de sculptures, elle y: Admitted to sculptures, she studied with Conrad Marca-Relli and joined the young Milton Resnick. School founded in 1923 by sculptor Onorio Ruotolo to offer free education to the poor; completely free upon arrival of Elaine, unpaid teachers. Courses in fresco, mural painting, easel, drawing, cartoon; bare models — “this is living!”. Consequences: Beginning of his true vocation.
Opposante active au régime de droite du: An active opponent of President Mendieta's right-wing regime supported by the United States, Porset exiled to Mexico and married artist Xavier Guerrero, close to Diego Rivera's early murals. Consequences: Guerrero becomes the major link between Albers and Mexican artists
Début de la série de voyages au Mexique,: Start of the series of trips to Mexico, fourteen in total, some three months. 14 trips in total; some of a duration of three months Consequences: Beginning of the collection of pre-Columbian art and a lasting influence on the work of the Albers
De retour aux États-Unis, Albers commenc: De back in the United States, Albers starts painting instead of continuing the colorful glass paintings of its Bauhaus years; Mexican themes appear immediately in his painting after the first trip. Consequences: Birth of patterns like Tenayuca and, later, the “Homenaje al cuadrado” series.
Opposante active au gouvernement de droi: An active opponent of President Mendieta's pro-American right-wing government, Porset moved to Mexico and married artist Xavier Guerrero, who had collaborated in Diego Rivera's first murals; a couple at the centre of a circle of artists engaged in post-revolutionary fervour. Consequences: Guerrero becomes an essential link between Albers and Mexican artists, architects and intellectuals; Porset may have played a role in organizing the August 1936 exhibition.
Trois mois au Mexique ; Josef écrit que: Three months in Mexico; Josef writes that Mexico is the promised land of abstract art, thousands of years old, and measures its progress to its well-being and production. 7 pounds taken (about 3 kg), 11 oil paintings; "we hope to return soon and often" Consequences: Recurring theme in its correspondence: Mexico feeds its creativity.
Après leur premier été mexicain, Anni ré: After their first Mexican summer, Anni creates two large-format wall tapestries, more spontaneous and personal than his Bauhaus works; for the first time she gives titles to her work and signs Monte Alban initials embroidered at the bottom left — breaking with the creative anonymity of the Bauhaus. Monte Alban: limited palette of black, grey and creamy white; white weft yarn floating on the surface, lined and shaded by black wefts evoking unexcavated mounds Consequences: Exceeding the ordered geometries of the Bauhaus tapestries of the late 1920s.
Dès 1936 au plus tard, les Albers recuei: By 1936, Albers collected fragments of pre-Columbian pottery and figurines; Little boys offered them some from the car window, as they also sold turkeys and goats by the roadside. fragments of pottery, finely shaped heads, figurines usually broken, found by the peasants by plowing their fields; Turkeys and goats for sale Consequences: beginning of a sustainable collection and passion
Après son premier séjour mexicain, Josef: After his first Mexican visit, Josef Albers painted Archaeologic I, Archaeologic II and Temple, now lost and known only by black and white photographs. Paintings of small size, very bright colors according to Irving Finkelstein who saw them in 1965; concentric compositions evoking archaeological sites Consequences: Possible Genesis of Homage to the Square in geometrical plans of prehispanic degrees temples
L'auteur et le couple Adamic allaient ch: The author and the Adamic couple went to the nearest booth every evening at about 11 p.m. to pick up the morning paper, almost daily vehement discussions. One night, during the abdication crisis of Edward VIII, Louis, stuttering refusing to stutter, grinned teeth against the king (“the damned fool”); the author says envy a man able to love so much, Stella approved, Louis replied with a biting courtesy. departure at about 11 p.m. for the morning newspaper; Louis Adamic begs for words
L'article d'Adamic (d'abord dans Harper': Adamic's article (first in Harper's) raises requests; additional applications also come thanks to a favorable chronicle by Gaynor Maddox affecting two million readers. After a heated discussion, it was decided not to include any separate items in the catalogue: too much self-satisfaction, contrary to the college's policy of advertising discretion. Consequences: Increased applications
Elaine partage un studio avec son petit: Elaine shares a studio with her boyfriend Milton Resnick and Ernestine Blumberg (who can sign leases because she has a job); they organize their work spaces, share meals and social life. Consequences: bohemian environment: joyfully despised poverty, hard work and conversations
Robert Jonas, instructeur à la Leonardo: Robert Jonas, an instructor at Leonardo da Vinci, takes him to an exhibition of the American Abstract Artists and tells him that the two best American artists — by Kooning and Arshile Gorky — are not there; In two weeks, Elaine has met with Kooning and knows she will marry him. She's under twenty, he's thirty-four; She's still Milton Resnick's girlfriend. “it took me about two weeks”; Age gap: she ~20, him 34 Consequences: beginning of the relationship that will define her entire life as an artist
Un compagnon des cafétérias rapporte que: A cafeteria companion reports that Bill, who was in love with Elaine, said he wanted to be a single game for the first time — “just Elaine”.
Une peinture de Bill figure dans l'expos: A painting by Bill appears in the New Horizons in America exhibition at MoMA, alongside Bolotowsky, Browne, Davis, Gorky, Greene, Matulka, McNeil; Elaine proudly boasts of his friends as proof that Bill is a great “New Horizons in America” exhibition talent; exhibited artists: Ilya Bolotowsky, Byron Browne, Stuart Davis, Arshile Gorky, Balcomb Greene, Jan Matulka, George McNeil Consequences: official affirmation of Elaine's conviction that Bill is a major artist
Après quelques années, Anni établit un a: After a few years, Anni set up a weaving workshop and started working and teaching alongside Josef. She directed the weaving program throughout her time (1933-1948) and performed some of her most ambitious works there. Consequences: Weaving becomes a major discipline of the college.
À partir de 1936, Schawinsky conçoit son: Starting in 1936, Schawinsky conceived his Stage Studies course as a laboratory where students built an understanding of the fundamentals of stage creation, applying the experimental logic of Albers he admired. The course is included in the art catalogue, separate from Robert Wunsch's Dramatics curriculum. Consequences: Leads to public performance Spectodrama
Performance publique en quatre parties c: Public performance in four parts running the course Stage Studies, encompassing optical, form and colour, acoustic, sound, language, music, time, space, architecture, technology and illusion. The neologism Spectodrama combines Latin specto (I observe) and drama (Jeu), merging spectator and performer, the scene treated as a total work of art. Part 1 scene 7: two figurines of moving planes of contrasting colors manipulated to show the variation of chromatic intensity during covers; lighting enhancing effects
Le travail physique quotidien (13h-16h): Daily physical work (13h-16h) officially becomes the work program: heating/plumb maintenance supervised by Bascomb Allen, roads led by Josef Albers, cooking guided by cooks Jack and Rubye Lipsey. work from 1 to 4 p.m.; dig furrows, harvest corn, repair showers, maintain roads Consequences: The college survives the meagre years of Depression thanks to this program, which flattens the hierarchies between teachers and students.
Plusieurs femmes arrivent comme compagne: Several women arrive as companions of their partners or with subordinate positions: Irene Schawinsky costume designer (1936-1938), making costumes of her husband Xanti's pieces; Johanna Jalowetz teaches singing and binding after the death of her husband Heinrich, campus musicologist. Frankenthaler, Elaine of Kooning, Knight Lawrence, Newhall and Fiore do not receive any appointments. Consequences: Some later gain independent teachings; others contribute as students or volunteer teachers.
Le séminaire d'écriture de Rice prend le: Rice's writing seminar took the name of “creative writing” in 1936, marking the transition from a progressive education tool to a teaching art alongside music, theatre and fine arts. Consequences: Introduction of techniques and exercises from the Wunsch manual, Studies in Creative Writing (1933)
Wunsch introduit l'écriture créative au: Wunsch introduces creative writing to the college by insisting on the “discipline” of writing, granting that ultimately only the technique can teach itself. Consequences: Creative writing becomes a central element of artistic education at Black Mountain.
Sa sœur Janet naît ; à seize ans elle se: His sister Janet was born; At sixteen she will be elected “reine de la patate douce” of Louisiana. Louisiana “Yam-Königin”
Anni utilise un fil blanc « flottant » p: Anni uses a white thread “flottant” to create a pattern evoking the mysterious authority of ancient inscriptions — textile as text. floating white wire
Dans l'esprit de son idole Herman Melvil: In the spirit of his idol Herman Melville, Olson embarked three weeks on a fishing schooner during the summer of 1936. three weeks at sea
Des fabricants de briques exhument des q: Manufacturers of bricks exhume quantities of vases and figurines of surprising variety and finesse, in a style distinct from all that was known; Once their value is known, systematic looting begins. Consequences: Massive pick-up of the site; Tlatilco collectionism (including future Albers collection)
Perry, 65 ans, ancien coureur de fond (c: Perry, 65 years old, former cross-country runner, explains his reading of the Ecclesiastes: putting his trust in works — pleasures, great achievements, wisdom — is idolatry and vanity; one must act according to his strength (“à toute chose une saison”) without putting his trust in it; Trust goes to God. The reporter approves by quoting “la course n'est pas aux agiles”. Perry then doubts: is any career worth another? The reporter replied that everything seemed solid from afar and collapsed as soon as he was taken into his hands. Perry is 65; quotations from the Ecclesiastes, ch. IX; man about to melt in tears Consequences: Mrs. Westover suggests that her husband might have been right to stick to one thing
Sortant d'un taillis de bouleaux, Perry: Out of a birch, Perry reaches the white fence of Route 4W; A green roadster is now 80 miles an hour. He sits down to take his breath, fixes a broken spark plug on the roadway and knows that by fixing long enough he can make revel in a timeless vision all the history of the place (compressor rollers, dynamite salves, the horse of the colporteur). In front of panels (Gaskell 21⁄2 mi, Middleton 10, Malory 15, Cicero 125), he imagines time limits: 5 years, 50 years, 150,000 years. broken piglain ignition candle; old shoe hung on the panel, damaged by rain and sun; green roadster at 80 mph
Début octobre : quatre gamins font l'éco: At the beginning of October: four kids do the bushy school, lit a fire, tell dirty stories and play string (cat's-cradle). Perry emerges from a scarlet sheath, its white form appears and disappears between trunks; The children name him with fear and admiration, unable to point because of the strings between their fingers. Fire among colored trees; string passed from fingers to fingers; white form of Perry
Premier panneau : pirate sexy torse nu e: First panel: Sexy pirate naked torso taking a smiling girl in nightshirt, legend “Nature in the Raw is Seldom Mild”, Lucky Strikes, “It's Toasted!”. Second: a glasses farmer reading his wife a letter from their son “just bought a Ford V-8”, “Consult your local Ford dealer”. Third, from Christmas: mother in purple dress, blond hair marceled, light halo, baby with the baby star of the cinema Baby Kelly, two golden candles, “Sheffield Farms vous souhaite un Merry Xmas”. Fourth: “BUY REM” (cough syrup). Behind, one showed a girl in tears for not renting a phone to Bell. ads: Lucky Strikes, Ford V-8, Sheffield Farms, REM, Bell Telephone, Burma Shave (crimes cited)
Après une année comme artiste à plein te: After a year as a full-time artist at WPA, Kooning abandons the safer idea of earning a living in the applied arts (commercial illustration) and styled himself pure artist, realizing his teenage dream. One year of WPA; according to his metaphor, he puts all his eggs in the basket of art Consequences: Birth of his path as an independent artist, in doubt and the leap of faith
Se lie aux premiers collectionneurs amér: Joins the first American collectors of his work, Burckhardt and Denby; painted full time, starts the series of men standing and sitting; meets the critic Harold Rosenberg. Self Portrait with Imaginary Brother, c. 1938.
Série de dessins linéaires géométriques: Series of geometrical linear drawings signed and dated 1936 (PLATES 100-108), the first expression of linear concerns that will later underpin series of prints, vinyl engravings and architectural commands. Seven drawings of type PLATE 100, all 1936, with diagonal symmetry (same as 180 degrees), composed of nine to twelve lines, some varied by dotted or thickened; executed with feather and ruler, fine black lines not modulated; signature and date with light pencil at bottom right; one compound of eleven lines of thickness equal in three sizes; two more (PLATES 107-108) totally asymmetric, more incomplete; one (PLATE 109) made of two continuous lines of constant width. Consequences: These drawings announce the linear work of the next 40 years of Albers.
Albers et Bolotowsky sont membres fondat: Albers and Bolotowsky are founding members of the American Abstract Artists (AAA); Bolotowsky explains that the majority of the group left nature to get the essence, while some, including him, began abstract by rejecting nature.
Albers invite l'émigré suisse Schawinsky: Albers invites the Swiss emigrant Schawinsky (student of Schlemmer from 1924 to 1928) to teach painting and theatre. Fleeing Nazi Germany, Schawinsky had passed through Italy and advertising. Advertising customers: Illy Caffè, vermouth Cinzano, Olivetti typewriters; widely distributed photomontage of Mussolini leading the masses for the 12th anniversary of the fascist revolution Consequences: Schawinsky becomes the only defender and performer of the Bauhaus theatre in the United States
Anni et Josef Albers visitent le Mexique: Anni and Josef Albers visit Mexico, including the archaeological site of Monte Alban; This encounter feeds Ancient Writing (glyphs, golden son) and Monte Alban. golden son in Ancient Writing; Monte Alban degree temples Consequences: turning from the mid-1930s to symbolic imagery
L'écrivain Louis Adamic, lors d'une visi: The writer Louis Adamic, during a visit in 1936, collected from Rice a long explanation: teaching method rather than content, process rather than results; Education is not “obtient”, it is tested; the facts change but the method of dealing with them remains; philosophy, literature, art, music, drama are the best training grounds for imagination. published in “Education on a Mountain”, p. 518-19 Consequences: the most complete formulation of the Rice doctrine on art at the centre of the curriculum
Trois ans après l'ouverture, Locke — anc: Three years after the opening, Locke, a former Liberal colleague from Lincoln (Nebraska), became a fiercely independent editor of Dayton Daily News, visited the college (~50 students, 16 professors). Noting that the original welded group is diversifying, he asks Rice what it will do when an “intrigant” arrives. Rice, very confident, lift shoulders. He later decided that the intriguant — Irving Knickerbocker — was already there. Approximately 50 students, 16 professors Consequences: a perception of future conflicts
Rice convoque une réunion générale sur l: Rice convenes a general meeting on the nature of the institutions that blindly survive their goals, and then asks why not decide tonight to close the college so that it becomes unique among all institutions. Silence, hiccups, then debate; Rice ready for all arguments, with the most powerful voice; A Central American refugee, tortured in his country's prisons, rose and launched a tirade unrelated to the subject. La meeting goes away by itself; Rice sits at the end of the table, smoking his pipe, next to a tiny log cabin he built with the matches of his pipe. tiny log cabin made of burnt matches, placed at the elbow of Rice; period of depression; European refugees in assistance Consequences: demonstration of the ambivalence of Rice towards all institutional ties
Avant le départ des Adamic, Louis lit so: Before the Adamic left, Louis read his draft in a community meeting. The article salutes pioneer students, distinguishes Albers and Wunsch, but puts Rice on a pedestal: “idéaliste-optimiste : intelligent, bien informé, fantastiquement honnête”, “peut-être l'un des grands enseignants de tous les temps”. La discussion that follows is critical: several students say for the first time that Rice is a Socrates sometimes insensitive whose power can be misused. Zeuch states that Adamic, without community or educational experience, was actually “ghost-writé” by Rice. Adamic quotes on Rice; “open secret” of the ghost-writing Consequences: Rice admits awkwardness, says he is hungry for gratitude; the article attracts a wave of applications
Après l'avertissement, Rice conseille à: After the warning, Rice advises Goldenson, a passionate golfer and good coach, to give up teaching in class to become a professional golf instructor. At the faculty meeting (7 December 1936), Goldenson cited this as proof of insensitivity; Dreier finds that “c'était un très bon conseil”; Wunsch mentions that Rice also made insensitive remarks about its staging; Goldenson counters: “pas après avoir été renvoyé de la faculté”. Rice explains that his advice was calculated, to shock Goldenson out of the idea that one teaches with a mass of information. Consequences: Increased resentment of Goldenson
Goldenson, soutenu par Zeuch et d'autres: Goldenson, supported by Zeuch and others, objects that no colleague had yet attended his classes when the written warning arrived in his mailbox. “On m'a jugé sur des choses en périphérie. C'est comme juger une ville par ses banlieues.” Warning received “dans ma boîte”
Knickerbocker écoute avec sympathie les: Knickerbocker listens with sympathy to the unhappy students (especially new and young) of the college and Rice. Factions are formed, students aligning behind Rice or Knickerbocker. Wunsch, seeing the community at the edge of the split into two colleges, estimates that Knickerbocker “choie” students; Dreier tends to approve it. Knickerbocker says it is necessary to protect some students from Rice's “effet extrêmement destructeur sur la personnalité”, and claims to have given them all the information possible about Rice and its methods. Consequences: Climate of internal cold war; some expect a discreet departure of both men during the summer, but both return
De Kooning se lie avec deux voisins : l': De Kooning is linked with two neighbours: the author and dance critic Edwin Denby and photographer Rudolph Burckhardt, descendant of historian Jacob Burckhardt. They become his first collectors; the carefully composed black and white photos of Burckhardt shape the artist's public image.
De Kooning entre en contact avec l'assoc: De Kooning comes into contact with the emerging American Abstract Artists association, dominated by communist ideas; his political sense assures him a quick acceptance, but despite several requests he refuses to become an official member: he cannot accept the prohibitions of the group (in particular figuration) and remains interested in art as a whole, feeling foreign, different. Consequences: Maintaining its independence between abstraction and figuration.
Amitiés avec le photographe Rudolph Burc: Joined photographer Rudolph Burckhardt and dance poet/critic Edwin Denby, who became his first collectors; at Ibram Lassaw, participates in discussions leading to the founding of the American Abstract Artists; meets Harold Rosenberg; dedicated exclusively to painting, begins the series of male figures standing and sitting; first participation in a group exhibition, “New Horizons in American Art” at MoMA.
Cubism and Abstract Art puis Fantastic A: Cubism and Abstract Art then Fantastic Art, Dada and Surrealism succeed each other in spring and winter 1936, imposing the dual framework of abstract formal rigour and of solicitation of the unconscious where abstract expressionism will be born. Consequences: Decisive impulsion to the abstract ventures of Kooning, culminating in Elegy (v. 1939)
Le bureau Terramare, organisme officiel: The government's official public relations agency, Terramare, commissioned a brochure from Bayer distributed around the world to promote Führer's achievements. Cover: young Aryan blond, smiling, serious and proud, in Hitler Youth uniform, German flag in hand; mischievously arranged photo, typography accentuating purity and training. Consequences: One of Bayer's many brochures and posters for the Reich.
Bayer conçoit une brochure célébrant la: Bayer designs a brochure celebrating the life of the Third Reich and the impact of Hitler, accompanying an exhibition for tourists of the Berlin Olympics. It includes the Heinkel plant designed by Herbert Rimpl. Later, he will only discuss the duotone technique. Brochure with Heinkel factory, cottage worker houses Consequences: This involvement in Nazi propaganda will color the vision of many on the Bauhaus.
Kandinsky écrit à Schoenberg une longue: Kandinsky wrote to Schoenberg a long and warm letter; no response retained. Consequences: Definitive silence of Schoenberg
Après plusieurs années à Paris (retouche: After several years in Paris (retouche of photos, theatre sets, painting at night), disgusted by the too commercial aspect of the environment, he moved to the United States and could devote himself to painting, apart from a little teaching. Consequences: he discovers Demuth, Dove, Ryder, Gorky, first artists to impress him in this country
Début d'une longue relation de mécénat e: Beginning of a long relationship of patronage and friendship: Edlich buys about thirty-five works during the meagre years; he is also Kline's family doctor and will assist him during his last illness. about 35 works purchased Consequences: allows Kline to survive in the decade before its fame
Elaine obtient son diplôme en janvier (l: Elaine graduated in January (exits in the course of the year were common). Her photo of yearbook shows her duvetous hair, half-insured half-sage, to Barbara Stanwyck. Yearbook Tribute: “Elaine the fair, Elaine the lovable, Elaine the lily maid of Brooklyn”. Consequences: Joined Hunter College.
Sur la suggestion de Henry Allen Moe, se: At the suggestion of Henry Allen Moe, secretary of the Guggenheim Foundation and friend of the college, Adamic and his wife Stella, dancer, stopped at the college in January 1936 for two or three days; There's three months left. A student: “He was like a sponge, and we water” — it was a sponge and we water Consequences: A long magazine article, then a prolonged crisis in college
Une interview de Rice paraît avec un ton: An interview with Rice appears with too much tone, denigrating the other colleges; Evarts notes in her diary that many were disgusted, fearing that she might antagonize sensible and caring people. Journal d'Evarts dated January 29, 1936 Consequences: Internal malaise among college members
L'écrivain yougoslave Louis Adamic, célè: The Yugoslav writer Louis Adamic, famous for The Native's Return (1934) and as Rice a year old Guggenheim Fellow in Europe, arrives with his wife Stella in January 1936 for an afternoon visit suggested by Henry Allen Moe. They remain for almost two months; Adamic falls under the charm of the place and people, especially of Rice, who binds himself with immediate friendship with him and develops his ideas for him at length. visit scheduled for one afternoon; nearly two months of stay Consequences: article “Education on a Mountain” for Harper's
Lors des visites de sites préhistoriques: During visits to prehistoric sites, little boys tend fragments of pottery through the car window, as are turkeys and goats; Albers examine finely formed heads and broken figures, unbelieving to hold centuries-old pieces found by the peasants by plowing; archaeologist George Vaillant confirms their authenticity. Words: A woman from a remote area, spreading a small clay head: “Es natural” — she belonged to the ground she knew atmosphere: Marvelously mixed with unbelief, rural trade in the belly of the car Issue: Birth of the collection that will feed all their work
Les Albers reviennent encore et encore a: The Albers return again and again to the museum; Josef photographing entire days; they buy for a few cents “petits dieux” heads dug up by the peasants; fragments of pottery in hands, unbelief. Words : Anni : “nous ne pouvions pas croire que dans nos mains il y avait des pièces précolombiennes centenaires trouvées par les paysans en labourant” Atmosphere : Fiery fascination Issue: Birth of a collection of more than 1,000 objects
Vers 23 h, les trois vont chercher le pr: Around 11 p.m., the three will search for the first newspaper of the crisis; usual argument, more lively that night; Louis, stingy, refusing to stutter, grinça 'the damned fool' (Édouard VIII); Rice: 'I really envy'; Stella: 'Me too'; Louis, with a biting courtesy word by word, asks why; Rice: 'I envy anyone who can love so much' Words: Louis: 'the damned fool'; Rice: 'In fact, I envy Him'; Stella: 'So do I' Atmosphere: vehemence, New York night, stormy friendship Issue: fidelity to love against reasonable judgment
Sortie habituelle de nuit pour le journa: The usual night out for the morning newspaper; That night's argument, during the abdication crisis, is harsher than usual. Louis, grinning teeth, rips out words — a sting that refuses to stutter — against Edward VIII. The author responds gently that he does not think; in front of the accuser noise of Louis, he goes so far as to say that he envys the king; Stella, before the explosion, drop “moi aussi”. Louis, facing two fools, demands with a chopped politeness that we explain to him; “j'envie quiconque peut aimer autant”. Words: Louis: “the damned fool”; author: “je l'envie”; Stella : “moi aussi” ; Louis, word for word : “Peut-être pouvez-vous me dire pourquoi. Je vous en prie.” Atmosphere : nocturnal vehemence, New York kiosk, winter of abdication crisis Issue : confrontation between angry public morality and private tenderness
Jonas emmène son élève à l'exposition et: Jonas takes his student to the exhibition and tells him that the two best American artists are not included; Elaine decides to meet them; In two weeks she has met with Kooning and knows that she will marry him Words: Jonas: from Kooning and Gorky are the best and not at the show; Elaine : it took him “about two weeks” Atmosphere : voluntary lightning strike, immediate fascination (“mesmerized”) Issue : the beginning of everything — the life of Elaine as an artist
Scène sept de la première partie : deux: Scene seven of the first part: two figurines of moving plans with contrasting colors are manipulated in front of the public; shapes and colours overlap, the chromatic intensity varies under lighting; the scene is performance, demonstration and end-of-course exam at once.
