Atmosphere: Ludic, optical, theatrical — audience becomes observer-spectator Issue: Merge spectator and performer, treat the scene as a total work of art
Quatre gamins font l'école buissonnière: Four kids do the bushy school around a fire; Perry emerges from a scarlet sheath, its white form appears and disappears between trunks; the children look for him, embarrassed by the strings of the game between their fingers, and designate him in turn Words: “Regardez ! c'est Perry Westover qui s'entraîne pour la course !” — “Où ? où ? je ne le vois pas” — “Là il est !” Atmosphere: admiring terror, autumn fire, red shrapnel Issue: the old man become legendary figure in the eyes of children
Rice convoque une réunion générale dans: Rice convenes a general meeting in the Lee Hall lobby on institutions that blindly survive their goals, and then proposes to decide, that night, to close the college to make it unique. Silence; Someone's a hood. The debate begins, Rice is ready for all arguments and dominates with its powerful voice. The tortured man in his country's prisons rises and launches a tirade without direct connection to the subject. La meeting goes away; People get up and move; Rice sits at the end of the table, smoking his pipe, a tiny log cabin with matches placed on his elbow. Words: Rice: “survivent à leurs buts mais continuent aveuglément” institutions; “pourquoi ne pas décider, ce soir même, de fermer le collège pour qu'il devienne unique parmi toutes les institutions ?” Atmosphere: silence, hiccups, oratory fever — “équivalent moral et émotionnel d'une vieille réunion de réveil”; then appeasement, pipe smoke Issue: test the community's attachment to its institution, and reveal Rice's ambivalence to any attachment
Adamic lit son brouillon plein d'éloges: Adamic reads his draft full of praise for Rice; the discussion turns to criticism: students dare say for the first time that Rice is an insensitive Socrates; Zeuch denounces ghost-writing; Rice admits its heaviness, invites students to come and comment, tells them that they share the fault of having raised it by bringing to it problems that they could deal with themselves, and calls to see the good advertising side of the article. Words: Zeuch: Rice “a pratiquement ghost-écrit pour M. Adamic. C'est un secret ouvert.” Rice: Students have their share of responsibility in its power. Atmosphere: Rare community tension, first veiled and then declared criticism Issue: The charism of Rice becomes a community affair; revelation of his hunger for recognition
Avant leur départ, Adamic lit son projet: Before they left, Adamic read his draft article to a community meeting. The article honours courageous students, distinguishes Albers and Wunsch, but especially celebrates Rice, describing it as “idéaliste-optimiste”, and compiles the most complete summary to date of its philosophy of education, with lengthy quotes from Rice. “an idealist-optimist: intelligent, well-informed”; Harper's publication, p. 519 sq. Consequences: Rice becomes the stake: public hero of the college
Max Weber s'adresse au congrès réuni fac: Max Weber addresses the congress meeting in the face of the disastrous situation in the United States and against fascism abroad: the artist is invited to make relationships, and ends “connecté au dépôt de mendicité”. Quote by Weber on artists' poverty
Avant même l'arrivée de Gropius à Cambri: Even before Gropius arrived in Cambridge in 1937, Dean Hudnut approached Albers several times, without agreement. Jill Pearlman argued that Hudnut, although a modernist, did not want to recreate the Bauhaus at the Graduate School of Design and invoked budgetary problems. Letters from Hudnut of 21 February and 23 March 1936.
Après une première version, Adamic lit s: After a first version, Adamic read his article word for word in front of the whole community, stating that it is a journalistic text intended to make known the college, then to revise for a book. La first part (rollins counter, foundation) is well received; then rumbling: portrait of Rice in chief and savior (“questions of educational policy were left almost entirely to the leader”), idealization of the influence of the group, people who “meurent” and reborn from their ex-self. A free and prolonged discussion breaks out after reading. Adamic: People at BMC “die”, burn with self contempt, then “reborn” get up from the ashes of their ex-self Consequences: La meeting turns against Rice, accused of encouraging idealized vision and preventing its realization
Joe Martin ouvre : le collège n'est pas: Joe Martin opens: the college is not as good as Adamic says, his examples are the exception. Evarts: There's malice, too much. Hendrickson: The influence of the group sometimes stiffens the defenses. Barber attacks Rice publicly: the group doesn't know when to stop, after a man has been crushed he is left “cuire dans son jus”; Rice judgments become group property; Rice “abuse délibérément de son pouvoir ou ne se rend pas compte de sa force”; “trop de moutons dans cet endroit”. Nat French confirms: Rice hurt. Wunsch defends Rice and challenges; Goldenson answers: “We have a rough Socrates here, perhaps we need a little Jesus”. Rice ends up with a long confession and a plea to break his power. Rice remains silent during the attack of Barber, firing imperturbably on its pipe Consequences: The debate continues for weeks, at meals, in studies, letters and diaries; Most consider the debate beneficial, others are shocked; clarification and aggravation of antagonisms
L'attaque de DeVoto (Harper's, avril 193: The attack on DeVoto (Harper's, April 1936) triggered exchanges. Adamic finds the text “une scream”. Gannett, in the Herald-Tribune and then in private, judged a third of “ignorance grossière” DeVoto's remarks and recalled Theodore Parker's judgment on Brook Farm: success for individuals, failure as a community. DeVoto replica with fury. Harold H. Anderson (University of Iowa) provides the most brilliant answer, comparing the hierarchy of DeVoto between intellectual work and manual to choose between reading a sonnet and taking a bath. Chronology: letters of March 24, March 29, April 6, May 8, 1936 Consequences: Public defence of the college model
Adamic lit son texte mot à mot, préambul: Adamic reads his text word for word, preamble on his intentions; the first part goes well; The rumbles rise to Rice in “top dog and Savior”; Total silence until the end of the play, then free discussion that runs in Rice trial: Martin, Evarts, Hendrickson, then the Barber rule attack; French confirms; Wunsch counterattack; Goldenson: “un Socrate rude, il nous faudrait un peu de Jésus”; Adamic calls Rice; Long confession of Rice, lip pipe Words: Rice: “The worst sin in the world is impatience, and I am the most impatient person here”; “You should make yourselves into little anti-Rices”; “Rise up so that I'll not amount to anything” Atmosphere: full room, tension contained during reading, eruption at the end, whole night of debate Issue: community judges its founder, who puts himself on charge
Adamic décrit le processus par lequel un: Adamic describes the process by which a student, after the dark night of despair and isolation of his first months, is spiritually gathered in the group. Harper's, April 1936; “The lift of an eyebrow to them is a sentence” Consequences: Serves as a target for the author's criticism and the response of Bernard De Voto
Rice creuse des pommes de terre quand un: Rice digs potatoes when a student approaches it: “You're a nice one”. He plays innocence, learns that Knickerbocker claims to be dismissed, suggests that he ask to see the letter of the Board — the wording of which does not amount to a dismissal and leaves open a possibility of redress. Rice concludes that Knickerbocker has been a liar and that its supporters abandon him. Rice's response in tone of acid innocence: “We did? Are you sure?” Consequences: Duberman nuance: revolution was not so easy; Knickerbocker and Goldenson announce they will come back in the fall for their year of grace
L'essai d'Adamic fait connaître le collè: Adamic's essay makes the college known for the first time seriously: first contact with advertising, beginning of mythogenesis. In the following months, the college receives 40 to 50 letters of information per day, and for years of applications inspired by the article. 40-50 letters/day Consequences: Myth of BMC launched; Inflow of applications
Publication dans Harper's d'une première: Publication in Harper's of a first version of “Black Mountain: An Experiment in Education”, taken over in 1938 in My America (Harper & Bros.). Harper's, April 1936; Book 1938. Consequences: Registration of the college in the lexicon of the educational “expérience”.
Seule voix critique hors Black Mountain: The only critical voice outside Black Mountain: DeVoto compares participation in Black Mountain with that in Brook Farm, in prison or in the army, Judge “carrément dangereuse”, resembling “à un sanatorium pour maladies mentales tenu par des amateurs optimistes”. Adamic writes to Rice that DeVoto “résume ce qui ne va pas dans l'éducation et le monde”. Rice attributes the problem to the Utahne origin of DeVoto who hated the word “communauté” as much as Rice the Methodist Church. Harold H. Anderson (University of Iowa) reply: DeVoto compares the incomparable, “comme demander si l'on préfère lire un sonnet ou prendre un bain”; What laboratory does it take to find out how humans can live together? Harper's, vol. CLXXII, April 1936, p. 605 Consequences: National Controversy, Adamic defenders rise
Le board of fellows vote l'envoi d'avert: The board of followers votes the sending of warnings: to Knickerbocker at the end of the first year of teaching, to Goldenson at the end of the second year — it is “tout à fait pessimiste” that they can “devenir le genre d'enseignant que nous voulons ici durablement”. Vote: 5 for (Rice, Dreier, Mangold, Albers, Mary Beaman Moderator student), 2 against (Georgia, Martin). Vote 5-2; Letter from Georgia to Knickerbocker of 15 April 1936 Consequences: Polarization of the community, non-reinstallation in December 1936
Rice creuse des pommes de terre ; une ét: Rice hollow potatoes; one student: “You're a nice one”; “What have I done now?”; he informs him that Knickerbocker claims to have been returned; Rice plays the astonishment and makes him ask the letter — a trap that discredits Knickerbocker in the eyes of Rice Words: “You just fired Knickerbocker” — “We did? Are you sure?” Atmosphere: acid irony under apparent innocence, in the garden land Issue: the battle of the version of the facts: dismissal or warning?
Trois mois au Mexique, arrivée en voitur: Three months in Mexico, arriving by car from the North Caroline (seven days or more driving, Josef not loving the plane). Wonderful climate, well-being and intense production. Josef took seven pounds (approx. 3 kg) and painted eleven (or twelve) oil canvases; Letter to the Kandinsky of August 22, 1936: Mexico, “terre promise de l'art abstrait, qui ici a des milliers d'années” Consequences: Constant transformation of the work of the two artists; Anni creates Escritura antigua and Monte Albán
Josef expose œuvre graphique et la série: Josef exhibits graphic work and the series of Clave de sol aiguarrelles at the newspaper El Nacional (15-25 August). He began abstract linear drawings, painted Arqueológico and Templo, first studies for Tenayuca. The Albers meet Diego Rivera. Anni weaves two large tapestries, Escritura antigua and Monte Albán. Mexico City Address: Calle de París 23; letter to the Kandinsky of 22 August 1936
Exposition à El Nacional (15-25 août) :: Exhibition in El Nacional (15-25 August): graphics and Treble Clef series with gouache; beginning of abstract drawings, Archaeologic and Temple paintings; first studies for Tenayuca; meeting Diego Rivera. Anni weaves Ancient Writing and Monte Alban. Letters to the Kandinsky (22 August 1936, Calle de Paris 23): Josef is a full-day photography.
Pleine page photographique dans le suppl: Full photo page in Sunday New York Times supplement of June 7, 1936. A member of BMC judged it “horrible, mensongère à souhait”; the mail received (50-55 letters in the first week, about 40 the second) often started with “Dear Rollins Rebels” or “The Black Mountain Cooperative College”... “c'est le collège de mes rêves, d'autant qu'il ne coûte rien”. 50-55 letters the first week, ~40 the second Consequences: Deceptive public image of the college
Alice postule à l'été 1936 ; un membre d: Alice applied in the summer of 1936; one faculty member, doubting “if the college could stand another vampire”, voting against; he is put in minority and Alice enters in autumn among fifty-five students. 55 students back in 1936
Exposition des peintures à l'aquarelle «: Exhibition of “Clave de sol” watercolor paintings and recent Josef engravings, under the auspices of the LEAR (Ligue des Écrivains et Artistes Révolutionnaires), near the Parque de la Alameda and the Palacio de Bellas Artes (completed in 1934). Article in one of El Nacional on 16 August; Josef acclaimed as “l'un des fondateurs de l'abstractionnisme”. He expected negative criticism and was surprised at the reception. Perhaps organized with the help of Porset; one of the first exhibitions of his work in the Americas Consequences: Josef discovers that Latin American art is open, eclectic, favourable to abstraction
Gouaches « Treble Clef » et gravures réc: “Treble Clef” gouaches and recent Josef engravings exhibited in the lobby of the seat of the left daily El Nacional, 15 Avenida Dr. Mora, along the Alameda Park, close to the Palacio de Bellas Artes (completed in 1934). Under the patronage of LEAR (Liga de Escritores y Artistas Revolucionarios); First page article of El Nacional on August 16, 1936; large crowd of intellectuals and artists at the opening; Josef hailed as “l'un des fondateurs de l'abstraction”. Address: 15 Avenida Dr. Mora, alongside Alameda Park Consequences: One of the first Josef exhibitions in the Americas; radical press publishes long articles; Josef had expected adverse criticism
L'exposition, liée à la Ligue des Artist: The exhibition, linked to the LEAR, attracts a host of intellectuals and artists in sight; El Nacional title in one of 16 August 1936 that Albers is “l'un des fondateurs de l'abstraction”, his works being perceived as revolutionary by their complete break with any historical or anecdotal trend. First page article of El Nacional, 16 August 1936; "One of the founders of abstraction" Consequences: Josef expected hostile criticism; He wrote to Kandinsky a few days later that the radical press had published lengthy praiseworthy articles.
Anni écrit aux Kandinsky qu'elle a beauc: Anni writes to the Kandinsky that she loved Rivera's first frescoes very much but that he now makes revolutionary illustrations “horribles”, while finding him powerful and more interesting than his current painting. letters to Kandinsky, summer 1936
Un mois avant, Noguchi avait laissé ente: A month before, Noguchi had suggested that he could come to work at Black Mountain and build a wall in bas-relief; Rice, Evarts and Martin, excited by his talent and personality, had met him. Nothing came out of it, apparently because of the opposition of Albers. Letter from Martin to Mangold, August 31, 1936
Inauguration de Clave de sol et de gravu: Inauguration of Clave of soil and engravings under the auspices of the LEAR, crowd of artists and intellectuals, article in one on August 16, Josef proclaimed founder of abstractionism Words: Josef in Kandinsky: “j'attendais des critiques négatives... mais ce fut tout le contraire” Atmosphere: Unexpected triumph in the left press Issue: Latin American recognition against New York forgetfulness
Gouaches et gravures de Josef accrochées: Josef gouaches and engravings hung in the lobby of the radical newspaper, under the aegis of the LEAR; a large crowd of artists and intellectuals; El Nacional salutes him on August 16 as “l'un des fondateurs de l'abstraction”; Josef, who was waiting for hostility, writes to Kandinsky that the artists were extremely interested Words: Josef in Kandinsky: “J'attendais des critiques défavorables, ce fut l'inverse” (paraphrase) Atmosphere: Post-revolutionary fervor, intense curiosity for abstraction Issue: The German abstract painter confronted with the muralist Mexico he considers for propaganda — and disavowed by his own success
Josef, qui s'attendait à des critiques h: Josef, who expected hostile criticism because he despised socialist murals as propaganda, sees the crowd of intellectuals and artists rushing; El Nacional the sacred in one “l'un des fondateurs de l'abstraction”; The radical press publishes long articles. Words: In Kandinsky: “J'attendais des critiques adverses, ce fut l'inverse : les artistes étaient extrêmement intéressés.” Atmosphere: Surprise and euphoria after apprehension. Issue: The recognized abstraction of revolutionary murals.
Les pour et contre de l'admission d'un é: The pros and cons of admission of a student named “Sweeney” are the subject of a four-page typed letter (single line) of Tasker Howard, then to the admission committee, to the entire committee; The Journal of John Evarts reported this in September 1936. four simple interline pages
Kocher, encore rédacteur en chef d'Archi: Kocher, still editor-in-chief of Architectural Record, cites BMC among ten pioneering institutions in design pedagogy, alongside MIT, Harvard, Cranbrook, Taliesin, etc. Other schools cited: University of Cincinnati, MIT, Michigan, Cranbrook, Taliesin, Minnesota, Harvard, Fine Arts Institute of Design, NYU; he cites the trial of Albers “Art as Experience” (Progressive Education, Oct. 1935) Consequences: National visibility of the college in the architectural milieu
The Architectural Record consacre un art: The Architectural Record devotes an article to the Education of the Architect and includes Black Mountain, although the College does not have an official architecture program; A. Lawrence Kocher was the editor of the journal, which probably explains this inclusion. The Architectural Record 80.3, p. 212
À l'automne 1936, Rice propose à la facu: In the autumn of 1936, Rice offered the faculty weekly discussions on teaching; Albers presides first, then the presidency rotates. Themes: value of the master class against dialogue; “impérialisme de l'enseignement”; “frontières et dangers des personnalités”; “déduction contre induction”. La faculty, which often attends the courses of each other, argues with first-hand information. The exact topics listed; rotating presidency Consequences: One of the few places of higher education where we discuss from the perspective of the student as well as the instructor
Inclus dans New Horizons in American Art: Included in New Horizons in American Art; meets the critic Harold Rosenberg
Six semaines après la rentrée d'automne,: Six weeks after the fall season, the Board of Fellows adopts an unambiguous resolution: Knickerbocker and Goldenson will not be renewed (Georgia and Martin are going back). According to Dreier, Rice remained behind, expressed his opinion without developing it. Consequences: Protest eruption
Zeuch, se voyant comme indépendant et pa: Zeuch, seeing itself as independent and paratoned from discontent, requires an extraordinary faculty meeting with student representatives — Rice and Albers having gone on a trip. It lasts late in the night, of a remarkable frankness, and exists in stenographic account. Zeuch asks why Knickerbocker was returned: it is not an “advance” on other institutions. Knickerbocker says he'd rather stay. Wunsch explains that he had hoped he would not come back, admired him to come back, and then learned from unsolicited students that he was forming “deux collèges”, a group moving away from the “centre”; angry students found support at Knickerbocker. Knickerbocker: isn't it natural? Zeuch: Isn't it healthy? Wunsch: Not if it's an “union of weakness”. Consequences: Uncovering contradictions between declared goals and actual college procedures
Dreier invite Albers à participer à 4 Pa: Dreier invites Albers to participate in 4 Painters: six works each by Albers, Dreier, Drewes (former student of Bauhaus) and Kelpe. Albers himself offered the Addison stage to Sawyer in June 1936; Bartlett Hayes' press release compares abstract art to music. Albers sends six recent paintings; lean catalog containing the Albers “Why I Favor Abstract Art” manifest; Local newspaper reproduces the press release almost word for word Consequences: First public manifesto of Albers in favor of abstract art
Certains jugent tout feedback (surtout f: Some consider any feedback (especially favourable) as flaring; Others see it as support. Albers summarizes the median route: as little intervention as possible, the student must say “j'ai fait mon travail”. Rice and Zeuch agree on the parsimony of negative feedback; Rice notes that the most devastating in Albers is the brief look at the work followed by a passage without a word. Zeuch refuses any praise (“Je ne dis jamais : c'est un bon travail”); Rice press, weary: Zeuch should follow Albers drawing lessons and be ignored once in a while. Knickerbocker defends the magisterial course which “peut susciter un intérêt et être une inspiration”, citing a professor of geology of Harvard who made “vivre et trembler la terre sur l'estrade”. Meeting of 19 October 1936
Zeuch suggère qu'il y a place même pour: Zeuch suggests that there is room even for the weirdest personalities: “Une personnalité désintégrée peut être une personnalité forte.” Albers: any school has the right to choose personalities adapted to its program. Rice Zeuch test : “Iriez-vous chercher de mauvais enseignants ?” Zeuch : “Oui. Prenez-en un ou deux.” Rice close : “Ne pouvez-vous pas faire confiance au Seigneur pour vous les envoyer ?” Meeting of October 12, 1936
Le board of fellows vote pour la premièr: The board of followers votes for the first time salaries beyond living expenses, determined “sur la base du besoin”, including intangible needs. Rice and Wunsch $2,100 each, Albers $1,700 (second), Georgia $1,300, Joe Martin $300 Consequences: Comparisons and grudges when amounts became public in June 1937
Rice et Albers absents en voyage ; Zeuch: Rice and Albers absent while travelling; Zeuch asks why Knickerbocker was dismissed, citing the college's proclaimed superiority; Dreier questions Knickerbocker who would prefer to stay; Wunsch exposes its conversion: initially hostile, admiring the return, then alerted by students about the formation of “deux collèges” Words: Zeuch: the “n'est pas un progrès” referral; Wunsch: “deux collèges” form; Knickerbocker: “n'est-ce pas naturel ?”; Wunsch: Not if it's “a union of weakness” Atmosphere: remarkable frankness, late in the night, stenographical report Issue: the gap between proclaimed ideals and actual procedures
Deux mois après son retour, Josef écrit: Two months after his return, Josef wrote to Kandinsky: Alfred H. Barr, whom he knew from Germany and who quoted his teaching in a note from the catalogue of Cubism and Abstract Art at MoMA, did not include him in the exhibition; He attributed it to Barr's narrow vision and complained that he had not painted since he returned. Quote: “le pauvre Barr, qui ne croit qu'aux œuvres reproduites le plus souvent”; Josef is 48 years old in 1936 Consequences: Reve his injury: ensuring his place in the annals of painting
Deux mois après le retour du Mexique, Jo: Two months after Mexico's return, Josef writes extensively on art at New York and Paris and mentions Cubism and Abstract Art at MoMA; Barr, whom he had met in Germany and who was interested in his teaching (footnote in the catalogue), did not include his work. Josef attributes it to Barr's narrow vision and complains that he has not painted since his return to Black Mountain. 12 paintings made in Mexico, zero since the return; Age: 48 Consequences: Reveals Josef's ambition and anxiety about its place in the history of painting.
Après Thanksgiving 1936, le board of fel: After Thanksgiving 1936, the board of Fellows voted for the non-reinstallation of the two teachers after the current year, with little instigation of Rice. Only Martin and Georgia voted against. Zeuch leads the counterattack, furious especially for Knickerbocker, and requires a review in faculty meeting, where Wunsch explains that information spontaneously from students has gradually undermined its confidence in the usefulness of Knickerbocker. Vote: Martin and Georgia against Consequences: Departure of the two professors at the end of the academic year
Après Thanksgiving, le board of fellows: After Thanksgiving, the board of Fellows voted for the non-renewal of Knickerbocker and Goldenson for the following year, with little momentum from Rice; Only Martin and Georgia vote against. Consequences: Trigger the Zeuch counterattack and the community crisis
Longue réunion où le Board of Fellows ex: Long meeting where the Board of Fellows explains its vote: Wunsch accuses Knickerbocker of creating a second college, a group of students stowed against Rice; Knickerbocker defends itself; the two remaining members of the Board (Martin and Georgia) reveal that they voted against; Zeuch protested against Rice sitting as prosecutor and judge; Goldenson complains that it was never observed in class before its notification. Wunsch heard from September that Knickerbocker “faisait bien”; his information came from unsolicited students; Dreier and Tasker Howard had spoken to five students Consequences: Strengthening internal split; after Christmas holidays, petition of Zeuch
Avant d'être recruté, Knickerbocker dit: Before being recruited, Knickerbocker said that he warned Rice at Cambridge that he was not a peaceful individual, that he was used to fighting for what he believed, and that Rice should not invite him if he did not want that type of person.
Environ trois mois après la rentrée, deu: About three months after school, two students fled to marry; the college reacts “pretty calmly ; the rector was more upset than anyone else” according to a member of the staff.
Albers est invité à donner trois atelier: Albers is invited to give three workshops to Harvard's newest Graduate School of Design, whose Dean Joseph Hudnut recruits Gropius.
« A Second Foreword » (décembre 1936) et: “A Second Foreword” (December 1936) and a speech at BMC's lunch at the Cosmopolitan Club of New York on December 9, 1936 (approx.) repeat the same paragraph on this distinction. two tapuscrits at the JAAF Archive; one “written in December 1936” registrant
La présidente de Sarah Lawrence, Constan: La president of Sarah Lawrence, Constance Warren, exchange with faculty on administration and curriculum; a delegation from St. John's College discusses several days of methods (Willimetz: “Rice ne fut jamais plus impressionnant que dans ce cadre”); Chicago School of Design students and professors inspect the art program; Among Antioch visitors, Will Hamlin immediately decided to transfer to Ohio after three years.
Wunsch expose : des faits arrivés gradue: Wunsch exposes: facts gradually arrived after September make it dubative about the usefulness of Knickerbocker; it would form “deux collèges”, a group moving away from the center. Knickerbocker replicates that Rice has an “effet extrêmement destructeur sur la personnalité”. Zeuch poses its doctrine of individual integrity. Tasker Howard returns the charge: Knick's warnings blind students. Wunsch specifies that the problem is out of class. Anni Albers requests the vote of the two remaining members of the Board: Martin and Georgia admit to having voted against, fearing a club college. King compares the Board's decision to the Hitlerian remilitarization of Rhineland. Zeuch protested: Rice sits as a prosecutor and judges a man he hates — “c'est le début de la fin”. Schawinsky asks Knickerbocker to explain its method: “la vie est le plus grand art”. Goldenson concludes: no one visited his classes, he was judged on things on the margins — “pourquoi n'a-t-on pas fait la chose décente ?” Words: Wunsch: “il y avait ici deux collèges en formation”; Wunsch: “si ce n'est une union de faiblesse”; Zeuch: “le début de la fin de Black Mountain College”; Goldenson : “pourquoi n'a-t-on pas fait la chose décente ?” Atmosphere : court tension, interrogation in good order, verbatim transcript Issue : the identity of the college : community welded around a centre or pluralism of individualities ; the fate of two teachers
Jonas la repère en classe : elle se dist: Jonas the landmark in class: she is distinguished by her appearance (black trench-coat, beret) and by the big book about the schizophrenia she is wearing — perhaps seeking reasons for her mother's behavior She relies on her “petit pull bleu” to be noticed; brief liaison; he takes her to the first exhibition of the American Abstract Artists Consequences group: Jonas presents her to Willem of Kooning in autumn 1938
Été 1937 : la mère d'Anni, Toni Fleischm: Summer 1937: Anni's mother, Toni Fleischmann, and her father Siegfried visit the Albers in Mexico; Toni keeps a diary of this stay, a major documentary source. Travel diary retained Consequences : Documentation of routes
Vers 1937, Albers photographie la pyrami: Around 1937, Albers photographed the Tenayuca pyramid, especially the stone snakes that belted its base; the site becomes a recurring pattern. print 25 x 20 cm approx.
Article d'Anni Albers publié dans le Bul: Article by Anni Albers published in the College Bulletin (No. 5); reprinted in College Art Journal in January 1944. Black Mountain College Bulletin, 5, 1937; College Art Journal, III, 2, January 1944, pp. 51-54
Opportunate d'acquerir des terres et bat: Opportunity to acquire rustic lands and buildings on the other side of the valley: an old camp and summer resort. 676 acres plus about 50 acres adjacent Consequences: The site is sign “Lake Eden” and purchased
Adamic revient au collège à l'automne 19: Adamic returned to college in the fall of 1937.
Procès-verbal d'une réunion de fin d'ann: Minutes of an end-of-year 1937 meeting on four students (“Cane”, “Carter”, “Norris”, “Somers”) — see details in the scenes. Consequences: Cane: decision rejected; Carter: returned to the outside world; Norris: doubt about return; Somers: allowed to stay
Le renvoi de Knickerbocker finit par ent: Knickerbocker's dismissal eventually led to the departure of about a third of the student body and faculty — proof, Duberman notes, that he was not without the magnetism that Rice denied him. Consequences: Major Schism in College History
De Kooning travaille sur une commande po: De Kooning works on an order for a section of a three-part mural entitled Medicine
Graham publie ce livre qui suscite des d: Graham published this book, which aroused discussion and established his reputation as an intellectual leader among the artists of his generation.
Albers propose un atelier de couleur : a: Albers offers a colour workshop: after the experience of the previous year, it wants to give more space to practical exercises; Each seminar should combine theoretical introduction and then practical work of students, continued in duty at home if possible.
Fort de l'expérience de l'année précéden: With the experience of the previous year, Albers offers the Dean Hudnut more practical exercises: each seminar should start with a theoretical introduction followed by manual work of students, extended if possible in duty at home. Letter to Dean Joseph Hudnut, JAAF archives.
Pique-nique célébrant la visite d'Aldous: Picnic celebrating the visit of Aldous Huxley, photographed: Rice, iron-ringed glasses on a full face, in lively conversation with Huxley surrounded by students and trees. picture : Back Huxley in the foreground
Moholy-Nagy rencontre Siegel, 24 ans, do: Moholy-Nagy meets Siegel, 24, whose portfolio (photograms, overprints, manipulated negatives) illustrates the types of photographic vision in his 1925 book.
Le professeur de théâtre Xanti Schawinsk: The theatre teacher Xanti Schawinsky, trained at Oskar Schlemmer at Bauhaus, creates his play Spectodrama: abstract costumes in folded paper and coloured plans, games of colorful lights, moving decorations, complex sound effects, theatre in circles. folded paper costumes Consequences: installs the college's theatrical experimentation culture
Essai sur l'enseignement des métiers : l: Test on the teaching of trades: raw material as a training ground for invention, the dual orientation of teaching (models for industry and work of art). test dated “1937”
Dès ses premiers talks publics en 1937,: From his first public talks in 1937, at twenty-five years old, Cage talks about his influences and procedures which he already named “expérimentales”; These texts will be widely published and gathered in Silence in 1961. Silence collection (1961) Consequences: La public awareness of Cage eclipses almost all other BMC practices, unlike Albers's largely unpublished writings
Devient citoyenne des États-Unis: Become a citizen of the United States
Rice répond à Hutchins qui prônait « la: Rice responds to Hutchins who advocated “la poursuite sincère des vertus intellectuelles” and “un stock commun d'idées fondamentales”; Rice argues that education must care what people feel, otherwise the structure of thought collapses as in Nazi Germany where pure spirit universities remained silent before Hitler article “Fundamentalism and the Higher Learning”, Harper's, 1937; Hutchins, “The Confusion in Higher Education”, 1936
Célèbre pour ses idées progressistes sur: Famous for his progressive ideas on music at school and his Concord Summer School of Music, Surette first came often enough to be considered visiting professor, then accepted a position in 1937. His musical influence was overshadowed by his literary interests: he read Blake aloud, and all began to read Blake. Consequences: the development of music education in the curriculum; Blake's vogue
Article « Fundamentalism and the Higher: Article “Fundamentalism and the Higher Learning” responding to the Hutchins program (University of Chicago, great classical texts, identical truth everywhere): Rice formulates its most clear philosophy — education as learning in a way of doing, not acquiring a stock of ideas; “savoir ne suffit pas”. Hutchins, The Higher Learning in America, 1936; article pp. 587-588, 595 Consequences: public definition of BMC philosophy
Les huit étudiants ne reviennent pas ; Z: The eight students do not return; Zeuch and King find additional positions during the summer, bringing the non-revenue faculty to five. The year begins with 55 students enrolled. 55 students enrolled; Five Faculty Departures Consequences: Apparent Climate Sanitation
Pendant que Nell fait de longs séjours à: While Nell spent long stays in Sullivan, Indiana, after her mother's death, Rice fell in love with a young student, met during the autumn ritual of circulation between students' studies. He describes this as an “spasme soudain” due to his marital misfortune. Rumors; Nobody knows if the relationship was physical. We will learn later that the young woman was more interested in another student. Shared glass in studies; previous rumours about Rice with a theatre professor from New Jersey College for Women and a secretary from Henry Allen Moe's office Consequences: Nell surprises Rice in flagrante delicto; Community fury after Christmas
Ses parents rendent visite à Frank à Cha: Her parents visit Frank at Chapel Hill and take her to dinner at Carolina Inn. Rice leaves the table for toilets; Nell, the face distorted by anger (“comme un chat furieux”), blows his son: “Je l'ai surpris. Je l'ai vue avec elle.” Frank rises up, walks to his room, weeps on his bed, then keeps silent towards his parents for weeks. Dinner at Carolina Inn, Chapel Hill chic restaurant Consequences: Durable family injury; Community conflict
Premier succès public : sa maquette pour: First public success: his model for the Hall of Pharmacy at the World Exposition of New York 1939 was accepted and then translated into life-size painting by professional frisquists. Consequences: Short-term success: deleted from WPA lists.
De Kooning emménage dans un nouveau loft: De Kooning moves into a new loft; The dialogue with Picasso and Gorky led to a series of self-portraits from 1938. He met Franz Kline and Barnett Newman in the late 1930s.
Reçoit une commande pour une fresque du: Receives an order for a fresco of the Hall of Pharmacy of the World's Fair of New York 1939 (executed by professional muralists); meets Philip Guston, Barnett Newman and art student Elaine Fried, who becomes her student. Consequences: Beginning of the relationship with his future wife and pupil
Le groupe AAA, fondé en 1937 en réaction: The AAA group, founded in 1937 in response to social realism and inspired by De Stijl, has no Kooning members: “j'étais avec eux” spiritually, but “je désapprouvais leur étroitesse, leur fait de me dire de ne pas faire quelque chose”. Quote: “I disagreed with their narrowness, their telling me not to do something” Consequences: Independence between figuration and abstraction
Herbert Bayer ne perd les faveurs du gou: Herbert Bayer lost the German government's favour only in 1937, after working for his propaganda exhibitions. Consequences: Previous to the United States
Malgré ses travaux de propagande, Bayer: Despite his propaganda work, Bayer lost the favours of the German government — he had a Jewish wife and did not support Nazi politics. Consequences: Prelude to his departure for the United States.
Gropius, premier invité pour le poste, l: Gropius, the first guest for the position, recommends it; He taught at the Harvard Graduate School of Design and in 1938 became head of the department of architecture. Consequences: Multiplication of Bauhaus exhibitions at MoMA and elsewhere; Bauhaus enters the bloodstream of American culture
Avec Marcel Breuer, les Gropius émigrent: With Marcel Breuer, Gropius emigrate for Walter to teach at Harvard's Graduate School of Design. American citizen in 1944; founded The Architects Collaborative (TAC) in 1945; died in 1969 at 86, spreading his architectural vision around the world — sometimes with hubris (Pan Am Building). Founded TAC 1945; Pan Am Building
Les nazis saisissent 102 Klee dans les m: The Nazis seized 102 Klee in the German museums in 1937 and included 17 in the “Entartete Kunst” exhibition in Munich; The catalogue compares its paintings to the work of internees schizophrenia and sees it as an “confusion”. 102 works seized, 17 exhibited
Le Troisième Reich confisque 102 Klee da: The Third Reich confiscates 102 Klee in German museums and exhibits 17 of them in the “Entartete Kunst” exhibition in Munich; The catalogue compares its paintings to the work of hospitalized schizophrenics and sees it as evidence of a psychologically unstable character. 102 works seized; 17 exhibited in Munich Consequences: Klee marked as “le plus dégénéré des artistes dégénérés”
Première exposition précoce d'aquarelles: First early exposure of watercolours on the coast of Maine; It then passes to the tempera and alternates from the two mediums.
Après les longues vacances de Noël, Zeuc: After the long Christmas holidays, Zeuch officially petitioned the Board to reconsider its action against Knickerbocker and Goldenson; the petition is rejected. A “os” thrown to Goldenson: permission to resign, as he claimed to have wanted. Dissidents turn to governance issues
Vers la mi-hiver, la liaison s'amorce. R: In mid-winter, the link began. Rice, walking with a student, explains that he knows Alice “un peu mieux” because she needs to be “brought out”, to feel important, “blossom” — benevolent father posture. During an evening of sketches, Alice, costumed in paper-maché that makes her tiny body and her head huge, parody a singer; Everyone's having fun except Rice, jealous. Paper-mashed costume, huge head Consequences: Rice, after the power struggle, goes “rock the community” with a love affair
Meyer conclut son réquisitoire contre l': Meyer concludes its petition against the “antique mal de la publicité”: it dealt with only one aspect (unproductive effort, creation of disproportionate desires, habit of advertising); “si insultants, si nerveux” panels did not survive; So “aujourd'hui nous démolissons ces panneaux”. No applause: nothing to rejoice about. billboard draped with a lemon yellow curtain; Meyer sits back in support Consequences: announces demolition
Vers 17 h, thé et gâteaux distribués ; t: Around 5:00 p.m., tea and cakes distributed; three carpenters explain the technique: sawn back supports left on a few stai, corners cut in the front posts as if to cut down pines; Tony pushes with all his weight, two others pull the stai with strings; the panel collapses with a crack and a deaf “bunnnnng”, cloud of dust, revealing the grass field and flowers of the meadows. The right panel, draped with lemon yellow, is preserved. Tony's cigar wrapped in paper, stored in the chest pocket, later lit up; “Un—deux—et trois !” countdown; children went behind to watch Consequences: the field found; a panel kept to be redone
Derrière un rideau bordeaux tenu par deu: Behind a burgundy curtain held by two young carpenters on ladders: a young linden with leaves in heart and some cream flowers in the sunlight. Dido explains: what appears behind a curtain or in a frame, it is considered more peacefully, “en lui-même”. Surprising, almost disappointment first, then understanding that leaves and petals are the organs of invisible roots; the tree had grown hidden behind a fence. Enraged applause of three or four minutes; Dido suggests exposing a tree alone in the middle of a theatre scene; Meyer objects that the tree would be less beautiful away from its meadow; Dido doesn't agree. The public hopes for a dialectic game, which does not take place. burgundy curtain, lemon yellow curtain, ladders, heart leaves, cream flowers Consequences: linden becomes one of the traditions of the Ninth of May
Harry, gant de base-ball au poignet, sor: Harry, a baseball glove on the wrist, pulls out a fried leaf from his hip pocket and reads with a loud voice a poem composed that day on the flowers of meadows gently growing in the high grass in the middle of the noise of baseball. No applause (boys are not applauded; all are “sans l'habitude de la publicité”), except children. Dido attracts him and whispers: “It is true, it is true!—the meadowflowers grow softly in the knee-deep grass”; The boy blushes to the ears and refuses to repeat what has been said. Fielder glove hanged on the wrist; curled sheet of the hip pocket; whispered remarks from other boys Consequences: reading this poem becomes customary in the Ninth of May
Un quatuor venu de plus de cent milles j: A quartet from more than a hundred miles played the Quartet op. 130 in Beethoven's b flat. Principles established by Dido and followed throughout the country: never a public gathering without excellent music; We do not surprise the unprepared soul with complicated music — they begin with simple, major and minor chords. Children and several adults walk away for half an hour. Description of the four musicians; During the Dance went Tedesca, Dido, haggard, think with horror of his ruined life and weep; The little Viola laughs and sings following the score, Mrs. Troy smiles at her “d'un air de reine”. Half-minute break before Cavatina; Maritimus's gaze on assistance; During the Cavatina, listeners are like dead, eyes open without seeing, arms in left positions; a very small child arrives from the field and is terrified; At the turn of the melody, tears flow. erect desks; agreement of instruments, pinched notes falling into the deepening silence; Tony's cigar lit up
Fin d'après-midi, soleil ovoïde derrière: Late afternoon, ovoid sun behind the hill tinting linen. Dido decorates the saved panel and proposes a principle: to display in public vehicles a poem, a mathematical theorem or the reasoning of a beautiful physical experience — “un seul acte de pensée qui vaille”; But he doesn't think we can extend it to the panels, because we can take too much time, worry the souls. The sun sets; He cannot break the silence and only makes a gesture; two boys drop the yellow curtain: appear a elegantly printed sentence and a large circle. Miss Campbell, English teacher, thinks the word “describe” is wrong. The Venus star shines on the hill; the assembly separates. setting sun tinting linen; Venus, “après-coup du Soleil” Consequences: foundation of “May Ninth” traditions: burgundy and lemon yellow, lime, reading of Dido and Walker poems
Fable satirique sur la marchandise (épig: Satirical fable on merchandise (Epigraph of Capital, Book I). Impetigo, once a buyer of twelve large scissors at wholesale prices, shakes a two dollar note (reputed unlucky) at the supermarket: Alcoa has just published a full page painted with aluminum paint in Saturday Evening Post boasting its utensils (“ils useront pour toujours”, “brilleront au mur”, “aucune saleté dans les courbes”); the same Tuesday, the company withdrew the range to reserve metal for National Defence. It's not the real frustration that comes with the “dépression nerveuse”, but the horrors of the imagination: the motorist in the rain to whom Texaco advertising promises comfort at the next turn, while it is forbidden to sell gasoline after sunset. The economist Impetigo sees with satisfaction the advertising refine its effects (each wants and “a absolument besoin” of everything) and with fear the lack of private income. “La face de l'économiste devint blanche.” two dollar note; 12 large scissors; metal pot with lid “Titegrip”; advertising page in aluminum paint; collection of aluminum by Boy Scouts on July 4th; saleswoman's response: “The Boy Scouts will collect your aluminum on the Fourth of July”
Dans Social Frontier, Dewey reproche à H: In Social Frontier, Dewey reproaches Hutchins for his recourse to a fixed authority: without saying it fascist, he compares his approach to the mistrust of freedom; who will decide the definitive truths? Rice, friend of Dewey, subscribes to this criticism. Social Frontier, III, January 1937, pp. 103-104
Quarante kilomètres en deux heures sur d: Forty kilometres in two hours on wet roads; the driver lays stones and mattresses to cross ruts; Arrived shaken, immediately forgotten in front of ruins unheard of for them Words: Toni Fleischmann in his journal: “la route est très mauvaise, presque impraticable sous les fortes pluies” Atmosphere: Boue, rain, bumps, then wonder The Issue: The physical price of the archaeological dream
Quarante kilomètres en deux heures sur u: Forty kilometers in two hours on a high rain road; the driver pilot through the mud, descends several times with help to open the passage to the Stock and laying stones; passengers arrive shaken but forget everything in front of ruins different from all the previous ones; the next day, laces towards Monte Albán. Words : Toni Fleischmann, journal : “la route est très mauvaise, presque impraticable à cause des fortes pluies” ; the old “bâtissaient toujours leurs temples aux plus beaux endroits”. Atmosphere: Boue, effort, shaking — then wonder. Issue: The Physical Price of Access to Art Sources.
Zeuch : « académiquement une perte sèche: Zeuch: “académiquement une perte sèche, il ne s'est pas amélioré”. Mangold: “a-t-il assez d'intelligence ?” Zeuch: “il n'a pas assez de volonté”. Mangold: “il a trop bu ce semestre”. Gair (student): spoke with him and with Leslie, his roommate; “ce lieu l'effraie, peut-être plus que tout autre ne le ferait”. Disposition: adjourned. Words: “Academically, I think he is a dead loss” (Zeuch); “this place scares him” (Gair) Atmosphere: Clinically speaking about absent students Issue: An alcoholic and frightened student on the verge of exclusion
Schawinsky : « le trimestre dernier il é: Schawinsky: “le trimestre dernier il était complètement égocentrique ; maintenant il fait des choses pour le groupe ; parfois il ne fait rien pendant des jours, mais on ne peut pas savoir s'il ne pense pas”. Evarts: “de la progression, mais il vaudrait mieux qu'il trouve un travail — il apprendrait à coopérer”. Weston: “nous échouons avec une personne de grande capacité”. Albers: “très talentueux mais très unilatéral ; toujours intellectuel ; un environnement plus dur lui ferait du bien ; il a besoin d'une forte réalité”. Verdict: Better for him to enter the outside world. Issue: Talent Against Community Engagement
Mangold : « très bon travail mais ne par: Mangold: “très bon travail mais ne parle pas en classe ; deuxième année ; faut-il la garder ?” Wunsch: “quelle est son influence ?” Mangold: “une morte en ce domaine”. Steinau: “un poids mort”. King: “l'an dernier elle se sentait une freak, plus cette année ; donnons-lui un an de plus”. Albers: “j'ai une image d'elle, la même que le premier jour — et ce n'est pas un masque”. French: “intellectuellement, elle devrait revenir”. Rice: “un cas où le Collège a échoué ; nous l'avons laissée vivre dans un petit cercle ; elle est plus isolée que jamais ; ce sera toujours un F — pour le Collège ; ce qu'elle veut le plus, c'est être aimée, et personne au monde ne la trouve importante”. Verdict: doubts about her return, to tell the parents if she wants to return; the admission committee and the treasurer can always refuse. Words: “The most important thing for her is to be liked. The difficulty is that there is nobody in the world who thinks she is important” (Rice) Atmosphere: A clumsy heart of a faculty that recognizes its own failure Issue: An isolated student, a mirror of community failure
Portell : « sa famille (midwestern insta: Portell: “sa famille (midwestern installée au Sud) et son lycée ont eu un mauvais effet ; ses travaux sont très bons, ils demandent de la pensée indépendante ; hier elle a rendu un article sur les Noirs trois jours à l'avance — un article qui exigeait un vrai courage pour quelqu'un de Géorgie”. Zeuch: “les deux seuls étudiants du Sud ici ont un sentiment d'infériorité face aux Nordistes”. Portell: “elle est consciente de sa situation financière ; il faut l'aider”. Albers: “elle a une compréhension mathématique ; je crois en elle comme Portell ; elle a besoin de plus de temps”. Rice: “cela la met à six ans d'âge mental ; je ne suis pas d'accord avec Albers et Portell — mais quand on amène quelqu'un ici, on contracte un engagement ; il ne faut pas abandonner avant d'avoir tout fait”. Albers: “son cerveau vaut mieux que sa bouche ; elle vaut plus que beaucoup d'autres”. Verdict: it stays. Words : “That brings her up to about six years old” (Rice) Atmosphere : Courteous confrontation Rice/Albers-Portell, arbitrated in favor of the student Issue : Should the college honour its debt to a poor student from the South
Alice paraît dans un costume de papier-m: Alice appears in a paper-mache costume making her tiny body and her head huge, parodying a singer; assistance is fun — except Rice, that jealousy already eats. Atmosphere: General laugh, deaf worry of a man in love Issue: The paternal mentor betrays himself as jealous lover
Repas champêtre sous les arbres ; Rice,: Country food under the trees; Rice, round glasses surrounded by iron, discuss with animation facing Huxley, photographed from the back in the foreground Atmosphere: Summer relaxation, trees, cross conversations Issue: The college receives the most famous writer in its young history
Ses parents invitent Frank à dîner. Rice: Her parents invite Frank to dinner. Rice abstains for toilets; Nell leans towards his son, hardened face “comme un chat furieux”, and blows his confidence. Frank rises without a word, walks to his room, falls on his bed and cries; His parents knock on his door, he can't talk to them and will keep them quiet for weeks. Words: Nell: “I caught him at it. I saw him with her.” (“Je l'ai surpris. Je l'ai vu avec elle.”) Atmosphere: Chic restaurant, sudden swings into emotional violence Issue: Intimate injury that repeats public crisis
Tony reprend son cigare, explique la tec: Tony takes back his cigar, explains the slaughter technique, counts “Un—deux—et trois !”, grows with all its weight; Crack, “bunnnnng” deaf, dust cloud; field and flowers reappear; the children behind shout “Ready!” Words: “O.K., boys— Ready? Here goes! One—two—and three!” Atmosphere: a burst of cracking assistance, dust, laughter from the carpenters reappearing Issue: concrete and joyful victory over advertising
Après la pause d'une demi-minute et le r: After a half-minute break and Maritimus's gaze, the Cavatina begins; assistance becomes like dead: eyes open without seeing, body without grace, arms in left positions; a little child arrives from the field and is afraid; at the turn of the melody, tears flow, breathing is “formelle avec le chant” Atmosphere: absolute silence, soft music violence, tears, evening light Issue: the total aesthetic experience that suspends the entire community
Harry, sans applaudissements, fourre sa: Harry, without applause, wraps its leaf in its pocket and moves away; Dido draws him near and whispers to him that his verse is true; the boy blushes deeply; the others ask what has been said, he will not say it Words: “It is true, it is true!—the meadowflowers grow softly in the knee-deep grass” Atmosphere: complicity with a low voice, modesty of the child Issue: the transmission of the master to the young poet, in secret
Discussions étudiantes et réunions commu: Student discussions and community meetings late winter-spring 1937 on the voice to be given to each. Rice replies that the college is first an educational adventure, not a community, and that it is better judge than anyone who has to teach. Zeuch prefers to trust the entire community rather than a small group. Consequences: Protestation of eight students
Pendant les vacances de printemps de la: During the spring vacation of Grade 4, four students (two boys, two girls) leave together in Florida. In the fall, the college found that they did not have “été intelligents” and risked the moral reputation of the institution, already suspected of being an “centre du libre amour”. The Board of Fellows and the Faculty meet several times, with the participation of student officers and the summons of interested persons. Journal de Mort Steinau: April 7 (Board sits with the four), April 8 (decision that Fred and Ms. Moellenhoff speak to them), April 9 (student meeting on mixed groups on travel) Consequences: Provisional agreement: mixed groups do not go on vacation together; no other sanction
Huxley, venu de sa propre initiative ave: Huxley, who came on his own initiative with his wife, son and friend Gerald Heard, chatting with everyone, asking difficult questions about the United States, astonished by the poverty of the deep South, praised the extraordinary “espérance” of America, deplored the “dictature des patrons” and wondered “comment descendre l'autogouvernement jusque dans l'industrie”. One night, round table on the “limites du roman”. Heard, even more impressive for many, speaks of disposing of all addiction, of unlimited responsibility between members of a true community, announces that man will soon be able to converse with trees and flowers and that telepathy and clairvoyance remain to be explored by the West. Quatre mois après la mort de Klee, Time: Four months after Klee's death, Time characterizes his work as a childish scribble, an artistic scribble; the article, unsigned, mentions the American collections and notes that American connoisseurs paid its ectoplasmic scratches 750 dollars a canvas — direct reference to Edward Warburg's purchases, whose prices are reduced by 50 dollars by mistake. $750 per canvas according to Time (error: $50 less than reality); Willard and Buchholz galleries in New York Consequences: The American public discovers Klee through this cartoon; the article also reports the invitation of Gropius to Bauhaus and ironizes on Hitler and degenerate art
Chaque après-midi, camions descendant la: Every afternoon, trucks coming down the mountain full of teachers and students; on the construction site, Straus with white hair throws stones at a young girl who passes them to a boy who seals them in the cement wall; Sarton helps the wall one afternoon. Words: “Rosalind, it is a great sight…” Atmosphere: Joy of common work, almost religious Issue: Utopia in action
Été 1941, de retour aux États-Unis, Jose: Summer 1941, back in the United States, Josef began a long series of pen and ink drawings, then translated into zincography, evoking the ancient temples of Mexico; Titles: Santuario, A Monte Albán.
Été 1941 : vaste série de dessins à la p: Summer 1941: extensive series of pen and ink drawings with clear and modulated lines and strict geometries evoking the sites of ancient temples in Mexico; Then translated into zinc lithographs, under the collective title Graphic Tectonics, with evocative titles such as Sanctuary, Shrine, To Monte Alban. Titles : Sanctuary, Shrine, To Monte Alban
Récemment rentré aux États-Unis, Josef A: Recently returned to the United States, Josef Albers undertook a wide range of pen and ink drawings, with sharp and modulated lines and strict geometries evoking the sites of ancient temples in Mexico; they will be translated into zinc lithographs. Drawings and ink; Evocative titles : Sanctuary, Shrine, To Monte Alban
Surette, crédité d'avoir commencé la mus: Surette, credited with having started music at the college, died in 1941 leaving him with a considerable musical library.
Réfugiée d'Europe en guerre arrivée aux: A refugee from Europe at war who arrived in the United States in 1940, admitted to the University of Chicago without a diploma, Zoya spent a summer at BMC: memorable Eric Bentley course, warmth of Graaf Frances (Russian history), smiling face of refugee musicologist Heinrich Jalowetz, professor of philosophy “eingegbildée” (pretentious) named Straus, modesty and great pedagogical talent of Josef Albers; corn denning under a lead sun and helping to build a silo. After two weeks of quarantine for a rubella, his hasty departure. 14 days of quarantine in a small study cubicle (German rubella) Consequences: experience closest to a kibbutz for her
Curieuse de voir la vie au-delà du collè: Curious to see life beyond college, Zoya hides in a truck up to Asheville. During the driver's races, she drinks at a fountain in the back of a five-ten store and feels dozens of eyes piercing her back: the sign indicates “For Colored”. sign “For Colored” above the fountain Consequences: a few days later, she lays her hoe in the field, packs her bags and returns to Chicago
Face à l'opposition à la « mystique du t: Faced with opposition to the “mystique du travail”, the faculty sets one to three afternoons a week as the optimal working time on the site, more likely to harm the college's studies and life. 1 to 3 afternoon/week Consequences: Official framework for volunteering
Rejoint le corps enseignant, venant de R: Joins the faculty, coming from Reed College where she was appreciated but where the institution was overstaffed 37 years old, doctor of the University of Leiden (thesis on Serge Essenine)
Questionnaire distribué à la communauté: Questionnaire distributed to the community: “Quelle est votre opinion sur la combinaison travail académique et travail physique ?” Results: students (1 indifferent, 2 unfavourable, 11 favorable, 15 very favorable); students (2, 9, 11, 16); teachers (1, 0, 6, 1); teachers (3, 2, 6, 4). Complete encrypted table, shorty Forbes
Panofsky vint au collège pendant le cong: Panofsky came to college during the Albers sabbatical leave in 1941.
