Le collège quitte les bâtiments de Blue: The college leaves the buildings of Blue Ridge for the site of an old summer camp by Lake Eden, surrounded by woods, hills and mountains. former summer camp; semi-rustic main building with large social hall and dining room with a long grilled veranda overlooking the lake Consequences: new living and teaching environment
Le collège quitte le campus de Blue Ridg: The college leaves the Blue Ridge campus (Lee Hall) for the site of a former summer camp on Lake Eden, several kilometres below. Former summer camp site surrounded by woods, hills and mountains; semi-rustic main building with large social hall and dining room with long grilled veranda overlooking the lake; field stone fireplace. Consequences: New educational opportunities related to the surrounding nature.
Albers introduit le concept de matiére e: Albers introduces the material concept by showing 28 photographs of magazines with pronounced textures, with comments. Fashion photo: “la peau lisse et la dentelle froissée s'aident”; whisky advertising: “liquides, glace et argent chatouillent l'appétit”; Other: “Glace et roses. Cruel, mais intéressant.”
Albers présente 28 photographies de mati: Albers presents 28 photographs of materials, including a fashion photo (smooth skin and curled lace), two whisky advertisements (liquid, ice and silver; ice and roses). 28 photographs; “Ice and roses. Cruel, but interesting” Consequences: Official introduction to the design course
Écrivant en 1941, Albers précise que ces: Writing in 1941, Albers specifies that these studies are technical exercises concerning only the craft of drawing, necessary preparation for serious work; They do not directly give works but develop discipline. Essential goal: “seeing eyes and obedient hands”.
Chaet, alors étudiant à Boston, assiste: Chaet, then a Boston student, attended an Albers conference — his first meeting with him (date of 1941 according to the inscription of Albers on a manuscript of the speech). Interviewed on 5 January 1996 by Fred Horowitz.
Photographie prise par Albers du Studies: Photograph taken by Albers of the Studies Building under construction (ca. 1941).
À sa mort en 1941, Surette, fondateur de: Upon his death in 1941, Surette, founder of the Concord Summer School of Music, a member of the advisory board since 1933 and a short professor, left his entire music library to the college. huge recorded music library Consequences: Feeds campus music saturation
Engagée à l'automne 1941 comme enseignan: Engaged in the fall of 1941 as a plastic apprentice teacher, reclassified a year later to applied arts, then in 1943 in charge of wood work, post held until his departure in 1947. Consequences: The construction program is intensifying, especially at the farm.
Exposition de maquettes d'architecture d: Exhibition of architectural models of low-cost houses, photographed by Claude Stoller; The four-winged Studies Building (sleeping, library, administration, classrooms) is also modeled.
En un an environ, les étudiants achevère: In about a year, students completed their individual workspaces in the 200-foot building (about 61 m). Building: local stone foundation in rubble, wood frame, transit coating (asbestos), International style in the middle of a rural southern landscape Consequences: The building becomes an icon of the college and still remains today
Embauche de Molly Gregory comme apprenti: Molly Gregory was hired as an apprentice teacher and installation of the woodworking workshop, where Kocher probably built his stool and table. Consequences: Development of woodworking in college
Maison conçue par Kocher pour le profess: House designed by Kocher for Heinrich Jalowetz music teacher; acoustic experience with perforated plywood wall panels and vermiculite ceiling coating that visibly improved the sound of Jalowetz's piano. Claude Stoller was the construction manager (captain job). Conventional and prefabricated elements; The house, slightly redesigned, is now a private residence Consequences: Stoller becomes professional architect
Le jeune Mark Dreier, enfant du professe: Young Mark Dreier, the child of Professor Theodore Dreier, was tragically killed in a vehicle accident on campus; In his memory, Alex Reed (student) and Molly Gregory (faculty) designed and built Quiet House, a simple stone building. white painted wooden doors, handles and black hinges Consequences: Place of consolation, retreat and renewal for this mostly secular community
Pour Le Médecin malgré lui (1666) et Les: For Le Médecin spite of himself (1666) and Les Précieuxs ridicules (1659) directed by Robert Wunsch, student Frances Kuntz manufactures twenty-six costumes and decor with a budget of $25: she sprays cheap muslin to imitate velvet, silk and lace, and uses peanuts, tapered wheat, wadding, wood chips, crepon paper and serpillars to create elaborate wigs. budget of $25; 26 costumes Consequences: example of low-resource visual ingenuity
Wunsch produit le premier magazine litté: Wunsch produced the college's first literary magazine, “......toward a projected College magazine”, exclusively composed of student works, printed in the early 1940s as the United States entered the war. Four pieces in prose and three poems; Contributors: Jane Mayhall, Frances Goldman, Emil Willimotz, Robert Sunley, Sue Spayth Consequences: Creative writing begins to be valued as an artistic practice rather than an educational exercise
Un document « toward a projected College: A “toward a projected College magazine” document dated around 1941 is kept in the college archives; he feeds several notes of the article on writing exercises.
Selon le souvenir de sa sœur, à huit ans: According to her sister's memory, at the same time at the age of eight Rauschenberg had as pets a horned lizard, a goat, a cock, redfish and two hunting dogs that had a litter of nine puppies. A horned lizard, a goat, a cock, red fish, two hunting dogs, nine puppies Consequences: Alloway connects this menagerie with the animals stuffed with combustibles (angora goat, Canyon eagle, Satellite cocks and Odalisque).
L'été de ses onze ans, le bateau ramenan: In the summer of its eleven years, the boat bringing the family back to the island after a birthday party exploded. Susan is badly burned; his brother Danky, his 18-month-old elder, dies. She remembers: “J'ai changé après la mort de Danky”; their parents had catalogued them — she “la bonne”, she “le intelligent”. explosion of the vessel; serious burns; brother and sister separated for a year and a half Consequences: every year on Danky's birthday she does a work for him; First permanent contact of the family with “la dure réalité”; the adoption of a girl and a boy; family life changed forever
Lettre affectueuse du père (signée « Dad: Father's affectionate letter (signed “Dad”): glad that Jean lets him ride his horse, suggests that he may become a Pony Express rider; Questions about baseball, promise of a finger glove next time; He listens to radio games almost every afternoon; He joins a comic song on biblical baseball: “Ève vola la première, Adam vola la seconde, et Satan arbitra la partie ; Rebecca emmena le lanceur au mur… Goliath fut retiré par David, Cain frappa un coup sûr, le Fils prodigue fit un home run, et frère Noah distribua des chèques pour la pluie”. Baseball glove, radio, song “Eve stole first”
Goodman rédige une analyse théorique du: Goodman writes a theoretical analysis of the frame and screen, citing films and the state of cinema of 1941 explicit reference: “encore, en 1941, dans le style de l'Exposition de Paris de 1925”
En pleine rupture avec les valeurs polit: In full rupture with the political and moral values of American society, Goodman undertook to revise a short short story composed in 1935 and discovered that it was written in a way that he no longer mastered: overdetermined symbolism and naturalistic detail became intolerable to him. Roman composed in 1935, revision attempted in 1941, balance taken in 1945 Consequences: It draws a theory of the connection between the author's psychological attitude and the literary way
Réunion de Black Mountain College à New: Meeting from Black Mountain College to New York; Albers is opposed to “laisser-faire indécis de beaucoup d'écoles dites progressives”.
Au mariage de Frank et Ann Pace à Haverf: At the marriage of Frank and Ann Pace in Haverford, John Andrew and Nell Rice were last seen. Consequences: La separation of the couple ends in divorce.
Alors que son divorce avec Nell se profi: As her divorce with Nell develops, Rice meets the woman who will become her second wife: a beautiful blonde of Norwegian origin, graduated from St. Olaf College, secretary in Manhattan and part-time singer in small ensembles. Consequences: Dikka will push Rice to complete his book; She will become Dikka Moen Rice.
En 1941, après qu'elle et toute sa famil: In 1941, after she and her whole family had to sell their jewellery or use it as bribes, Anni made and exhibited necklaces of amazing originality with trombones, sink colanders, hairpins and other hardware and stationery items. Trombones, sinks, hairpins.
Il bâtit la longue pièce servant de stud: He built the long studio room, poured the concrete floor, laid a row of north lanterns inclined to 30 degrees; it produces about twenty sculptures a year. 30° lanterns; two oil stoves; 20 pieces per year Consequences: installation of the “Terminal Iron Works”
Agacée par le temps que Bill passe avec: Annoyed by the time Bill spends with Gorky, Elaine takes him to another party to meet nineteen-year-old Agnes Magruder, “très belle, très élégante” Consequences: Agnes becomes his second wife eight months later
Article sur le travail textile au Black: Article on textile work at Black Mountain College published in The Weaver, vol. VI, No. 1, p. 3-7. The Weaver, VI, 1, January-February 1941, p. 3-7 Consequences: Make known the BMC weaving workshop off campus
Pendant que le chauffeur du camion fait: While the truck driver is shopping, Zoya explores, drinks at a fountain in the back of the store; She feels dozens of eyes piercing her back, turning around: everyone stares at her. She looks for her mistake, then sees the sign “For Colored”. Atmosphere: sudden malaise, incomprehensive shame, tilting Issue: revelation of segregation; decision to leave BMC a few days later
Quelques jours après Asheville, en binan: A few days after Asheville, by bumping corn, she stops in the middle of the field, lays her hoe, packs her bags and returns to Chicago to understand this country that owes her life and refuses freedom to a part of her citizens. Atmosphere: clear gesture, resolution in a field under the sun Issue: bifurcation of a life: future civil rights activist
De retour d'un semestre à Harvard, Alber: De back from a semester to Harvard, Albers compares a 300-year-old institution to an 8-year-old and concludes that the youngest, with no great past behind it, remained alive and promising. Words: He did not find the comparison discouraging. Atmosphere: Prickly pride of the small Southern college in front of the northeast giant. Issue: Defense of BMC's vitality against the respectability of Harvard.
Albers montre 28 photographies de magazi: Albers shows 28 magazine photographs; he comments on a fashion photo (smooth skin against curled lace), two whisky advertisements (liquid, ice and silver; ice and roses). Words: “Voyez comme les deux surfaces s'aident ; la peau lisse et la dentelle froissée”; “Glace et roses. Cruel, mais intéressant.” Atmosphere: A sharp look on mass culture.
Une jeune employée s'achète un ice cream: A young employee buys an ice cream soda on her day off, then decides to buy a dress without trying it; Back home, the dress doesn't fit her and her parents reprimand her for wasting her money Issue: Lesson of modesty and frugality, imitating the moral news of PEA anthology
Un vieux boutiquier insatisfait de sa vi: An old shopkeeper dissatisfied with his life at “peser des clous et mesurer de la corde” sits on the wooden bench in front of his shop, looks at the dusty green station and says he wants to create; The narrator wonders what he wants to create Words: “I want to create” (I want to create), says Mr Goldfinch Atmosphere: Melancholy of Unsatisfied Creative Desire Issue: Innate Creativity vs. Work Life
Par un jour gris, l'odeur de cornichons: On a grey day, the smell of pickles or mould suddenly makes a childhood memory; the teenager sent by his parents to grocers whom they judge “mauvais”, “malades”, “bons à rien”, discovers in them kind people and workers Words: “never again would I believe as I had in my mother, father, and all the adult world” (I would never believe blindly my parents and the adult world) Atmosphere: Sensory memory, smells, gray days Issue: Allegory of experience Black Mountain: leaving parents, thinking for oneself
Retour d'une fête d'anniversaire vers Ou: Return of a birthday party to Outer Island: the transport boat explodes; Susan is badly burned, his brother dies. Atmosphere: Summer tragedy, permanent rocking Issue: First permanent meeting of the family with the harsh reality; adoption of two children
Dans sa tournée des anciens étudiants ne: In his tour of New York's former students, Rice stops at the shared home on the Hudson River; He left again, the situation being too precarious for him. Words: According to David Way: “Il a trouvé notre situation beaucoup trop précaire. Il n'y avait pas de gens riches pour le tirer d'affaire.” Atmosphere: Fun, misery of students faced with the founder's need for comfort. Issue: La social fall of the founder now begging the hospitality of his former students.
Albers écrit que l'art ne peut être anal: Albers writes that art cannot be analyzed to the end but that a clear head never hinders an authentic feeling; he insists on exercises of movement, parallelism (horizontal, vertical, oblique), equality (repetition of signs) and spatial illusions; purpose: “des yeux qui voient et des mains qui obéissent”.
Les nouveaux quartiers sont habitables m: The new neighbourhoods are habitable but barely: interior of the unfinished Studies Building, insulation of the nine existing buildings, transformation of the stone rotunda into a music building, baths into chemical laboratories, cottages into teachers' housing. 9 buildings to isolate Consequences: beginning of the crossing of the valley with the beautiful weather
Jour après jour, l'étudiant Derek Boving: Day after day, student Derek Bovington drives a tractor with a huge trailer between Lee Hall and Lake Eden: weaving looms, pianos, books, kitchen and laboratory equipment, personal affairs — and all the heating system of Lee Hall (radiators, pipes, bricks), to the great damn of the Blue Ridge Assembly. radiators, pipes, bricks carried away; a student will comment later: “not terribly high-minded”, while arguing that the system belonged to the college that had installed it at its own expense Consequences: strained relationships with the Blue Ridge Assembly; Bovington will die later in the war
Il quitte BMC après un an, l'argent cour: He leaves BMC after a year, money runs and “le monde appelait”. In retrospect (1977), he felt he had learned not skills but values: goodness, mutual respect, perfection of his art.
Étudiants et professeurs sillonnent le p: Students and professors travel across the country to find money. Evarts, California official, meets Henry Fonda (“a very good guy, he may even contribute a small amount”), Frederic March (“une très belle maison, pas trop voyante”), Herman Mankiewicz (“une sorte de malin, mais très cultivé et pas dupe”); Only Melvyn Douglas actually gives Hollywood money. only Hollywood money obtained: from Melvyn Douglas Consequences: funds so low at a time that all work could stop
Au moment où tout allait s'arrêter, Drei: By the time everything stopped, Dreier announced that an anonymous donation of $5,000 had arrived by post; the regularity of these “donateurs anonymes” at the appropriate time will make it suspect that it is Dreier itself, alternating with family contact or Forbes. 5000 dollars, anonymous Consequences: the site continues
Mary M. Atwater publie dans The Weaver (: Mary M. Atwater published in The Weaver (July-August 1941) a skeptical article entitled “It's Pretty—But Is It Art?” (It's pretty — but is it art?), critical of the work of Anni Albers. The Weaver 6, No. 3, p. 13-14
La rentrée est repoussée de deux semaine: La returned is delayed by two weeks to catch up with the project; Almost all students come back early to help. The college officially opens its new doors at the end of September, in half-finished buildings; by the cool autumn mornings, we eat lunch in coats. At the first general assembly, Albers, returning from a year of teaching at Harvard, gave a speech about the pride of having only eight years of existence in the face of three centuries of tradition. 2 weeks late; Breakfasts in coats Consequences: New Era of the College at Lake Eden
De retour d'un an à Harvard, Albers ouvr: De returns from one year to Harvard, Albers opens the first general assembly and delivers a speech comparing the three centuries of Harvard tradition to the eight years of college, claiming belief in conduct, expression, metaphor and manual type. Words : “We are finally on our own grounds” / “Life means change. Our aim is forward.” Atmosphere : exaltation, joy of accomplishment Issue : consecration of the new site and the educational creed
Obstacles en cascade (dont le faux calcu: Cascading obstacles (whose false calculation of drying and sawing in the oven of oaks felled at Asheville, while buying oak parquet from the timber merchant would have cost the same and was faster); The college suspends the academic calendar, everyone gets on the roof. Richard Carpenter, a young biologist terrified by heights, nails a whole day on the roof. oak parquet cut and then dried in the oven to Asheville; Small year later, Carpenter died of lung cancer at 31 years of age. tree placed at the highest point, wine and food in celebration, good child speech
Après Pearl Harbor, le collège, longtemp: After Pearl Harbor, the college, long cut off from politics, first reacts unbelievably: first radio brought to dinner since the Willkie campaign; five months after the war began, a student asked the faculty meeting to stop thinking BMC like “un monde en soi”. La Drain War men and money; survival depends on a government training program, but only two options (the Navy V-1, the Air Force Listed Reserve Corps) seem feasible, and the college has never been accredited. programs: Navy V-1, Air Force Listed Reserve Corps; national, regional or state accreditation problems Consequences: search for a training mission to survive
Pour tenir l'échéance auto-imposée de No: To meet the self-imposed Christmas deadline, the college suspends the courses; everyone climbs to the roof; Carpenter, a young, terrified high-rise biologist who just arrived, climbs and nails all day long. In the end, a small tree is raised to the highest point, wine and food are spread, talk good children. Atmosphere: ordinary heroism, exaltation of sacrifice, celebration at the top Issue: overcoming obstacles to ending the roof before Christmas — poignant forerunner: Carpenter will die of lung cancer a year later
Pour la première fois depuis la campagne: For the first time since the Willkie campaign (1940), someone brings a radio to dinner; A student notes her astonishment. Atmosphere: unbelief of a community that had deliberately cut itself off from the world Issue: the outside bursts into Lake Eden
Le collège écrit à divers collèges pour: The college writes to various colleges to obtain statements that they would treat students of Black Mountain as those of accredited schools; Antioch, Swarthmore, Reed and North Caroline University (chaired by Frank Graham) send affirmative letters. Consequences: Black Mountain gets quota in V-1 and Listed Reserve Corps programs
La faculté, ayant déjà donné sa main-d'œ: La faculty, having already given its workforce to build the site, decides not to draw any money beyond $10 per month and per person until the survival of the college appears assured; Some refuse positions elsewhere, including one to $10,000. $10/month per person; an offer denied to $10,000 Consequences: Dramatic savings for survival
Le collège contracte une seconde hypothè: The college contracts a second $18,000 mortgage (the first, of which $11,500 remains to be paid); New fund-raising campaign in the summer of 1942, where Albers, Kocher, Mangold and Dreier spend almost all summer, the rest of the community setting up friends and neighbours on a part-time basis. $18,000 + balance of $11,500; near maximum borrowing Consequences: Precarious survival
Privés de leur spécialiste mobilisé, le: Private with their mobilized specialist, the staff build “une baraque plutôt douteuse” hens; hens prefer trees to hens, lay very little, and end up eaten by college. Consequences: Fun failure of self-sufficiency
Fritz Hansgirg, chimiste réfugié, et sa: Fritz Hansgirg, a refugee chemist, and his wife arrived for the fall of 1942 in a cream Cadillac, followed by a Hammond Grand organ (installed in the dining room for community use) and a stunning collection of classic records. Cadillac cream; Hammond Grand; Classic discs Consequences: Bach evenings and cookies that enchant some and horrify the element “anti-gemütlichkeit”
Hansgirg et Straus inspectent un grand t: Hansgirg and Straus inspect a large 15 by 10 foot hole in the pasture, remains according to Hansgirg of a thirty-year-old gold search; large pieces of apparently pure mica lie around; the government needs mica as insulation, the Soviet and Indian supply being disrupted. 15 x 10 foot hole Consequences: Hansgirg offers experimental mining; faculty meeting splits with “dix-huit personnes bâtissant des châteaux en Espagne”
En deux jours, 250 livres de mica sont r: In two days, 250 pounds of mica are collected; The Colonial Mica Corporation of Asheville (government agency) sends inspectors who judge “bonne muscovite” samples; A full-time miner is hired to dig a well on the vein and galleries below. 250 pounds; “good muscovite” Consequences: Euphoria rising
Les Cohen, allemands passés dix ans dans: The Cohen, Germans spent ten years in English-speaking countries (especially Dartington Hall), and Bentley, 25, join the faculty Consequences: Form with Graaff then Foreman the suspected group of “collectivité”

Sam Brown, Moderator étudiant, organise: Sam Brown, Student Moderator, organizes a meeting on the teaching/learning process, but receives no response from students. La North Carolina Conference refuse le d: The North Carolina Conference denies the right to award diplomas: insufficient library books, guaranteed annual income and salary scales for teachers below the minimum required. Consequences: Seeking accreditation from other universities (Northwestern, Chicago, Swarthmore, Johns Hopkins, Antioch, UNC, Bard, Stanford, Reed), May-July 1942
BMC est refusée au droit de délivrer des: BMC is denied the right to issue degrees: insufficient library books, insufficient guaranteed annual income, teacher salary scale below the minimum required. Reported in letter from Wunsch to W. B. Alexander (President of Antioch), May 7, 1942 Consequences: Accreditation procedures at many universities
Le collège estime que son personnel de b: The College estimates that its office and kitchen staff earn 30 to 50% less than elsewhere; Two experienced secretaries and one accountant only receive $30 a month plus lodging and cover. $30/month, 30 to 50% under the market
Elaine occupe brièvement un emploi à ple: Elaine briefly occupies a full-time job at Liquidometer, painting the dials of aircraft instruments for the war effort, alongside Jackson Pollock; She shared her sandwiches, so he ended up bringing two Pollock sandwiches, then two; “they were good”
Pendant l'été 1942 à Harvard, Albers con: During the summer of 1942 at Harvard, Albers designed its Graphic Tectonic suite, zinc lithographs manipulating the line to create space and symbolism, as in To Monte Alban. Zinc lithograph; Graphic Tectonic: Ascension (1942), 173⁄4 x 81⁄2 in.
La famille est internée avec des millier: La family is interned with thousands of Japanese and Japanese-Americans: first at the Santa Anita racetrack, then at the Rohwer War Relocation Center in Arkansas. Asawa refuses victim status, participates in community life and meets artists informally.

Hayes est emprisonné et battu après avoi: Hayes is imprisoned and beaten after protesting when you ask your wife and daughter to leave the white zone of a shoe store
Au début des années 1940, des exercices: In the early 1940s, creative writing exercises appeared for the first time in the higher division exams, which marked the student's transition... (text cut)

Olson et Shahn travaillent ensemble pour: Olson and Shahn are working together to mobilize ethnic minorities for President Roosevelt's re-election in 1944.
Brochures du « Music, Art, and Work Inst: Brochures of the 1944 “Music, Art, and Work Institute” held at the Western Regional Archives of North Caroline (8 x 5 inches each). format 8 x 5 inches

Des professeurs présentent à Frank Facke: Professors present to Frank Fackenthal, acting president, a ten-point formal proposal creating the Seminars; Five points concern the recruitment and examination of students, and Seminars are authorized to issue academic credits; Proposal 6 provides for own publications (a seminar on slavery or crime, which will never exist). Ten proposals; Proposal 6 cited almost entirely Consequences: Against all expectations, the Seminars will gradually exclude students and will stop publishing, in favour of dialogue
Expulsé de l'université au bout de six m: Expelled from university after six months for refusing to dissect a frog in anatomy class; Shortly afterwards, called under the flags in the Navy. a frog, an anatomy course Consequences: incorporation into the Navy, basic training in Farragut, Idaho
Situé dans le Sud ségrégué, le collège a: Located in the segregated South, the college admits black students from 1944.
Gropius loue l'innovation pédagogique d': Gropius praises the educational innovation of Albers: it does not give students a fully-made system but objective tools to deepen the matter of life, changing approach “grosse de vie, présente et future”.
Le collège accueille une conférence très: The college hosts a highly publicized and internationally renowned conference celebrating Schoenberg's 75th anniversary — proof that Black Mountain was an outpost of experimental music in the 1930s-40s.
Fuller brevette une projection de la ter: Fuller patents a low deformation earth projection, foldable in several orientations and assembleable in three-dimensional globe shape; it presents it as a template for the display of information in networks (global energy comparisons, resources, unequal consumption between industrialized and underdeveloped nations) Project aimed at educational distribution in elementary schools; failure due to prohibitive costs Consequences: Instrument of his vision of the “Spaceship Earth”
Le cofondateur du purisme français peint: The co-founder of French purism painted during his stay an influential series of realistic paintings on Black Mountain
Albers crée un tissu de draperie en chen: Albers creates a chenille drapery fabric with white plastic chain and copper lurex, with thin stripes that sparkle at night and remain quiet and discreet during the day, for the Rockefeller Guest House. caterpillar, white plastic, Copper lurex
Vente de « The Metamorphosis of Mr. Crac: Sale of “The Metamorphosis of Mr. Cracovaner”; Following a first reading agreement for three years, the New Yorker was given a right of first refusal over all his short fiction. Consequences: Irregular income but literary recognition.
La famille Rice passe à quatre membres a: La family Rice grew to four members with the birth of Elisabeth in 1944. Consequences: La family lives “sur un lacet” with one or two new ones per year.
La family Rice increases to four members with the birth of Elisabeth. Consequences: Enlarged family, always precarious income.
Tôt dans le débat communautaire, les étu: Early in the community debate, students voted two to one to admit blacks in the following quarter (autumn 1944). Result 2 to 1. Consequences: The faculty is divided almost exactly into two on the same issue.
Pendant quatre mois, le débat public fai: For four months, the public debate rages mainly on the black issue; camps: for admission (Foreman, Bentley, Graaff, Cohen, Jalowetz, Radin); against (Straus, Anni and Josef Albers, Hansgirg, Kurtz, Wunsch, Gregory, Miller, then after hesitation Dreier and Lowinsky). Camp 'for': Foreman, Bentley, Graaff, Cohens, Jalowetzes, Radin. Camp 'against': Straus, Albers (Anni and Josef), Hansgirg, Kurtz, Wunsch, Gregory, Miller, Dreier and Lowinsky after hesitation. Consequences: Sustainable Community Division.
Série de réunions de faculté (25 janvier: Series of faculty meetings (25 January, 1, 15 February, 12, 17, 19, 24 April, 3, 10 May 1944) on the admission of black students; Foreman writes a summary of the discussions. Multiple Community Bulletins (March 22, 26 and April 3, 1944) Consequences: Decision to admit a black student
Gretel ouvre le salon, allume ; Eva entr: Gretel opens the living room, lights up; Eva enters, screams, jumps on the coffee table; Gretel removes the small green snake before it descends Atmosphere: Comic, Star Cree, night after concert

Quartet Kolisch repeats Schoenberg across the lake. Table ronde après dîner sur la danse dan: Round table after dinner on dance in history, summer storm rolling around the valley. De Mille, raised index, says that it was the Church that banned dance in worship — a thundering blow instantly slams: shiver, waste, laughter led by Mille itself. Words: by Mille: It was THE CHURCH that prohibited dancing in the Atmosphere rituals: summer storm heat, huge silence, theatrical lightning, collective hilarity — “les forces de la nature semblaient de concert avec la discussion” Issue: the sacred irritates in aesthetic debate
Après une bonne trempette dans la baigno: After a good dip in the cast iron tub on lion's legs laid on the bare floor, Sussler dresses for dinner; right below, every afternoon Sadoff repeats the double bass; Still in hot water, she imagines the solitaires vibrate with thick strings, ensuring that no unnecessary noise is made. Les deux pianistes s'installent aux pian: The two pianists set up at the grand pianos in the dining room for an evening of excerpts from Carmen; singing students sing on their accompaniment; The Habanera, carried away in improvised tempos and extravagant rubatos, rips the room. Pour son anniversaire, Hansgirg reçoit :: For his birthday, Hansgirg receives: Bach trio on piano, cello and violin; Champagne is served with macerated peaches one week in alcohol at 100 degrees — after one or two, on “flotte sur la pelune”; During the concert, two mice come out and dance. Marion appelle : « Viens voir ça ! » Cor: Marion calls: “Viens voir ça !” Coron short, follows his finger pointed towards ten yards under dwarf pines: a white flower with long hooded stems — the oconee-bell he has been looking for in vain for years. He's leaping in joy. Words: Marion: “Come here and see what this is!” (“Viens voir ce que c'est !”) Atmosphere: wonder, species lost and found in its own garden Issue: reward for three years of quest
En pleine nuit, une fille frappe à la po: In the middle of the night, a girl knocks at Coron's door: a comrade is on the verge of death. Après une forte pluie, sortant de Meadow: After a heavy rain, leaving Meadows Inn, Coron notes in the gravel washed a small arrow point of a beautiful shape; then they “sautent du sol” towards him, especially in the sloping corn field. Atmosphere: wet ground, revelation that changes a life Issue: birth of a vocation as a historian
De Creeft distribue les rôles de toréado: De Creeft distributes the roles of toreadors, picadors, etc. by deliberately mixing antagonists to play anger Atmosphere: Surface gaiety, tension intact Issue: Trying to exorcise hate by playing
Bentley reçoit une lettre d'ancien étudi: Bentley receives a letter from a former student at the camp, full of big words; he asks Fran to read it aloud without warning him; It flows obscenities in a neutral tone, students roar, the faces of the faculty fall; she twists herself without understanding; then it is explained to Wunsch Words: “my general said, 'What the fuck are you doin'?!”; Fran: “I don't think they believed it… It wasn't good for my reputation.” Atmosphere: Student laughter, teacher horror, humiliation of Fran Issue: Light Cruaty of Bentley; discredit that sticks to Graaff
Bal costumé surréaliste : Janey Stone av: Surrealistic costume ball: Janey Stone with inscription in the crotch, female-gerb “reap me”, oil cans in the breasts, Holy Trinity in overhang, Jeanne Wacker hula bare torso; Hansgirg in disguise; Albers in ironed tweed and paper cones on the eyes; Noting the other costumes, he blushes with anger and goes out, high heel, followed by other teachers Words: Bentley: “It got the desired rise out of everybody”; Registration “Abandon hope all ye who enter here” Atmosphere: Provocation, hilarity, scandal, furious release Issue: The climax of the 1944 Cultural War
Convoquée deux fois en trois semaines, e: Convened twice in three weeks, she confronts her judges: no concrete accusation; Only that she would be too tender with the students Words: Prepared statement: no criticism of her teaching, nor of her political or religious views, nor of misconduct — only the tenderness and defense of the students Atmosphere: Procedurier, light Kafkaian Issue: The absence of charges delegitimizes the exclusion
Deux réunions du Conseil où de Graaff te: Two meetings of the Council where Graaff is trying to obtain precise charges. With each charge, another member rejects it. Fran on the linen: 'At the salary I'm paid, I can't afford a cloth pretty enough to hang out.' Jalowetz, homme du milieu, malheureux de: Jalowetz, a man from the middle, unhappy with controversy, gave a speech at a meeting of the Council denouncing the logic of self-deaf. Words: Jalowetz: 'We are often told that a community must have a common idea, but what we are offered on all sides are more ideologies than ideas... I always feel like self-defeating in class, and I think self-defeating is only necessary when you're afraid of something.' Atmosphere: Sad, desperate, lucid Issue: Last voice of reason before definitive split
L'homme du milieu prend la parole : on r: The man in the middle speaks: one repeats that a community must have a common idea, but one has seen only ideologies flock; It has the impression of self-deaf, and self-deafs only serve those who are afraid Words: “plus d'idéologies que d'idées”; self-deaf impression Atmosphere: tiredness and lucidity of an old man Issue: the voice of wisdom crushed by the camps
Au premier soir de Peggy Bennett Cole, a: On the first night of Peggy Bennett Cole, after the meal, a central table sings the first verse of “Green Grow the Rushes, Ho!” and then silences and waits; another table responds with training, then a third takes over; so on until the song runs out; The new student listens astonished. À l'aube magnifique mais glacée de l'aut: At the magnificent but icy dawn of autumn, George hits the big triangle, first around 6am to wake up, then 6:30am to call breakfast; few students present themselves; among the faculty, Ted Dreier in blue from work time to time, Wunsch fairly regularly. Atmosphere: dawn cold, fresh and mysterious light, triangle cry
Un jour de pluie battante, alors que la: One day of beating rain, while the light remains dark, a handful of braves arrive dripping in their raincoats, “brillants et mouillés comme des grenouilles”; We stick to the corner tables near the kitchen and windows on the lake, chatting in a low voice, laughing and enjoying. Atmosphere: Richness, “chères et braves” kitchen lights, intimate adventurers
Ted Dreier frappe son verre d'eau avec u: Ted Dreier hits his glass of water with a table knife to impose silence during dinner and announces that Jalo and Lowinsky have prepared a musical evening; Salve with oh, ah and applause. Atmosphere: Joyful, shivering applause
Après un examen réussi, Albers refuse de: After a successful exam, Albers refuses to validate the student: she does not know whether the ceiling beams run along or across. Jalowetz, Cohen, Eric and Graaff exchange eyes and whisper: “Et toi, tu sais ?” None know. Words: They wonder by whispering if they themselves would know the answer — no. Atmosphere: Ironic stupor of arbitrariness. Issue: The authority of Albers considered absurd by his own colleagues.
À la fin de son premier séjour d'été, Gr: At the end of his first summer stay, Gropius praises the teaching of Albers: instead of a ready-made system, he gives objective tools to deepen the substance of life and develop independence and constructive ingenuity. Words: He would like to send any design or engineering student to the Albers courses. Atmosphere: Public tribute of the founder of Bauhaus to his former colleague. Issue: Recognition of Albers pedagogy by the world's highest design authority.
Ouverture de la session : Jalowetz, anci: Opening of the session: Jalowetz, former conductor exiled, delivers an opening speech pleading for the role of music in “la tâche stupéfiante de reconstruire notre monde ébranlé”, in tribute to Schoenberg for his 70th birthday. Words: Jalowetz: music must serve “la stupendous task of reconstructing our shaken world” Atmosphere: solemnity of exiles, music against tyranny Issue: making art a moral act in the face of Nazism
Albers fait placer des papiers colorés i: Albers places identical coloured papers on different backgrounds; students find that their perceptions diverge; Vibration exercises, color change, materials (ash from cigarette to rock). Words: Albers to Rauschenberg: one color is worth another; believing that a color would be better is only a personal preference Atmosphere: clinical discipline, perceptual astonishment Issue: shaking common sense and taste
Lors d'une visite, Gropius observe la pé: During a visit, Gropius observes Albers's pedagogy and publicly salutes it: abandoning all-featured systems in favour of objective tools. Words: “Il leur donne des outils objectifs pour creuser la matière même de la vie… approche toujours changeante, grosse de vie, présente et future.” Issue: Recognition of the master of Bauhaus for the student who became a teacher.
Alors que les tableaux de Kooning se cha: While Kooning's paintings take care of Picassian distortions, Graham comes to sit back to the paintings, unable to attend the creative struggle, but repeating to his friend his loyalty. Words: “Bill, whatever you're doing is good enough for me”; it cannot “stand someone struggling” Atmosphere: Malay, aesthetic misunderstanding Issue: Fidelity of a mentor who has become reactionary to art that he no longer understands
Stephen Duggar Jr. écrit à Foreman (20 j: Stephen Duggar Jr. wrote to Foreman (20 January 1944); Wunsch made its own consultations (letters to Junius Allison on April 12, June 27, July 17, 1944) and received the same legal response.

Orr resigns (26 April 1944), admitting that the admission of a black student has partly contributed to it, but also denounces BMC disease: “tenter trop avec trop peu”. Zora Hurston (21 février 1944) et Rubye: Zora Hurston (21 February 1944) and Rubye Lipsey (21 February 1944) write to Wunsch; James E. Letter from Wunsch to Effie Mae Drake, February 1, 1944
Début du printemps : Wunsch propose d'ad: Early Spring: Wunsch proposes to admit one to three carefully chosen Blacks, as simple visitors, for up to three to four weeks, at the music institute, preceded by a course on race relations for the entire community. 1 to 3 people, 3-4 weeks maximum, visitor status. Le compromis retient une seule femme noi: The compromise retains only one qualified and elderly black woman, admitted for the entire summer session with a hybrid status as a 'member of the Institute' — Bentley mocks him in speaking of the Hofjude ('the Jew of Court'). Straus states that it remains opposed but will not fight for its opinion. One person, status 'member of the Institute', neither visitor nor guest nor student. De Graaff porte plainte contre l'accusat: De Graaff files a complaint against the Straus corridor charge; Straus repeats and adds the abuse of 'democratic institutions'; Radin asks from when a teacher has the right to lose patience; Bentley enraged that he was accused of communism; Lowinsky spades Bentley; Hansgirg confounding repeats the accusation by believing to remove it; Radin defends itself with its own case; After several hours, twenty exhausted people leave the night without resolve. Hansgirg: 'we must not poison the minds of students with communist propaganda against religion, etc.' Atmosphere: Unbearable Tension, 'the atmosphere was so dense that breathing was painful' (Dreier) Issue: La community breaks apart on the border between belief and propaganda

L'ancien étudiant Jamieson arrive en vis: Former student Jamieson arrives on a visit with “aussi fêlées que jamais” ideas and tries to raise interest in nudist weekends; Wunsch enters such anger that he refuses to talk to him. Reported in the letter from Wunsch to Evarts of May 6, 1944.
Premier Institut d'art d'été (1944). Bla: First Summer Art Institute (1944). Blair arrives early one morning in June, dirty and tired after a night on the Southern Railway: seats taken at Washington, standing on the platform between cars in high heels across Virginia, soot from the coal locomotive, seat found after midnight in a car infested with cockroaches, two hours waiting in Salisbury. No one is waiting for him at the station except the Alberss coming to pick up a package; a woman on the train presents Blair in Anni, they load everything in their old car and climb the bumpy road — then leave with the suitcases still in the trunk. New high-heel clothing and footwear; gasgen rationed; missing axle on the driver side of the old break; eight bumpy miles to Lee Hall; two offices and a spring sofa bed without mattresses or chairs in the studio; icy shower; wet mist mattress; naked bulb; Wet red clay bank in front of open window Consequences: His unauthorized cabin move blurred the allocation of rooms; The following week he was given the task of putting them in order — a good experience of the democratic process.
Réunion-bilan censée apaiser ; le Studen: Meeting-balance sheet intended to appease; the Student Moderator proposes that majority voting should replace consensus when unanimity is impossible; furious querre on this point. Consequences: The elders confirm their conviction that the new ones do not understand the principles of the community.
Dreier accuse Radin de commérage, intrig: Dreier accuses Radin of gossip, intrigue, communist conspiracy and obsession to develop the brain rather than the entire student person; Radin, furious, announces that he will not return to autumn and leaves with his wife several days before the end of the term, without explanation to the officials. Start 'structulent' (Wunsch) several days before the end of the quarter. Consequences: Radin does not return in autumn 1944.
Le groupe Kolisch commence le travail su: The Kolisch group begins work on Schönberg's Op. 7 String Quartet; New summer students rush into the dark lobby of the North Lodge, sitting on chairs and stairs to watch. Randall Jr. Consequences: charge for “loitering”
Inculpées de « loitering » (politique de: Indicted by “loitering” (Southern euphemism policy for prostitution; according to Jeanne, a vice campaign with police quotas, linked to a nearby military base). Private telephone calls, locked for the night with dozens of women, black separated from white by steel plates. A 14-15 year old girl, obviously tuberculosis, spits blood on the ground; his older sister, then thrown into the cell, announced that she had won twenty dollars of soldiers and yelled at his youngest. A Tennessee teacher, arrested in a hotel room with a soldier (free of charge), believes her life was ruined. At midnight, Barbara celebrates its 21st anniversary; They read their books, sleeping a little crouched on the ground. segregation by steel plates; 20 dollars earned by the sister; coughing blood; anniversary of the 21 years of Barbara at midnight Consequences: forced medical examination the next morning
Jeanne doit crier sur un garde pour qu'i: Jeanne has to yell at a guard to keep his hands for him. They explain to the young doctor being a student at Black Mountain, returning from a visit to a professor in Fisk and from one night at the Highlander Folk School — instead of sympathy, outrage: in many Southern spirits, Black Mountain and Highlander are outposts of the red threat. The doctor is furious when they require to read the exam authorization before signing, blocking the line. Examination described as “quelque chose sorti de Faulkner”; He announces that Barbara is positive for gonorrhea. Sadistic examination; medication; 2nd negative Asheville review 5 days after Consequences: conviction aggravated by blennorrhagic report
Assises sur un banc pendant que le juge: Sitting on a bench while the judge ships fights and family disputes; They realize that no defendant, neither they nor prostitutes, has a lawyer. A journalist advises Jeanne: say “I want a lawyer” first; But before the judge, too shaken, they say nothing. The judge sees the report of blennorrhea, launches a long conference on the Scottsboro case and condemns them to sixty days of workhouse. A lawyer, apparently sent by the journalist, ran and promised to contact the college. 60 days of workhouse; Conference on Scottsboro; quiet and nice lawyer Consequences: transfer to county penitentiary
Un chef de la police redoutable, radio à: A fearsome police chief, a short-wave radio on California criminal news, asks them, among other things, what they think of blacks (Jeanne, “vraie lâche”, retreats to the Bible). Footprints: Jeanne weeps, the photographer must wait for her to dry her eyes. They can write letters, but censored: they write that they are “entre les mains d'amis du Dr Straus” to say “fascistes racistes” fraud. Shortwave radio; censored letters; “friends of Dr. Straus” code Consequences: Dreier alerted by lawyer
48 heures après l'incarcération, Dreier: 48 hours after incarceration, Dreier arrives in Chattanooga, calls the judge who reprimands him for unproperty and treats the girls of “couple de prostituées”. Le journal de Chattanooga publie un arti: Chattanooga's newspaper publishes a rather important article (because of the judge's lecture on Scottsboro) appointing Black Mountain College; someone sends it to Asheville Citizen, but the deputy editor, favorable to the college, calls Wunsch who explains everything and convinces him not to reproduce the article. Le jour du retour des filles, réunion sp: On the day of the girls' return, special meeting: the case rekindles sleeping antagonisms since the compromise on the admission of blacks. Fran's defense of Graaff (Andy did nothing dishonest) against Wunsch and Dreier (“protéger le collège”), Molly Gregory (if she remains she will be “héros ou martyre”, she will be “prenne les conséquences”), Anni Albers (Andy seems “frivole et amusée”, says it's “la meilleure expérience de sa vie”). The schoenbergian emigrants gathered at Black Mountain — with the Blue Ridge in place of the Alps — form the nucleus. Steuermann (pianist chosen by Schoenberg, New York) and Kolisch (violinist, founder of the Kolisch Quartet, on tour with the Pro Arte Quartet) are the most active; Krenek, exiled to the United States in 1938, gives a series of lectures including “Arnold Schoenberg at Seventy”. Ten weeks of seminars, conferences, rehearsals and concerts; Schoenberg, in poor health, declines invitation Consequences: Ephemeral revival of the Viennese Verein in North Caroline
Après une nuit de train éprouvante, pers: After a rough train night, no one at the station except the Alberss coming to pick up a package; bumpy journey, forgotten suitcases in the trunk; icy shower; In the evening, break without door up to Lee Hall, night climb to the cabins, tempered mattress, wild room change.
