Words: Wunsch: look with 'quiet eyes' the storm fell; the observer would have thought 'a matter of life or death, not a political point' Atmosphere: Extreme passion for a procedural issue Issue: The real power in the community: former guard against news
Claquement de portière feinté en colère,: Folded door slamming angry, truck leaking into dust, Jeanne brandishing its Randall, raised inches, police car growing in 4-5 tight planes, police questions (“Êtes-vous vierge ?”), Andy's answers of acidic modesty, mad laugh suffocated by Jeanne Words: “I don't think that's any of your business”; “Maybe your friend will. Are you a virgin?” — “Yes” (with perceptible acid) Atmosphere: summer dust, sun, girls' insolence in the face of police arrogance Issue: the shift of careless freedom towards the Southern prison gear
Atmosphère : sombre, carnivalesque et te: Atmosphere: dark, carnival and terrifying Issue: Civil majority in prison
Accusations de Straus, défense de de Gra: Straus charges, Graaff defense, Gregory logic, Anni Albers spade, Josef Albers's remark that makes everything go wrong, exclusion vote, Bray's announced departure Words: paraphrased: Albers — think she suffers in secret “crée un sérieux problème au collège”; Gregory — “elle sera héros ou martyre” Atmosphere: suffocating, moralizing, hidden stakes Issue: converting a minor incident into a major explosion
Foreman part travailler pour le CIO Comm: Foreman is going to work for the IOC Committee for Political Action to re-elect Roosevelt and a Democratic Congress, leaving the college in a 'very bad hole' (Dreier) because he had promised to raise funds during the summer; Bentley, demonstrating its commitment to integration, teaches Fisk for the summer. Consequences: Loss of a fundraiser for the summer.
Deux étudiantes vénétrant Bentley, sans: Two students came to Bentley, without heroes on campus and away from home, warning their Graaff advisor and heading north to Bentley at Fisk. Two 20-year-olds. Consequences: A week later, a Chattanooga lawyer called Dreier about them.
Dix membres de la faculté signent un com: Ten faculty members sign a laconic statement: they no longer trust it supports “ce genre d'éducation” that they believe. Dreier, in a remarkably vague letter to Clark Foreman, accuses him with Bentley of being responsible for an increasingly immature and irresponsible attitude of students, of “choyer” his protégés instead of making them grow. Fran refuses to resign: that we define the charges and formally request his resignation. 10 signatories; Letter to Clark Foreman during absence Consequences: three weeks of meetings of the Board of Fellows; Open split
Trois semaines de réunions du Board of F: Three weeks of meetings of the Board of Fellows; We try to hide the “querelle de famille” from the people of the summer institute who see Black Mountain as a garden of Eden — but both factions sit on either side of the dining room and walk on opposite sides of the road to avoid. De Creeft, a summer member loving people on both sides, has the idea of mediation (beyond the passage). 3 weeks; separate factions in the dining room and on the roads Consequences: impossible to hide; “exode ou purge” in progress
Lors de la réunion du 17 juillet 1944, d: At the meeting of July 17, 1944, Graaff suggested that many college students are not virgins; Hansgirg “manque de s'évanouir”. Story of Graaff (telephone interview of 10 December 1967).
De Graaff soutient avoir mis en garde le: De Graaff claims to have warned girls against auto-stopping; Andy and Jeanne, as long as they remember, confirm his version. Telephone interview of 10 December 1967; interview of 31 May 1967.
Dreier sirote son café, écoutant Jalo et: Dreier sips its coffee, listening to Jalo and Cohen describe the arrival of musicians; In the dark hall of the North Lodge, the full-bodied students watch the Kolisch Quartet work Schoenberg; Dreier finally smiles — the phone rings: a Chattanooga lawyer, about Anderson and Wacker; Dreier feels he should never have smiled. Atmosphere: Net broken musical euphoria; Unforeseeable 'phone call' Issue: The hope of rebirth by the institutes versus the legal crisis that is coming
Deux étudiantes reviennent d'Highlander: Two students return from Highlander and Fisk in auto-stop; gonorrhea rumor; Lowinsky and Anni Albers are indignant at the irresponsibility of Graaff; Hansgirg almost fainted; Faculty meetings on 10, 14 and 17 July; Dreier writes that even false advertising made an action inevitable. Words : Bentley : “she didn't have it . . . there wasn't any gonorrhea around Black Mountain” Atmosphere : Rumor, indignation, moral dizziness Issue : Reputation of a young woman against college reputation
Les joueurs travaillent le Quatuor op. 7: Players work the Schoenberg Quartet op. 7 in front of the audience; the partition scrolls on the suspended screen; disagreements over a sentence, discussions, true explanations, hard and focused work; gradually the order emerges from the nascent familiarity. Words: Wunsch to Evarts: “It was a privilege”; He talks about disagreements, real explanations, hard and concentrated work, a dramatic adventure where order arises from work. Atmosphere: Creative tension, concentration, intellectual adventure at the heart of summer Issue: La music as a model of democracy and cultural reconstruction in wartime
Diverses lettres de démission parviennen: Various resignation letters arrive at the Board, which responds pro formaly; Kurtz wrote on behalf of Board to Graaff on September 13, 1944, with a cheque of $1,000. $1,000. Consequences: Consumption of split.
Une déclaration signée datée du 13 août: A signed declaration dated 13 August; the Wunsch declaration of 15 August; letter from John Swackhamer to the College on August 21; Wunsch to Evarts on August 23, September 1, October 18; Evarts response on 25 September; Wunsch reports the reactions of Cohen and evokes Kurtz and Dreier, fatigue and depression (letter to Forbes dated December 7, 1944). Consequences: Exhaustion of Wunsch, which will eventually leave.
Dès la rentrée d'automne 1944, Lowinsky: As early as the fall of 1944, Lowinsky raised integration into a faculty meeting; nearly a year of debate followed (accreditation, local reaction; Student or teacher? how many, of what sex?). Straus and Kurtz oppose it. Lowinsky is commissioned for surveys, starting with Dr George Redd, a sociologist from Fisk University who has already visited, who opens it to the network of black colleges of the South. Straus, on research leave at Johns Hopkins, will never actually come back. Consequences: May 1945: formula stopped — two black students for summer institutes, then a black teacher in autumn “si des gens de calibre adéquat sont disponibles”
L'Institut de musique de 1944 réunit pre: The 1944 Music Institute brings together almost the entire circle of Schoenberg students and admirers in the United States; Schoenberg, over 70 years old and living in Los Angeles, feels unable to travel long and sends Jalowetz (“Jalo”) a warm personal greeting for the opening. letter from eight summer students to Wunsch, 14 Sept. 1944; financial estimates signed Frederic Cohen; speech by Lowinsky, 10 April 1956 Consequences: Great joy of Jalowetz
Janis le retient pour « Abstract and Sur: Janis retained him for “Abstract and Surrealist Art in America” and published the book of the same title.
Les partants préparent un nouveau collèg: The leavings prepare a new college: without a work program, focused on the arts, with “conseillers-fiduciaires”, and seeking to train politicians in particular (Wunsch to Forbes, December 7, 1944); Cohen tries “paqueter” a Music Institute (letters from Milton Rose to Dreier and Gordon Chalmers, President of Kenyon College, March 1945). Consequences: The project does not replace BMC.
Après la rétrospective Mondrian et l'exp: After the retrospective Mondrian and the exhibition Stuart Davis at the MoMA in 1945, intrigued by “l'énergie, l'agressivité et une sorte d'inévitabilité lyrique” of Davis's paintings, she goes back several times to take notes and writes a twenty-page essay, which was also typed double-sided, not intended for publication, to clarify her thinking; Bill and Denby rent him, Thomson is impressed; 12 years later she publishes it almost unchanged in ARTnews and receives a thank you note from Davis 20 pages, typed on both sides of the sheet
Après une critique hideuse dans Time, l': After a hideous review in Time, the St. Albans schoolboy goes down the hill to buy the book of Miller from Franz Bader. Publication of the book in 1944 Consequences : Beginning of the admiration of Williams for Miller
Venegas cesse d'enseigner le cours de co: Venegas ceased teaching the course of architectural composition conducted according to the classical Fine Arts model since the foundation of the School in 1894. Consequences: Opening to modernist reform.
Harriett Engelhardt, ancienne élève d'An: Harriett Engelhardt, former student of Anni at BMC, died in 1945 working for the Red Cross in Germany; Her mother suggests a foundation in her memory. Anni brings together a considerable collection of fabrics, especially from the Americas, exposed to BMC and used as teaching material. Consequences: Collection acquired later by Yale
Le collège accepte ses premiers étudiant: The college accepts its first black students, the first “biracial” institution in the southern United States; still symbolic gesture according to Lane, but early. Lane talks about “token gesture, but one made early” Consequences: A pioneering position in the segregated South
Pendant la session d'été 1945, Emma Hoff: During the summer session 1945, Emma Hoffmann painted in oil the daughter Africa Hayes and Mrs Hayes; the Hayes concert, a small voice of great emotional strength, retains an audience from all walks of life.
« Report from the Academy : The Experime: “Report from the Academy : The Experimental College”, Partisan Review vol. 12 n°3, 1945: after having heard Eliot advise young writers to avoid the academy (working for example in insurance, like Wallace Stevens), Bentley notes that most American poets transplanted are teachers; Disappointed by American higher education, he chose experimental reform. Theft. 12, no. 3, 1945 Consequences: Reflection on the function of the experimental college.
Dernières nouvelles : environ quarante é: Latest news: about forty students; a group of elders at New York are thinking about retrying experience elsewhere. about 40 students
La question de l'admission d'étudiants n: La question of admission of black students was not resolved positively until autumn 1945.
Préparation de fêtes : journée à l'ateli: Preparation of parties: day at the carpentry workshop to make improvised services — grapefruit plates, shallow circles turned in six-inch mahogany squares, delicate forks with three teeth, small butter knives in the wood of an old walnut, turned, sanded, oiled. six-inch mahogany squares; old walnut wood
Une déluge de montagne fait sortir le ru: A mountain flood brings the stream out of its bed; Lilly wakes up his daughter, a human chain forms to evacuate the cook and his family from their cabin, water to the knees. The water drops quickly, the cook's clothes are ruined, a collection is organized. Water to knees; destroyed clothing; donation collection Consequences: Collection to buy clothes from the cook
En se promenant avec les Bodky, Roland H: While walking with the Bodky, Roland Hayes finds a rattlesnake wrapped behind a tall tuft of grass, picks up a stone and kills it with a jet of deadly precision. The cook strip the snake and prepare it for the Erwin Bodky dinner. Stone launched; Snake stripped and cooked; “ça goûte le poulet”
Par une nuit de pleine lune qui inonde l: On a full moon night that floods the valley, a group walks through the dusty road to the waterfall and its slippery rocky basin; all bathe naked, the bravest under the fall, then dry while dancing before walking back at dawn, warmed by walking. Ice water, slashing teeth, “d'un blanc spectral” body, farm dogs barking away, back to dawn
Concerts festifs le samedi soir avec des: Festive concerts on Saturday evening with leading European and American artists in front of students, teachers and visitors of Asheville; Everyone gets dressed a little. Moments cited: Carol Brice in the Vier ernste Gesänge in Brahms; Bodky and Heinitz in the Sonata in the major for Beethoven's cello and piano, with total silence between the movements. Audience dressed; “on aurait entendu tomber une épingle” between movements
En quelques jours terribles, alors qu'il: In a terrible few days, while he is rector of the college, the homosexuality of Wunsch is revealed explosively. Consequences: His life ruined; the college's claim to an exceptional humanity seriously compromised.
Neuf nouveaux enseignants engagés à l'au: Nine new teachers hired in the fall of 1945, eight young, American, with children. Registration slightly increased to 60 students (only 25% boys). The college is officially accredited for the GI Bill in music, English, social sciences, mathematics and (if material improves) chemistry. Percy Baker, a black biologist from Virginia State College, hired as a simple “chargé de cours invité” for the fall of 1945 in accordance with “recrutement racial” policy. 60 students, 25% men; IM Bill Licensing Consequences: New Fellows Council Policy: First appointment is still on trial for one year and then renewals for one, two, three and five years.
Selon l'accord passé avec le Board of Fe: According to the agreement with the Board of Fellows, Wunsch waits an hour in the morning to come back and pick up his things, then leaves permanently before the community wakes up, without kissing or saying goodbye, in his little roadster. However, he was only the previous day the full leader of the college. 1 a.m.; “those little feet go back and forth” carrying books; the same small roadster as usual Consequences: Definitive removal of Wunsch from college life
Molly Gregory, officier le plus gradé ap: Molly Gregory, the most senior officer after the departure of Dreier on vacation at George Lake, braves the prohibition of the ability to disclose the case: she brings the whole community together and Herbert Miller tells the truth about the arrest, presenting the departure as a fait accompli. No protest from students or seniors about the fact or manner of departure. Dreier Vacation at George Lake Consequences: Official false version then released
Communiqué officiel : après des années d: Official statement: After years of non-vacation work, Wunsch suffered a mild nervous depression and felt it was good to resign to take a necessary rest. formula “slight nervous breakdown” Consequences: Dissimulation of arrest for homosexuality
Wunsch rentre d'abord en Louisiane, mala: Wunsch first returns to Louisiana, sick several months of an “mauvaise infection de la mâchoire”; He was cured, joined California in a roadster and literally disappeared: letters without answer, visits rejected — not out of anger against Black Mountain but out of feeling that he had got what he deserved: punishment and anonymity. Only rumor: office worker in a post office. roadster; jaw infection; supposed postal clerk work Consequences: Voluntary destruction of Wunsch
Enseignant à l'Université du Maryland et: As a teacher at the University of Maryland and completing his Harvard PhD in Psychology, Wallen first followed his CV by the Harvard Appointment Bureau, then, after two days of reflection on the traditionalism of the procedure, wrote a personal letter stating that the CV would never say who he was. 27 years two years of teaching in Maryland; woman and baby Consequences: Letter-manifest that will seduce the college
Straus, en congé à Johns Hopkins, trouve: Straus, on leave at Johns Hopkins, finds first in the letter “beaucoup de banalités présentées bruyamment” and expects the worst; he meets Wallen, is pleasantly surprised, the authentic judge, stubborn in discussion, then after a second visit to the home of the Wallen, strongly recommends hiring. modern apartment “sans fanatisme” : prints of Frans Hals and Van Gogh plus a Picasso ; “sa voix parlée semble un ténor mais il chante deuxième basse” Consequences: Definitive positive recommendation
Les Wallen séduisent d'emblée la communa: The Wallen immediately seduce the community, except “deux des membres les plus vocaux de la faculté” (Wallen suspects Albers, which “n'aime pas la psychologie”) who seize a rumor of Allport's letter — army reform for “instabilité nerveuse” — to postpone the appointment; The rumor is checked with the army, deemed false, and Wallen receives a one-year contract. “instabilité nerveuse” rumor; One-year contract Consequences: Arrival of Wallen in autumn 1945
Wallen, 28 ans, formé à Harvard, est eng: Wallen, 28, trained at Harvard, is engaged to teach psychology; His idealism translates into a desire to impose more order on the college, which deeply irritates Albers. Wallen is 28 years old in 1946, graduated from Harvard Consequences: Main Source of 1946 Frictions
Vers le milieu des années 1940, tout obj: In the mid-1940s, any unusual object was labelled “matiére”: an inescapable dinner, mouldy remains, a pile of garbage, a cow's dung. The students laugh at it, some laugh nicely. “You name it, and I'll make a matiére out of it” Consequences: New habit of responding to everything in visual terms
Au milieu des années 1940, Albers inaugu: In the mid-1940s, Albers inaugurated an independent basic painting course, which he then brought to Yale. Consequences: The course aims to figure-ground, application of marks to articulate volume in space, interaction of colors.
L'ancien peintre en résidence du Bauhaus: The former painter in residence of the Bauhaus teaches an advanced course in the summer of 1945.
Bill Levi, diplômé de l'Université de Ch: Bill Levi, a graduate of the University of Chicago where he taught philosophy, joined the faculty among several new professors during a modest post-war expansion. La law GI Bill inflates student staff Consequences: Its relationship with Albers will be stormy (“prickly”)
Dans une interview, Albers défend sa sér: In an interview, Albers defends its Graphic Tectonic series executed in zinc-lithography: compositions constructed of elements produced preferably by mechanical means, combined in a mechanically accentuated order Very clean lines, uniformly modulated, clear demarcation between black and white
Albers approche Ansel Adams pour un cour: Albers approaches Ansel Adams for a summer course in 1945 and asks him if he thinks Edward Weston would be interested; Adams declines but offers Brett Weston and Paul Strand instead
Petit bâtiment de verre, béton et bois a: Small glass, concrete and wood building with two inclined glass walls for excellent acoustics, intended for musical practice and study. High glazed walls reflecting the surrounding woods, integration with nature Consequences: Reprised by California Arts and Architecture in April 1949 in photo-essay “Minimum House: A Student Project”
Johnson, informé du collège par Elaine S: Johnson, informed of the college by Elaine Schmitt Urbain during a summer school at the Art Institute of Chicago, is accepted with her for the summer 1945 Consequences: Beginning of a decisive training until 1948
Récital du ténor afro-américain dans le: African-American tenor recital in the Summer Music Institute, in front of the largest audience ever gathered at the college; program mixing classic tunes and black songs, applauded as one of the greatest moments in the history of the college about 400 spectators including 30 to 40 African-Americans, public overflowing on the veranda; program: operas by Monteverdi, Haydn, Mozart, Schubert, then Negro Spirituals and Creole and Afro-Brazilian songs; evening described as soft (“balmy”) Consequences: Lack of hostile reaction reassures the college and accelerates recruitment of black students and teachers
Alma Stone Williams avait été invitée au: Alma Stone Williams was invited to the Summer Music Institute in 1944; Sylvesta Martin becomes the first full-time black student in the spring of 1945, and Percy H. Baker the first full-time black teacher in the fall Consequences: the first white university in the South to admit a black student, a decade before Brown v. Board of Education
Wunsch est arrêté pour de prétendus « cr: Wunsch is arrested for alleged “crimes contre nature” and then leaves College Consequences: loss of one of the main supporters of integration
En 1945, le recteur du collège est chass: In 1945, the rector of the college was expelled following a case (adultery, truncated note). In the 1940s, discouraged members of promiscuity, homosexuals pushed to remain discreet; in the 1950s, sexual freedom became almost an argument of sale, homosexuality and extramarital relations more or less openly recognized — without sexism disappearing.
Après la guerre, le collège abandonne le: After the war, the college abandoned the rejection of “expression de l'émotion” in favour of a new appreciation of creative writing as an expression of self: the progressive educator was replaced by a poet, M.C. Richards, and the students were conceived as writers alongside the new creative writing teachers. Consequences: Changing the pedagogy from writing to college.
Près d'achever son diplôme, Asawa appren: Nearly completing her degree, Asawa learns that she will not be able to complete the internship required to graduate due to her race. Her friend Elaine Schmitt convinced her to join her in North Caroline for the Summer Institute of Black Mountain in 1946. Consequences: Asawa joined BMC in the summer of 1946; She draws tirelessly, flourishes in the courses of Albers (matter studies, exploration of the line in her notebooks).
Paul Beidler, ancien élève de Frank Lloy: Paul Beidler, a former student of Frank Lloyd Wright, replaced Kocher in 1945 and designed and supervised shortly after the construction of a music studio. Consequences: Continuity of modern architecture in college after Kocher
Démobilisé, rentre à Port Arthur et déco: Demobilized, returned to Port Arthur and discovered that his family had moved to Lafayette in the meantime.
Stationné à San Diego dans la Navy, Raus: Stationed in San Diego in the Navy, Rauschenberg visits the Huntington Library and discovers for the first time original oil paintings, including Gainsborough's The Blue Boy, which he knew only by books and playing cards. The Blue Boy (ca. 1770) seen so far on playing cards; He says: “It was a total overdose”; “Oh my God, these are not cards!” Consequences: He realizes that you can be an artist; His entire career will come from the link between reproduced photographic image and original painted.
Après sa libération honorable de la Navy: After his honourable release from the Navy in 1945, he returned to Port Arthur but his family moved without warning to Lafayette, Louisiana, with his sister Janet (born April 23, 1936). non-announced move to Lafayette, Louisiana Consequences: he leaves to work in Los Angeles
Rauschenberg sert comme « technicien neu: Rauschenberg serves as “technicien neuropsychiatrique” in hospital rooms; It draws a lasting conviction on the tenuous border between mental health and madness. His memory is “j'ai appris à quel point la différence est faible entre santé mentale et folie, et qu'une combinaison des deux est essentielle”. Consequences: The author draws this experience closer to that of Breton Nurse at Saint-Dizier in 1916 — a parallel never studied.
Péret attaque les poètes de la Résistanc: Péret attacks the poets of the Resistance: their “honneur” would be to stop being poets to become agents of publicity — fidelity to anticlericalism and the surrealist refusal of patriotic committed art. Formula cited: “tout bien pesé, l'honneur de ces “poètes” consiste à cesser d'être poètes pour devenir des agents de publicité”
La fin de la guerre est célébrée avec jo: La end of the war is celebrated with joy by many Europeans, faculty and American students. Consequences: Theodore Rondthaler obtains college approval for the benefits of the GI Bill.
Pendant la guerre arrivent Frederic Cohe: During the war, Frederic Cohen (co-founder of Jooss Ballet with Kurt Jooss) and his wife Elsa Kahl (dancer), Edward Lowinsky (musicologist), Max Wilhelm Dehn (geometry in Frankfurt), Eric Bentley (history and theatre), Molly Gregory (wood, graduated from Bennington's first promotion). After the war: John Wallen (psychology), M.C. Richards (reading and writing), Bill Levi (philosophy and social sciences), Natasha Goldowski (corrosion), Charlotte Schlesinger (composer and pianist), Trude Guermonprez (textile design, daughter of the Jalowetz), Franziska Mayer (teacher, niece of Max and Toni Dehn).
Motherwell, qui ne pouvait pas s'offrir: Motherwell, which could not afford another summer destination, teaches Black Mountain; among his students: Rauschenberg, Cy Twombly, Francine Gray. He remembers the baseball games on Sunday. Baseball on Sundays
Les Feininger décrivent leur impression: The Feiningers describe their impression of the site: high in the mountains, at the edge of a small lake in a wide valley, surrounded by wooded chains; magical mornings with vapors rising from the lake and mist slowly revealing the contours of trees and mountains. “the very element of light appearing as something mysterious and new”
Goodman note en bas de page que la phras: Goodman notes at the bottom that the sentence on conscientious objectors as 'the most beautiful types of people in prisons' is quoted from a private remark by the director of the Danbury Penitentiary dated 1945. Note 17: 'This sentence is quoted from a private comment by the director of the Danbury Penitentiary (1945)'.
Note de bas de page : une phrase du poèm: Footnote: A sentence in the poem comes from a private comment by the director of the Danbury Penitentiary in 1945 (his friends do not disapprove of the law and judges, only prisons). “My friends don't disapprove of the law and the judges, only the jails”
Le collège bénéficie d'une cohorte de vé: The college benefits from a cohort of talented veterans paid by the GI Bill — almost unconditional cash payments for tuition and living expenses — to attend this non-accredited, art-based college. Consequences: Creative years from post-war to college
Publie « Constructing Textiles » dans le: Publish “Constructing Textiles” in the newsletter of the Summer Art Institute of the College, taken from Design in April 1946
Rice réalise son vieux rêve de revenir e: Rice realizes its old dream of returning to Caroline from the native South. George Grice, president of the College of Charleston and an old acquaintance with academic lectures, finds him an old country house with low rent, available for one year during the absence of the owners. Large fireplaces, wide verandas; a working and interesting black family further on the road Consequences: Rice feels in its element.
Bob Wunsch quitta brusquement Black Moun: Bob Wunsch suddenly left Black Mountain after being arrested at Asheville for homosexual acts with a marine. Josef Albers was elected rector of the college shortly after. Consequences: Albers becomes rector.
Après la décommission de son dernier nav: After the decommission of his last ship in San Francisco, Paul Jobs bets a friend he will find a woman in two weeks; He married Clara Hagopian, a Turkish refugee Armenian family, raised in New Jersey. bet: two weeks
Excitée par l'exposition Stuart Davis au: Excited by the Stuart Davis exhibition at MoMA, before ever publishing on art, Elaine wrote for a month to clarify the works in her mind, and completed a ten-page article that she placed in Edwin Denby's mailbox. The next day, telegram of one word: “Magnificent”. She puts the article away without looking at it for about twelve years, until the Davis retrospective at the Walker Art Center in Minneapolis, when Thomas B. Hess asks her to update it. Ten-page article; telegram of a word: “Magnificent”; about 12 years of oblivion; published under title “Stuart Davis: True to Life” (1957); The artist's fan letter. Consequences: The revised article becomes “Stuart Davis: True to Life”, included in the collection.
Breton écrit qu'ici est un art entièreme: Breton writes that here is an entirely new art, the culmination of twenty years of patient and rough development of Gorky; Gorky's first admirers consider him a newcomer. Breton quote in 1945. Consequences: Breton among the first to give a fair printed assessment of Gorky.
Julien Levy devient son marchand ; les s: Julien Levy became his merchant; The surrealists, by the person of André Breton, formally acknowledge this — a fact of which he draws great satisfaction.
Après six mois de planification, Foreman: After six months of planning, Foreman (“très bouleversé et honteux”, according to Fran de Graaff) announced one evening that he would become secretary of the National Citizens Political Action Committee. Rude blow for the Cohen, without any money. 6 months of preparation Consequences: Fritz tries in vain to sell its Music Institute to other schools; the Cohen live in the “misère terrible” (Barbara Anderson) until he hires at the head of the Opera Workshop of Juilliard
Après le déjeuner, Kazin s'assoit seul e: After lunch, Kazin sits alone at the top of the steps and plays the final of Act II of the Wedding of Figaro, every day, eyes closed, face in the sun. The witness slides through the back of Round House every day to observe; first incomprehension, then wonder, then listen: sextet becomes the first music he really hears. Atmosphere: sunny and peaceful interlude, sounds of mixed voices drifting from the still lake, total concentration of Kazin Issue: secret birth of a musical perception; education through stealth observation
Les peintures alignées contre le mur ; A: Paintings aligned against the wall; Albers, wand in hand, designates a painting and questions with theatricality; the audience shouts YES or NO in chorus. Words: “Does this have color?” — “YES!” or “NO!” screams Atmosphere: Choir fervor, Albers dramatism, whole body learning. Issue: Make it feel that color is relation, not liveliness.
Angie, accroupie entre les plants, hébét: Angie, squatting between the plants, beheaded by the warm sun, suddenly sees a pair of snow-white sneakers on the red ground; his look goes up the net fold of the re-ed jeans to the white shirt and wide smile; Andy's running. Words: Introduction of Andy, Fellow New Englander. Atmosphere: Incredible heat, red dust, love lightning. Issue: The birth of a friendship that will survive in college.
Dé lugage nocturne ; Lilly secoue Angie: Night lug; Lilly shakes Angie: “le ruisseau a débordé”; All come out; a human chain forms in the water to the knees to evacuate the cook and his family; the water drops rapidly; The clothes are lost, a collection follows. Words: “The creek is over its banks” — “le ruisseau a débordé”. Atmosphere: Night emergency, water to knees, quick relief. Issue: Community solidarity in the face of the elements.
Pleine lune puissante qui floodlit la va: Full powerful moon that flooded the valley; energy such that one cannot sleep; walking by the dusty road, shadows carried, farm dogs on alert; at the cascade, “on va se baigner nus!”; Joyful splashes, icy water, braves under the fall, spectral white bodies; You slam your teeth, you dry up, you dress up in a hurry, you walk miles and warm up, back at dawn. Words: “Let's go skinnnydipping!” — “On va se baigner tout nus!” Atmosphere: Silver moon, icy and graying water, laughter, total freedom. Issue: The abandonment of inhibitions in a paradise setting.
Marche tranquille ; seul Hayes a vu le c: Quiet walk; only Hayes saw the rattlesnake wrapped behind a tall tuft of grass; he picks up a stone without a word and kills it with a jet of mortal precision; the cook stripes the snake and the kitchen for the dinner of Bodky. Words: “Tastes like chicken” — “ça goûte le poulet”. Atmosphere: Calm broken by the safe and fast gesture of the singer. Issue: The exercised eye of the legendary black artist, protector of his friends.
Chaque soir, écoute des nouvelles entour: Every evening, listen to news surrounded by Europeans whose relatives are in danger; At the table, three quarters of the guests slide without realizing it in French or German. Atmosphere: European charm, the anguish of war in the deaf. Issue: The college as an island of Europe at war in the American Arctic.
Arrivé, Weitzer néglige de réserver un m: Arrived, Weitzer neglects to reserve furniture; There's only one bar chair left squeaking. He asks around him: no one sympathizes. We send him back to the woodshop. He discovers independents who transmit their ethics to him; He designs his sandwich table and hangs it on the ceiling for lack of legs. Words: “Pourquoi ne pas monter à l'atelier et fabriquer quelque chose ?”; the ethics of the workshop: invent, be creative, do not copy, do not disturb me Atmosphere: total lack of compassion, but positive atmosphere; solitary pride in the object unique to the world; “chaude poussée de créativité” despite the screws that hang the legs and the hammock swinging Issue: the initiation of a novice to creative self-sufficiency
Des étudiants hostiles présentent une co: Hostile students present a cow dung construction among anonymous works; Albers goes down the row, rents balls resembling fish eggs, then reaches the dung : “si réelle qu'on veut la prendre et la sentir pour être sûr” — he smells it, and is sure of it. Without claping, he rests it, skips his usual comment on color and shape, and continues. Words: “Ah, une bonne escroquerie : des billes à l'aspect d'œufs de poisson... et celle-ci ? Merveilleux — on dirait une vraie bouse boueuse ! Si réel qu'on veut la sentir pour être sûr...” Atmosphere: tension, silent provocation of students; Albers' cold-blooded unnerving Issue: Who will give in: the master or mutins?
Wunsch, libéré de prison, attend une heu: Wunsch, released from prison, waits an hour in the morning, comes back looking for his things while the college sleeps; Molly, awake, listens to her little steps go back and forth with the books; it suppresses the desire to come down and help him because he has been forbidden; He leaves before dawn forever, in his little roadster. Molly, responsable après le départ de Dr: Molly, responsible after Dreier's departure, summons the whole community despite the faculty ban; Miller tells the truth about the arrest and presents the departure as a fait accompli; none protested, neither students nor elders, although some were attached to him. Straus, méfiant, rencontre Wallen à Balt: Straus, suspicious, meets Wallen in Baltimore and is pleasantly surprised; second visit to the couple's home: charming woman, measured prints; he wrote a flattering portrait and recommended the appointment. Words: Wallen “genuine”, does not speak “comme un livre imprimé”; “voix de ténor, chante deuxième basse ; une surface douce et gentille sur un fond solide”. Tenté par remplacer Carl Rogers à l'USO: Trying to replace Carl Rogers at the USO — career and income doped, but living at New York, little time to write and for the family — Wallen declines and accepts Black Mountain, seeing there a greater learning experience for him and his wife. Words: Wallen wants to check if an increased understanding of the dynamics of human behavior “a un rapport avec l'efficacité des processus démocratiques” Atmosphere: Internal weighing between ambition and ideal Issue: The arrival of the man who will subject the community to psychological examination
Un soir d'été, le ténor à la voix usée c: One summer evening, the tenor with a worn-out voice sings Monteverdi, Haydn, Mozart, Schubert, followed by spirituals and Creole and Afro-Brazilian songs, in front of a black and white audience that overflows on the veranda. Words: the audience will say the concert “beautiful beyond words” (of a beauty to exceed the words) and “un des plus grands moments de l'histoire de Black Mountain” Atmosphere: warm evening, full room, silent audacity of a racially mixed audience in the segregated South.
Le jeune technicien neuropsychiatrique t: The young neuropsychiatric technician works daily among the mentally ill. Words : “J'ai appris à quel point la différence est minime entre santé mentale et folie, et qu'une combinaison des deux est essentielle.” Atmosphere : Flash-back material : the rooms, the proximity of madness, before the BMC. Issue: Founded the artist's report to the irrational, echoing the Breton Nurse of Saint-Dizier (1916).
Après un mois de travail, Elaine glisse: After a month of work, Elaine slides its first art article — ten pages on Stuart Davis — into Denby's mailbox. The next day comes a telegram of one word. Words: Telegram: “Magnificent”. Atmosphere: Excitation of the first critical work, silence of the next day, then the brilliance of a unique word. Issue: Birth of a critical vocation; she puts the article away, mission accomplished.
Après six mois de planification du nouve: After six months of planning the new college, Foreman, “très bouleversé et honteux”, announces that he becomes secretary of the National Citizens Political Action Committee Atmosphere: painful confession, hard blow for the Cohen without money Issue: the collapse of the rebel dream
Ancien étudiant devenu instructeur d'arc: A former student who became an architectural instructor, Beidler was appointed in February 1945 as an instructor and consulting architect; He designed the Music Cubicle, built the following summer. Consequences: Departure of Beidler after the summer of 1945 to found its firm; project of cubicles scattered on the abandoned campus
Vue d'installation de l'exposition de fi: Installation view of the Jane Slater graduation exhibition in March 1945, photographed for college documentation.
Dreier suggère, sans preuve et sans que: Dreier suggests, without evidence and without this view being considered at the time, that the sailor was a provocative agent: Wunsch's reputation for “nègreophile” infuriated the local police and judicial community, who knew his homosexuality since an incident at the University of North Caroline; They would have set him up. Consequences: Stay at the stage of shared suspicion, without proof.
Wunsch avait toujours tout fait pour cac: Wunsch had always done everything to hide his homosexuality: never any advances, never confidence; We thought he was “psychologiquement un peu neutre — aucun appétit sexuel”. Staff say they are shocked; Three or four members profess indignation (“Comment a-t-il pu nous faire ça ?!”), a sign that the institution's reputation begins to prevail over the well-being of individuals.
Wunsch démissionne immédiatement, sans q: Wunsch resigns immediately, without anyone holding him back. The college, warned by its lawyer not to pay any official payments, buys its library to pass on $700 — initially contested solution (Dreier to Stephen Forbes: paying more would look like an official absolution). In accordance with the agreement with the Fellows Council, Wunsch only returns to pick up its business at one o'clock in the morning and leaves before the community wakes up. Molly Gregory, awake, hears “ces petits pieds aller et venir, aller et venir, portant des livres” and regrets not having come down to help her — “on m'avait dit que je ne devais pas”. Dreier went on vacation to George Lake, Molly, the oldest officer, challenged the ban on telling the truth to students: Herbert Miller informs the community, departure presented as a fait accompli. La official version invokes overwork without vacation. 700 dollars, library purchased, 1 hour in the morning, lake George
Exposé comme homosexuel, Wunsch est forc: Exposed as homosexual, Wunsch is forced to leave secretly and shamefully the college, an illustration of the current code of silence. Consequences: Example at Duberman (p. 225-27) of how this code works
Libéré de prison, Wunsch respecte l'acco: Freed from prison, Wunsch respects the agreement: he waits an hour in the morning to pick up his things and leaves before the community wakes up. Molly, awake in his room, hears his small steps “aller et venir, aller et venir, portant des livres”; he was forbidden to intervene; She resists the impulse to come down and will regret it all her life. Words: He was told: “il ne voudrait voir personne”; “on m'avait dit que je ne devais pas”. Atmosphere: Night, not felt, shame and modesty, indiscreet compassion of a woman nailed to bed. Issue: La collective cowardice disguised in regard; an individual consciousness that does not forgive itself for killing itself.
Carol Brice, début de carrière, venue av: Carol Brice, beginning of career, coming with her mother and baby, remains four weeks; the day of his last concert comes Roland Hayes with woman and daughter. Having never heard Brice, he is so conquered that at an evening at the Lowinsky he sings his own unprecedented arrangements of black spirituals and promises to send him copies. Hayes, a magical storyteller and charming man, stays for two weeks, talks about hours during his black man experience and black music. Fees and scholarships covered by the Julius Rosenwald Fund. stay of 4 weeks (Brice) and 2 weeks (Hayes); funding Julius Rosenwald Fund Consequences: huge impact on the community
La plus grande foule jamais vue au collè: La the largest crowd ever seen in college — 400 people including 30 to 40 Blacks — arrives for Hayes; Lowinsky briefed the openers: extreme courtesy, “où vous voudrez” answer to the seat question. Integrated spaces, no incidents; At the reception, a White whispers: “les temps ont changé”. Lowinsky silenced the fear of Klan. Words: “Où devons-nous nous asseoir ? — Où vous voudrez.”; “Times have changed, haven't they?” Atmosphere: controlled tension and then silent triumph Issue: the integration tested in front of the North Caroline; risk bet
Le jour du dernier concert de Brice, arr: The day of the last Brice concert, arrival of Hayes with woman and girl; having never heard Brice, he is conquered; in the evening, he sings his own unprecedented arrangements of black spirituals and promises the copies for his Atmosphere concerts: transmission between generations of black singers, intimacy of an evening Issue: the relay passage between the end and the beginning of a career
Mme Straus apporte la nouvelle de l'entr: Mrs Straus brings the news of the USSR's entry into war against Japan, shortly after the arrival of Martin.

Nina connaît un succès presque sensation: Nina was almost a sensational success in the Fourth Brandebourgeois Concerto; the next day she goes on a picnic with partners of the concert. Picnic in a pasture or on a top
Devant un paysage avec route, Mme Charea: In front of a landscape with road, Madame Chareau talks about the “tendresse des poteaux télégraphiques”; it notes the “combinaison de pauvreté et de luxe” of the place. John Reiss shows objective and non-objective paintings that give Martin its first spontaneous pleasure in front of BMC student work. Ground meals (hard eggs, salads, fruit, milk, cheese) due to lack of chairs
Au repas, Kauder lance que les mouvement: At lunch, Kauder launches that movements born of a disintegration world become absurd transposed into healthy America; the most absurd being that the Europeans themselves come to imitate it; Martin dreamed that Dada, a farce of 1918, was now taught as an art of masters. Words: Note of Kauder between an omelette and honeybread. Atmosphere: Irony at the table, friction Europe/America. Issue: What do exiles really transmit?
Calme matinal ; on entend Straus travail: Morning calm; we hear Straus working the violin; Three small clouds drift over three small hills. Atmosphere: Silence, acoustic fog of the violin, serenity.
Hayes, voix déclinante, construit son ré: Hayes, a declining voice, builds its recital by rhythm: calculated breaks carry the listener to the end. Words: Lowinsky: “le mouvement est ponctué par la pause”. Atmosphere: Rhythmic fascination.
À l'automne 1945, Elaine embarque impuls: In the fall of 1945, Elaine embarked impulsively with Bill Hardy, an engineering student attending the arts, to visit Edwin Denby who spent his summers in Provincetown; the storm shakes the boat, it wakes up on the floor running from the cabin; She claims the platonic episode but apparently only returns in early December, which puts Bill in fury according to Elaine, Hardy had never sailed and was “a pain in the neck”; Bill's biographers describe him as an experienced sailor (contest) Consequences: marital crisis
Sylvesta Martin, issue du Music Institut: Sylvesta Martin, from the Music Institute, became the first full-time black student; The Dr Percy H. Baker of Virginia State College is engaged as “lecturer invité” to teach biology in the fall of 1945. Julius Rosenwald Fund pays its $700 salary. In protest, R. R. Williams, a lawyer from the college at Asheville and member of the Advisory Board, resigned: he did not want to belong to an institution contrary to “l'opinion publique éclairée de Caroline du Nord”. $ 700 paid by Rosenwald Fund
Départ impulsif en voilier ; la tempête: Impulsive sailing departure; the storm shakes the boat at night; Elaine wakes up on the leaking floor of the cabin; she discovers that Hardy has never sailed Words: she will call it “pain in the neck” Atmosphere: night, water entering, sea sickness Issue: run away that hurts Bill and ends only in December
Malgré les fissures du mariage, la façad: Despite the cracks of the wedding, the façade of happiness is kept in the mail: the letter of November to his father contains a print of kiss with lipstick of Elaine and photos of each imprint of lipstick, photos of both spouses
Le studio que Bill avait amoureusement r: The studio that Bill had lovingly renovated is withdrawn from them after months of unpaid rent and the sale of the building; Bill and Conrad carry all their possessions in their hands on more than twenty blocks up to the new linoleum apartment rolled in balance on the shoulders of the two men; new rent: $18 a month, five floors without elevator Consequences: installation in a cold two-room without heating in Carmine Street
Tiny cold-water flat sans chauffage : po: Tiny cold-water flat without heating: dangerous oil stove to clean often for fear that soot will catch fire; they paint in the opposite corners of a room of 10 by 15 feet; Elaine notes that “cold-water” is an inappropriate term because only water was hot oil stove; 10x15 foot piece; rent $18/month Consequences: minor irritations (Bill whistles of classic themes) are increasing in this space
Albers rédige entre décembre 1945 et jan: Albers wrote between December 1945 and January 1946 an unpublished article on art at Black Mountain College for Junior Bazaar magazine. Unpublished, JAAF archive.
Pour partager les 35 dollars de loyer me: To share the 35 dollars of monthly rent, Bill rents a workshop on the second floor with Jack Tworkov; Elaine continues to paint alone in the Flat of Carmine Street, which also serves as a bedroom rent $35/month
Fin 1946, Albers commence sa première gr: At the end of 1946, Albers began its first large series of colours, in two ways: Variants (borrowed from the musical “variations sur un thème”) and Adobes. Mexican colours — deep reds, golden yellows, vibrant roses, burning oranges, greens and browns from the earth, saturated blues from the sky — invade his paintings. Double titles : Variants / Adobes

At the end of 1946, Albers began its first large series of colours, in two ways: Variants (musical borrowing, variations on a theme) and Adobes (a debt to vernacular architecture). Mexican colours: deep red, golden yellow, bright pink, warm oranges, opposed to green, brown and blue saturated from the sky
Anni achève With Verticals, sa dernière: Anni completes With Verticals, his latest work on the scale of his old wall hangings, in two main colors (deep red and rich gold) enhanced by black passages, the “verticales”. Weaving; fusion of Peruvian textiles and linear geometries of prehispanic architecture
Après un concert du samedi soir où il av: After a Saturday night concert where he had played (pianist, it seems), Jalo will have a drink at the Straus as often; On exit he announces “going home now” and collapses on the lawn a few steps away, giving it his last breath. Gretel finds this death beautiful: full of music, celebrating with good friends. lawn, a few steps from the door Consequences: The trip to Italy of the Lowinsky (Guggenheim Scholarship of Eddie, 1946) was postponed for a year: the college asked Eddie to stay in the music department until August 1947.
Bourse pour l'Italie, reportée d'un an à: Scholarship for Italy, postponed for one year due to the death of Jalo (the college retained Eddie until August 1947); Newhall teaches them the photography of manuscripts in preparation. Consequences: Departure to Italy in 1947.
Juste après le petit-déjeuner un jour de: Just after breakfast on a weekday, in the late summer of 1946 (Art Institute), a couple left with water and food to the ridge. She said she was innocent before him; patient and caring. On the way it shows wild flowers, birds, red lichen on the rocks. Grass corner among rocky outcrops, extended army cover, deep blue sky, view over Swannanoa valley; They lower their voice and watch the strangers out of caution. They make love, eat lunch, bathe naked in the sun, go down without regret: a summer adventure without complications. military blanket, red lichen, spring water on face, Swannanoa valley
La nuit de la mort de Jalo frappe la com: La night of the death of Jalo hits the community of despair. Woldin remembers its last concert and its transfigured face by leading “Jesu Meine Freude”; Students dig his grave, choose a stone with Johanna, Ross Penley moves it to the tractor; Brahms Requiem (“Behold all flesh is as the grass”) marks mourning. tomb carved by hand, selected stone, tractor, Brahms Requiem
À la fin de sa première année, Molly Gre: At the end of his first year, Molly Gregory announced his departure, leaving the workshop without a guard. Weitzer goes to see “les pouvoirs” and ends up with Rondy (Rondthaler), the manager, who tells him to handle the workshop himself. Accord: Weitzer responds to tools and materials, the door remains unlocked. negotiated condition: workshop door always open; Rondthaler worried that the tools will smear and the materials will be accounted for Consequences: Weitzer becomes almost instantly owner-manager of the carpentry workshop; his career is launched; no insurance, accounting or school image considerations
Printemps 1946 : Jim Tite, ancien batteu: Spring 1946: Jim Tite, a former professional jazz drummer who has become early, notes at dawn that the carpentry workshop building is a dozen feet longer than the known interior space. A cracking window and a door locked by a rusty cheap padlock, made of three knotty boards, one of which is removable; He enters by forcing with a fallen branch. Inside: talqueous dust, mould, spider cloths, a hand press made of cast iron, pedaled, an ancient even in 1946 — a Challenge-Gordon — and an inclined rack with broken characters (“pied”: em-quads, in-quads, interline and characters mixed with mites, flies, wasps, leaves, twigs and acorns. He announced his discovery at “Rondy” (Rondthaler), which blessed the resurrection of the Black Mountain Press. 12 feet longer than expected; door of 3 boards, rusty lock; Challenge-Gordon cast iron press; Insects dead in the wrecks. Consequences: Renaissance of the college press.
Jim Tite partage son enthousiasme avec A: Jim Tite shares his enthusiasm with Ann Mayer and “évangélise” others. They spend their free time cleaning the workshop, expanding it, sorting and redistributing the characters, oiling the press, replacing the wheel bearings on the tray, and installing an out-of-work Kelvinator engine. They travel to Asheville to stand behind a local printer, water him with questions, observe and learn, before returning to practice. Engine recovered from a defective Kelvinator refrigerator from faculty. Consequences: Birth of a printing course.
Tite, « sachant juste assez pour être da: Tite, “sachant juste assez pour être dangereux”, offers Rondthaler and Bill Levi a co-educated printing practice course with Ann Mayer. He believes that this was the first teaching experience of the college by students, a concept quickly adopted by others (Harry Holl in sculpture, Arthur Penn in theatre). One of his classes has twelve students, with the aim of covering all the college's printing needs to save him money. Harry Weitzer, coming out of his first class, becomes an excellent co-teacher. A class of 12 students. Consequences: Institutionalization of student-teaching.
Ils prévoyaient d'aller ensemble à New Y: They planned to go together to New York at the end of the quarter; One morning, Kremen finds her hammering an indistinct object. He asked why she was working on the work program so early — anecdote about self-sufficiency at the Black Mountain (cut text). Trip to New York expected at the end of the quarter.
Après avoir lu un reportage sur BMC dans: After reading a report about BMC in the Partisan Review, Kremen rushed there. At sunrise, the train crosses the Smokies in the morning mist and sees a log cabin with smoke rising from the stone chimney: a landscape out of his childhood dreams fed with readings about early America. This feels like BMC during activities such as driving livestock to pasture, cutting down trees, harvesting and peeling corn, or fighting a forest fire on the mountain. report in the Partisan Review; log cabin, stone fireplace, smoke, morning fog
Première année de Noland : logique et sé: First year of Noland: logic and semantics with A. W. Levi, sociology with Herbert Miller, tutoring of harmony with “Bimbus” Schlesinger, musical theory with John Cage. Almost immediately he became the student of Bolotowsky (cubist approach), which taught painting during the Albers sabbatical in Mexico. Upon the return of Albers, he took his design course (principles Bauhaus) — a decisive influence for his own design teaching later at the Catholic University of Washington. Consequences: influence on his future teaching at Catholic University
Baker, décrit par un collègue blanc comm: Baker, described by a white colleague as “courageux et sympathique quoique très tendu”, was replaced in the second quarter by the black composer Mark Fax. According to Lowinsky, both “ont fait un travail splendide, leurs cours étaient bien suivis”. No incident of the year, is judged “particulièrement remarquable” given the flow of visitors and the repeated concerts of “Vesta” Martin and Fax in front of people of the vintage.
Les étudiants votent une résolution dema: Students vote a resolution calling for the immediate admission of as many black students as capacity allows, an expanded campaign of applications, the admission of black men as well, and decide to subscribe during the Christmas holidays to help candidates without means. La faculty “souffle un peu” but gives way to the argument: unanimous admission of black men, extension of Lowinsky contacts to black high schools, editors and local sections of NAACP.
Les étudiants adoptent une résolution de: Students adopt a resolution calling for the immediate admission of as many black students as capacity allows, a broader nomination campaign, and the acceptance of black men (until then women alone). They also decided to conduct a fundraising campaign during the Christmas holidays to offer financial assistance to black candidates unable to even pay minimum fees. Collection during Christmas holidays Consequences: The teaching profession gave way to the argument and unanimously voted to add black men to the eligible persons
Après le vote de la faculté, Lowinsky él: After the faculty's vote, Lowinsky expanded its contacts to Black High Schools, newspaper editors, N.A.A.C.P. secretaries, Y.M.C.A. and the American Friends Service Committee's race committee. Consequences: Immediate but temporary results: five black students enrolled in the winter session 1947
Sans aucun soutien de la faculté selon u: Without any support from the faculty according to an admirer student, Wallen urges students to commit themselves specifically outside: a student accompanies two afternoons a week for a full term a young “schizophrène” patient of her age in a nearby psychiatric hospital; Others joined the Southern Negro Youth Congress, carried petitions in the region and tried to register on the electoral lists. Two afternoons a week; two miles of walk to the bus stop each time; a whole quarter. Consequences: Increased contact of the college with the black community and local racial issues.
Rejouant le scénario Bentley-Foreman, pl: Replaying the Bentley-Foreman scenario, several faculty members (especially Europeans, including Dehn and Albers) fear that Niebyl will use the Southern Negro Youth Congress as a cover to organize a Communist cell; Niebyl despised the low scientific level of the Communist Party and apparently never joined. Niebyl arrives with three disciples. Consequences: Board's decision not to renew its contract.
Un télégramme adressé à une étudiante es: A telegram addressed to a student is opened by mistake by someone else; the word circulates that it contains the number forty-seven — exactly the number of votes obtained the day before in community meeting for a proposal. It is concluded that the “complot” Niebyl is in progress and communicates with the outside. The student, subjected to an “bizarre inquisition”, revealed that the telegram came from a reactionary Republican friend and had no connection with the campus. The number 47; a telegram; a community meeting the day before. Consequences: This is so absurd that it feeds the challenge of Niebyl's return.
À l'expiration de sa nomination d'un an,: Upon expiry of his one-year appointment, the Board unanimously decided not to extend Niebyl. A petition of 61 out of 90 students protested: no sufficient reason given, his courses left a great place for the expression of opinions; they ask for the “plus pleine considération” and a community meeting. The Board rejects the petition dryly: no new point, no further statement, a community meeting would only lead to “discussions personnelles”. 61 signatures of 90 students; unanimous vote of the Board. Consequences: Rare case where Board goes against majority sentiment and refuses discussion; Wallen and Levi convince petitioners that the policy did not justify the decision.
Après un entretien à « communication zér: After an interview at “communication zéro” with Albers that accuses him of wanting an “takeover”, Wallen reads a written statement opening on the will of “mettre les choses au grand jour”; he recalls that Albers called him earlier in the year “The Kaiser”, diagnoses that his fears surpass his judgment rather than deliberate malice, and ironizes on the one who, fearing conflicts and dissension, acts to encourage them. Name given by Albers: “The Kaiser”. Consequences: Temporary clarification only.
Fin du printemps 1946, le collège adopte: At the end of spring 1946, the College adopted the proposals of the Wallen-Levi-Rondthaler committee: a Community Council of eight members (three teachers, three students, a representative of the wives and employees, one of the entire community — which may be a student) choosing committees (publications, concerts, library), dealing with student housing, campus cleanliness and “normes de conduite communautaire”, and calling community meetings on petition. A referendum may revoke any unpopular legislation by a two-thirds majority. The report also proposes a joint disciplinary committee of students/teachers with final power of expulsion, and a simple majority vote in faculty meetings when the traditional consensus fails. 8 members; two-thirds for referendum; Students/Teachers parity on the disciplinary committee. Consequences: Democratization seen by the fearful as a palace revolution; Wallen elected President of the Council the following month.
Le mois suivant sa déclaration, Wallen e: The month after his statement, Wallen was elected president of the new council, which seems to the suspect to further consolidate his power. Consequences: Strengthens the distrust of Albers.
Un étudiant rapporte à Wallen qu'Albers: A student reports to Wallen that Albers discussed with him the Council elections, talked about Wallen's “bid for power” and visited some of his advisers to support his favorite student candidates. Wallen informs faculty that these are the very tactics that Albers blamed Bentleyites two years earlier (interference in the Student Moderator election the previous year). Consequences: Open conflict between Albers and Wallen.
À la fin de sa première année, Wallen dé: At the end of his first year, Wallen decided not to complete the requirements of his doctorate of Harvard, believing that an increased awareness of psychological concepts can lead some to an unhealthy introspection: analyze instead of living. Consequences: Shows Wallen's doubts about psychology, which Albers does not see.
Faute d'argent pour construire (l'intéri: For lack of money to build (the interior of the Studies Building remains unfinished), Rondthaler obtains from the government three buildings: student studies, classrooms and reserve, and the third, the most elegant, becomes the first properly lit library of the college — great joy of Nell Rice, library forever. 3 buildings; illuminated library; Nell Rice Consequences: Increased capacity
Le gouvernement donne une presse d'impri: The government gives a printing press, library and office furniture, two typewriters, a new dishwasher, a meat chopper — and, with its “génie de l'inapproprié”, a hundred rotating chairs, a sewer drain and a very large steam pant ironing machine. press, 2 typewriters, dishwasher, chopper, 100 rotating chairs, driver, steam cookers
Dreier, « rêveur en chef », imagine un p: Dreier, “rêveur en chef”, imagines a 15-year program for 125-150 students he considers necessary for financial health. In the absence of an architect-resident, the college hires Architects' Collaborative of Cambridge, a young group to which Gropius has associated, for site plans and general layout. 15 years; 125-150 students targeted Consequences: matrix of future campus development
Mort de Jalowetz début 1946 ; Lowinsky a: Death of Jalowetz in early 1946; Lowinsky accepts a Guggenheim scholarship and then leaves for Queens College. The department is saved in part by the hiring of Charlotte “Bimbus” Schlesinger (trained in Berlin, Vienna, Russia, seven years at Foxhollow School) and by Ms. Jalowetz, who trains a few singing students and gives a binding course that some follow by affection for her. Consequences: Summer institutes 1947 almost suspended.
En 1946, Katherine Litz avait dansé dans: In 1946, Katherine Litz had danced in “The Princess Zonilda and Her Entourage” from Cunningham, a single concert at Hunter; Their paths did not return until 1952 at BMC. A concert at Hunter College Consequences : Reunion from 1952 to BMC (Echo material)
Wallen, psychologue idéaliste de 28 ans: Wallen, a 28-year-old idealist psychologist trained at Harvard, hired in 1945, wanted to impose more order on the college; Albers feared that its taste for efficiency and well-defined structures would stifle variety and spontaneity. Wallen: 28 years old, Harvard Consequences: increasingly conflicting climate
Répondant aux lettres de Ted et Bobbie D: Responding to Ted and Bobbie Dreier's letters on college problems, Albers admits to growing in doubt about his ability to do what it takes for him and for the college; It criticizes those who “placent le gouverner avant le servir” and aim to appear as important as to be; it demolishes Wallen; it reaffirms that good teaching depends on personality and experience more than on method and equipment; He hates equalization for himself; After 13 years of prioritising the college before its needs, approaching 60 years, it must consider its public obligations. “Approchant 60 ans”; 13 years in the service of the college; formula: “I hate equalization for equalizations sake”; call to “common sense” and “organizing oneself before organizing others” Consequences: Materializes the malaise that will lead to his resignation from 1949
La correspondance entre les deux vieux a: La correspondence between the two old friends, cut during the war, resumes; Albers sends care packages, clothes and Mexican coffee; Perdekamp expressed more concern about the sinking of German intellectual life than about comfort; He admires that Albers was so soon freed from historicalism. Perdekamp discovers Thomas Wolfe, who opposes heavy German culture to America where time flows Consequences: Refreshing the 1924 essay Historisch oder Jetzig
