Blumeneau, Lindenfeld et Zeisler étudien: Blumeneau, Lindenfeld and Zeisler studied with Albers in the summer of 1946; With Guermonprez, four women share the workshop, rich conversations on pre-industrial techniques Zeisler has formed a collection of non-Western art, rich in pre-Columbian textiles Consequences: Future radiation: Blumeneau Curator of textiles at Cooper-Hewitt, Lindenfeld tapestries and courses in Japan
Malgré des approches formelles et philos: Despite divergent formal and philosophical approaches, Josef Albers invited Jacob Lawrence to teach at the Summer Art Institute in 1946; he came with his wife, the painter Gwendolyn Knight Lawrence photo of the couple by Beaumont Newhall in summer 1946 Consequences: the encounter prompted Lawrence to intensify its work on line, shape, color and texture; he'll call himself a direct descendant of Bauhaus and credit Albers as “un des grands maîtres de notre temps”
Karnes étudie avec Josef Albers et Molly: Karnes studied with Josef Albers and Molly Gregory during the summer session 1946; She will be the only American studio ceramicist to have been both a student and a college teacher.
Les catalogues publiés chaque année depu: Catalogues published each year since 1934 cease after 1946; booklets stapled in identical format, photographs of the life of the college, stamp drawn by Albers.
Moholy-Nagy engage le jeune photographe: Moholy-Nagy hires the relatively inexperienced young photographer at the Institute of Design; Callahan's leaving Detroit for Chicago.
Junius Bird, conservateur d'archéologie: Junius Bird, curator of archaeology at New York's American Museum of Natural History, exhumes a site containing textiles dating back to 2500 B.C., including a bird's piece of floating chain wire in a plain canvas field. textiles dated 2500 BC; a bird; floating chain wire in a canvas field Consequences: Anni Albers makes it a major example of the direct formal language of the threads
Des jeunes amis d'Anni Albers lui racont: Young friends of Anni Albers told him, the year before 1947, of Gropius's opening speech for the new quarter at Harvard: what marked them was the experience of perceiving meaning and meaning in a confused world — the same orientation experience as at Bauhaus. Consequences: Parallel established by Anni between 1922 and 1946
La fille de Walter et Ise Gropius obtien: La daughter of Walter and Ise Gropius graduated from Black Mountain College; She's the godmother of the Dreier girl. Family sponsorship link
Un numéro spécial de Design magazine (47: A special issue of Design magazine (47.8, 1946) is devoted entirely to Black Mountain's Summer Art Institute 1945, illustrating the positive publicity generated by the summer institutes of Albers. Consequences: Strengthens Albers's argument for a reorientation to the arts
La revue Design consacre un numéro entie: La magazine Design devotes an entire issue (vol. 47.8) to the Summer Art Institutes of Black Mountain of 1945, generating a very positive advertisement for the college. Design 47.8 (1946), special issue “Black Mountain College” Consequences: Strengthens the position of Albers that sees visual arts and music as the dominant interests of students
Cherchant du travail à Los Angeles, il r: Seeking work in Los Angeles, he met Pat Pearman who advised him to study art at the Kansas City Art Institute through the G.I. Bill. G.I. Bill of Rights Consequences: Registration at Kansas City Art Institute
S'installe à Los Angeles, travaille briè: settled in Los Angeles, briefly worked as an illustrator for a Westwood newspaper, then as a packing clerk at the Ballerina swimsuit factory, where he met Pat Pearman, a stylist assistant, who convinced him that he had talent after seeing his drawings. Plant Ballerina Bathing Suit Consequences : Decision to become an artist
Invité par Albers comme instructeur invi: Invited by Albers as guest instructor for the summer of 1946, Lawrence discovers “un des grands professeurs de notre temps”, although their works have no apparent relationship; He will then base his own teaching on that of Bauhaus and Albers. Photo of Lawrence and Gwendolyn Knight by Beaumont Newhall, summer 1946 Consequences: Sustainable influence of Albers pedagogy on Lawrence teacher
La session d'été 1946, très remarquée, v: La summer session 1946, very notable, is worth a profile in Design magazine. Magazine coverage Consequences : Growth of the reputation of the college
Notes prises par l'étudiant Harry Seidle: Notes taken by student Harry Seidler during Albers color and design classes, summer 1946 Notes dated summer 1946, 8 pages
L'étudiant Harry Seidler prend des notes: Student Harry Seidler takes detailed notes during Albers colour and design classes in the summer of 1946. Notes kept at the Albers Foundation, 8 pages or more.
Institut d'art d'été : aux côtés d'Anni: Summer art institute: alongside Anni and Josef Albers teach the painter Jacob Lawrence, Jean Varda, sculptor Leo Amino, architect Bertrand Goldberg (former of the Bauhaus, invited because Walter Gropius could only come in conference) and the historian of photography Beaumont Newhall, freshly released from the MoMA. Maya Deren is invited for a film cycle organized by Albers and Newhall but cannot come. More than sixty students enrolled; among them Ruth Asawa, Joseph Fiore and Ray Johnson. Consequences: The April 1946 issue of Design magazine, devoted to college, greatly increases interest and enrolment.
Walter Gropius ne peut venir à l'été 194: Walter Gropius can only come in summer 1946 for a conference; Bertrand Goldberg, another Bauhaus elder, is invited to teach in his place.
Après l'année écoulée, Grice trouve à la: After the last year, Grice found a small wooden cabin in the family on the property of Boone Hall Plantation, an 18th-century establishment whose main mansion was rebuilt in 1935. Rice installs its writing desk in one of the nine brick huts in a room, remains of the slaves of the plantation. Abundant pecans and fig trees, good vegetable garden, crab caught from a nearby pontoon; Rice's culinary skills Consequences: Harvests complement the family's meagre income.
Commence la série d'abstractions en noir: Start the series of abstractions in black and white.
Graham, ancien aristocrate tsariste, aba: Graham, a former Czarist aristocrat, abandoned psychoanalysis for esoteric and magical systems, vilipended abstraction and worshipped the old masters; in a four-page manifesto entitled The case of Mr. Picasso (declarations made during an interview on 15 January 1942), he accused Picasso of “hoax” and of making international money. Manifesto of 4 pages, circulated in 1946 Consequences: Out with previous modernist commitments
À sa première publicité en 1946, la Wich: With its first advertisement in 1946, Wichita House received approximately 37,000 letters from potential buyers, but the shortage of materials and the initial cost of tooling prevented serial production. 37,000 letters; home available in cash for less than one hundred dollars Consequences: no start-up
Elle s'installe à New York ; son studio: It installs at New York; Her studio is in the basement, windows on the garden, she works in artificial light.
Après des années de travail acharné, Kli: After years of hard work, Kline goes through a depression such that he cannot touch a brush for months; Edlich ordered him the portrait of Mahatma Gandhi, whom he venerated. Kline paints a gentle, impersonal, distant study, as if he hadn't given much thought to the subject Consequences: Kline finds his easel
À partir de janvier 1946, Olson rend rég: From January 1946, Olson regularly visited Pound, interned for treason after his pro-fascist speeches on Italian radio; he collects and responds to his mail and creates an “Committee of Correspondence” to mobilize his support. Consequences: Model of the epistolar network that Olson will develop at Black Mountain
Un feu réduit le studio en cendres, détr: A fire reduced the studio to ashes, destroying about thirty paintings (half painted in the previous nine months); neither a book nor a canvas are saved. About 30 tables destroyed Consequences: Start of the disaster series
Après le concert du samedi, Jalo prend u: After the Saturday concert, Jalo has a drink at the Straus; he comes out, says “je rentre maintenant”, takes a few steps on the lawn and collapses, breathing his last breath Words: “going home now” — I now return Atmosphere: Winter night after a concert, warmth of friends, sweet death in music Issue: La disappearance of the musical pillar of the college
La nouvelle de la mort de Jalo frappe la: La news of the death of Jalo hits the community; students dig the grave, choose a stone with Johanna, Ross installs it on the tractor; The Brahms Requiem is Sung Words: “Behold all flesh is as the grass” (Extract from the Requiem) Atmosphere: desperation stun, collective mourning at the work of hands Issue: the community pays its last tribute through manual work
À l'aube, montée solitaire vers l'atelie: At dawn, lonely climb to the workshop; building length anomaly; Crushing window, rusty padlock, removable board torn by a branch; four-legged entry; Spider dust and webs; discovery of the Challenge-Gordon and the messy breaks; announces to Rondy and blessing received. Atmosphere: Wet mystery, smell of talc and moss, gothic darkness. Issue: A forced door opens an institutional renaissance: the Black Mountain Press.
Première image humaine de Lane à BMC : u: First human image from Lane to BMC: a long-haired woman jumps in front of him on the way, stops at the Y with her black spaniel cocker in front of the large lilac in bloom; with a wide gesture she takes the lilac in her arms, loves it, feels it, embraces it; Seeing to be seen, she laughs and starts a leap towards the road, questioning her from the look Words: “Eh, Blackie, que penses-tu de toutes ces folies ? C'est quoi tout ce cirque, hein, Blackie ?” (paraphrase) Atmosphere: Spring, lilac in bloom, joyful and slightly shameful momentum of the witness Issue: Founding meeting: the woman who seduces Lane will be her teacher
Un télégramme est ouvert par erreur ; on: A telegram is opened by mistake; it shows the number 47; 47 people voted the day before in community meeting for a proposal; The rumor concludes a Niebyl plot in connection with the outside; Finally, we question the recipient, who undergoes an “bizarre inquisition”; The telegram came from a reactionary Republican friend, unrelated to campus. Words: La intended for Duberman: she was subjected to an “bizarre inquisition”. Atmosphere: Paranoia mixed with ridicule; the greatest surprise being the irrelevance of the outside world. Issue: Suspect of communist conspiracy destroys Niebyl's reputation.
Après un entretien manqué avec Albers, W: After a missed interview with Albers, Wallen read his written statement: he cites “bid for power”'s accusation, recalls the nickname “The Kaiser”, refuses interpretation by projection, attributes Albers's conduct to fear, denounces his election interference as the very tactics he blamed the Bentleyites, pleads for trust and concludes with hope for “éclaircir l'atmosphère”. Words: “Je voudrais mettre les choses clairement au grand jour pour mettre fin aux grondements clandestins”; “devons-nous tous être exactement pareils pour coopérer ?”; “j'espère que cela éclaircira quelque peu l'atmosphère”. Atmosphere : Serious, tense, almost solemn; A whimsical tone at times. Issue: The future of trust in the community and the power struggle Wallen/Albers.
Bouleversé par leurs deux lettres trop t: Broken by their two letters too touching for an immediate response, Albers writes his most intimate answer: growing doubts, criticism of the faculty that governs instead of serving, attack against Wallen with a scrambled brain, plea for common sense and action, admitted that approaching 60 years he can no longer postpone his work. Words: “Both your letters were too touching to be answered immediately”; “I hate equalization for equalizations sake” Atmosphere: Epistolary Intimacy, Intertwined Affection and Wearness Issue: The desire to leave against loyalty
Pour ancrer la distinction entre angles,: To anchor the distinction between angles, Albers raises the whole class; Each one extends his pencil to 30, then 45, then 60 degrees, testing the angle in his body before drawing him Words: Albers insists that the angles be clearly distinguished Atmosphere: Playful and physical discipline, photographed (clicked from 1946) Issue: Smell that slight differences produce radical effects
Albers et ses élèves, rassemblés, tenden: Albers and its students, gathered together, each stretch their pencil at arm end to measure and compare angles in front of them. Atmosphere: collective concentration, open-air workshop Issue: teaching visual perception through gesture
Le corps enseignant de l'Institut d'été: The teaching staff of the Summer Institute arranges for the official photo; Jean Varda is tied in a tree. Atmosphere : summer, festive, a touch of fantasy
Quatre femmes, dont trois nouvelles venu: Four women, including three new arrivals, work simultaneously in the workshop; conversations about pre-Columbian weaving and pre-industrial techniques; Zeisler speaks of his work as “primitive sophistiquée” Words: Zeisler: “I think of my work as sort of sophisticated primitive” Atmosphere: Warm, stimulating, veneration community for ancient weaving Issue: Transmission of a legacy: BMC's workshop as a matrix of modern American textiles
Pendant l'été 1946, Nancy Newhall, sans: In the summer of 1946, Nancy Newhall, without a college appointment, photographed the couple Lawrence. Issue: Woman artist working but officially invisible at BMC.
Le jeune Jouffroy découvre The Armoire o: Young Jouffroy discovers The Wardrobe of Proteus and understands that painting can evoke “une image de l'inconnu”, which leads him to reconsider the basics of art and poetry. Words: “jusqu'alors, je croyais que seule la poésie pouvait explorer l'inaccessible en l'homme” Atmosphere: Aesthetic Revelation Issue: Critical Vocation of Jouffroy
Avec peu de temps, les deux peintres agr: In a short time, the two painters enlarged on about 17 square feet a small painting of the Last Judgment, with calcimine and charcoal, with $5 in hardware painting; A high heel appears in front of the satyre. Words: Kooning describes the source at Hess as “the four angels at the gates of Paradise”, Elaine as “Judgment Day” Atmosphere: Fast work, myth ink, macabre humour Issue: Human animality after the war
Après des années de labeur, Kline ne peu: After years of hard work, Kline can no longer take a brush for months; his doctor and patron bring him back to the horse by commanding the portrait of Mahatma Gandhi, whom he worships; Kline paints a soft and detached study. Atmosphere: overwhelming depression, then empathic docility Issue: Rescue of the painter by patronage
Admis avec classe avancée bien qu'il n'a: Admitted with advanced class although he does not have a BMC degree. Initially envious of the best technical drawing skills of others, he realized that the courses of Albers, the excellent physics course of Peter Bergmann and his construction experience largely compensate; He quickly mastered the technique. Consequences: Mr. Arch in 1949.
Un mois après l'incendie, cancer et opér: A month after the fire, cancer and drastic operation; According to Ethel Schwabacher, a farmer attached to his health, Gorky experienced the operation as a traumatic attack on the integrity of his ego.
Réunion de faculté du 13 février 1946 me: Faculty meeting of 13 February 1946 setting up the Wallen-Levi-Rondthaler Committee; Five-page report signed of the three; declaration of Wallen at the faculty of 13 May 1946. Curiously, in 1968, Wallen no longer remembered the origin of the Community Council: this “ne lui rappelait rien”. Five-page report signed Wallen, Levi, Rondthaler; Community Bulletins of April and June 1946; Newsletter Vol. V, No. 1 (November 1946) Consequences: Creation of the Community Council
Wallen a reçu plus de 25 % du corps étud: Wallen received more than 25% of the student body — seventeen out of sixty students — in interviews, mainly simple counselling sessions, but more and more students coming to have their TAT (Thematic Apperception Tests) taken at the beginning of the introductory psychology course. 17 out of 60 students; TAT tests at the beginning of Introduction Psychology courses
Design magazine consacre un numéro spéci: Design magazine devotes a special issue to Black Mountain (April 1946 cover attributed here to Alvin Lustig); students and faculty produce many attractive brochures, to the sunny images of young students, working the earth and doing art. Design cover, April 1946 Consequences: Utopian “boosterism” continuation
Invité à peindre une toile de fond pour: Invited to paint a background for Marie Marchowsky's Labyrinth choreography, created in April, with little time and $50, of Kooning expands a painting on recent paper — described to Hess as “the four angels at the gates of Paradise” and Elaine as an “Judgment Day”. With Milton Resnick, he painted a square of about 17 feet with painting bought $5 at the hardware store. A high heel shoe appears near the satyresque creature. Fee: $50; painting: $5; 5.13 x 5.18 m; Calcimine and charcoal on canvas Consequences: Expedition to hardware would have stimulated his taste for home and sign enamels, the material of black and white abstractions
Le magazine Junior Bazaar consacre un ar: Junior Bazaar magazine devotes an article to Black Mountain College (pp. 130-133). May 1946, pp. 130-33
Guermonprez, fille des Jalowetz restée a: Guermonprez, daughter of the Jalowetz who remained in the Netherlands during the war, obtained an American visa at the invitation of Anni Albers Consequences: She will teach alongside Albers from 1947 to 1948
L'émigré japonais Leo Amino arrive pour: Japanese emigrant Leo Amino arrives to teach at the Summer Art Institute in 1946; In the rural landscape, he finds echoes of organic forms of his sculptures. Son of a ikebana artist and calligrapher; no room in college to sink polyester resin Consequences: It continues to sculpt animal and plant forms in recovery wood
Dès la fin du Summer Art Institute 1946,: From the end of the Summer Art Institute 1946, the Albers left for a year: crossing the United States by car by New York, Boston, Niagara, Detroit, Chicago, Denver, San Francisco, Los Angeles to New Mexico (late 1946), then Mexico. Albers writes to Perdekamp that their economic limit is compensated by intellectual freedom that they would not exchange for a better situation elsewhere. travel by car, arrival in New Mexico at the end of 1946 Consequences: prolonged absence during a difficult year of college
Peu après le retour de Breton des États-: Shortly after Breton's return from the United States, Jouffroy met him by chance in a hotel and quickly joined the Surrealists. Consequences: Jouffroy's entry into the surrealist group
Premier voyage depuis la guerre (rationn: First trip since the war (ration of gasoline). Stay in Mexico from 1 May to the end of October 1947; visits to Oaxaca, Chiapas, Pátzcuaro, Guadalajara. Josef starts the “Variantes” / “Adobes” series. More than 100 studies in unmixed colours (salmon and pink excepted). Anni buys pre-Columbian and contemporary fabrics for the Harriett Engelhardt Memorial Collection. Letters to Ludwig Grote (7 July 1947) and Will Grohmann (22 February 1948)
Sabbatique d'un an à partir d'octobre 19: One-year Sabbatic from October 1946; Mexico from 1 May to the end of October 1947, the first trip since the rationing of petrol. First at the Mangold (Lerma 257 no 2), then rent #4 of the same building. Josef starts Variants / Adobes (more than 100 studies, colors not mixed except pink, without underlay or retouch). Anni collects textiles for the Harriett Engelhardt Memorial Collection, founded after the death in Germany in 1945 of his former student Harriett Engelhardt (Red Cross); Collection exhibited at BMC and used as teaching material. letter to Ludwig Grote of 1947-07-07; letter to Will Grohmann of 1948-02-22
Elaine produit pour Mademoiselle un arti: Elaine produces for Mademoiselle a background article on all the ballet companies of the New York season: dancers, choreographers, impresarios and theatres.
Premier match de football du Thanksgivin: First Thanksgiving 1946 football match (or 1947 according to Corkran): Informal university football satyre, parody program with stuffed jersey numbers (Atkinson 3.1416, Schauffler 98.6, Nakata .0005, Fox .606, Sherman 1.000 approx., Roberts 8:45). On the first game, Ike Nakata dives into Faf Foster who jumps him elegantly — twice; The third Ike Snap rose. The players themselves became harsh and serious. Cro-Magnons win 8-0 (Atkinson); Corkran remembers a 6-6 zero without expected conversion points. Dave Corkran blocks Dan Rice flat and launches a pass that Pete Jennerjahn grabs from his fingertips on ten yards before falling into the rhododendrons at the edge of the field, on the bank below Lake Eden. Parodic jersey numbers, rhododendrons, bank under Lake Eden, ball juggling on fingers Consequences: for Corkran, demonstration of the continuity between American culture and college life; better-resolved philosophical tensions on the ground
Premier jeu du match de Thanksgiving ; a: First game of Thanksgiving match; At the snap, Ike dives on Faf who is no longer there — he skipped it elegantly; second snap, same thing; On the third, Ike stands; the game resumes shortly after and Faf no longer jumps from the afternoon Atmosphere: Hilare on the benches, brutal on the field Issue: friendship and rivalry in the same duel
Avec un an de congé sabbatique du Black: With one year of Black Mountain College sabbatical leave, the Albers take place in La Luz, in the desert of New Mexico, 90 miles north of El Paso (Texas), in an already known adobe house on their way to Mexico. House of barro (adobe), ninety miles north of El Paso; Letter from Josef to Franz Perdekamp : “por fin paz... lejos de la educación y de la administración” Consequences : Birth of the Variants/Adobes series
En route vers le Mexique pour une année: On the way to Mexico for a sabbatical year of Black Mountain College, the Albers return to La Luz, a small town in the New Mexico desert 90 miles north of El Paso (Texas), a refuge already discovered before. House in adobe; blue sky; 90 miles north of El Paso Consequences: Josef starts painting intensely, away from teaching and administration
À Noël 1946, Anni Albers visite La Luz a: At Christmas 1946, Anni Albers visited La Luz in Texas and the local Mexican churches, the source of La Luz I (1947). cross woven in silver metallic yarn on orange, red, yellow, beige colours Consequences: tapestry La Luz I
Les Albers s'installent dans la maison d: The Albers settle in the adobe house they have already discovered; Josef writes to Perdekamp that at last peace, far from education and administration, they can think of them; he starts his strict painting diet and paints day and night; as early as September he reports on his discoveries on the colors that lose their identity Words: Letters to Perdekamp: “en una casa de barro, bajo cielos azules... por fin paz”; “es maravilloso”; pride when the greens become blue and the red neutral greys violacés Atmosphere: Desert, blue sky, isolation, lab effervescence Issue: La teacher's metamorphosis as a painter of pure color
Josef écrit à son ami Perdekamp depuis l: Josef writes to his friend Perdekamp from the adobe house: finally peace, far from education and administration, they can again think of themselves; It imposes a very strict pictorial diet. Words : “finally peace ... far from education and administration we are able once more to think of ourselves” — “enfin la paix... loin de l'éducation et de l'administration nous pouvons de nouveau penser à nous-mêmes” Atmosphere : Desert, blue sky, clay house, calm found Issue : The artist frees himself from the charges of college to be reborn as a painter
Dans le cadre de la réforme de 1947, Cru: As part of the 1947 reform, Cruz founded this course based on De Stijl's ideas and partly on the Bauhaus model; programme published in the magazine Plinto (No. 1, October 1947). Consequences: Becomes in 1949 the Composición Pura.
Montages datés '47 : Monte Albán (17 con: Mounts dated '47: Monte Albán (17 contacts) and Teotihuacán (35 contacts), certifying a new journey while Albers still teaches at BMC.
Anni réalise sa première petite œuvre du: Anni makes her first small work of the type she will call “pictorial weavings”, giving textiles the status of easel paintings — objects of purely aesthetic sense, regardless of use. South of the Border: ten centimetres high, one of its smallest pieces Consequences: Increased freedom of creation
Les dix peintures Adobe restées au Mexiq: The ten Adobe paintings left in Mexico are entrusted to Inés Amor, whose gallery founded in 1935 was Mexico's largest; a lasting friendship is born between them.
Le veau noir inattendu bouleverse quelqu: The unexpected black calf somewhat upsets the farm's plans. Jealous genaise (sey heifer), black calf
Le ravin près du cottage des Jalowetz es: The ravine near the Jalowetz cottage is cleared to serve as pasture for calves; three months of grazing on newly fenced cover strips; potatoes, silage maize, oats and clover sown; cabbage and onions above Black Dwarf; salads, radishes, cactus and lilies in the Albers garden; beans and sweet corn in front of the farm under construction; Bennett land (8 acres rented) in spring oats, barley, clover and lespedeza; 4500 small trees (robin trees, balsam trees, white pine) planted on eroded slopes; large unloading fork in the barn; three growing Guernsey heifers; Health records and tests. 8 acres rented; 4500 trees; three Guernsey calves
Un an après la mort de Jalowetz, étudian: One year after the death of Jalowetz, students and professors led by Eddie interpret Brahms' Requiem; Gretel sings tenor's desk with several women and very few men. female tenors, few men
Un petit recueil de poèmes écrits et imp: A small collection of poems written and printed in college even by M. C. Richards; Two poems are extracted (pp. 176-177). collection printed on site
Au printemps 1947, deux membres du corps: In the spring of 1947, two faculty members resigned one week apart: one felt that BMC was too college and not enough community, the other too community and not enough college. Before the end of the summer, they both went back on their decision and asked to withdraw their resignation, which was granted with joy. One-week quits Consequences: Evidence that college and community are not exclusive
Frank Rice, nouveau membre de la faculté: Frank Rice, a new faculty member in 1947, was hired to teach German and supervise printing. Having made a career elsewhere in the graphic arts, he is a devoted grammairian who teaches everyone to say correctly “printing shop”: “A print shop is where they sell prints. Was richtig ist, ist richtig. Nicht wahr?”
Bolotowsky emmène quatre jeunes filles d: Bolotowsky takes four young girls into her tabot and leads them crazyly on winding mountain roads to places of dream: ornamental lakes, mica mines, sleepy points of view. Each one lived some private torment, but this magical afternoon, they cavalk and pose as he filmed all the time; He himself played their mischievousness. The world seemed peaceful. tacot (jalopy); mica mines; ornamental lakes; film shot continuously; picture about 1947 of the four girls
La population locale déteste l'école pou: La local population hates school for its liberal Black admission policy; Krikorian, in Model A Ford, is arrested on leaving the city, sentenced for speeding and dangerous driving, then hit with a suspended vagabond violation: if he returns to town, imprisonment without further trial and road gang. His dead battery, the two policemen have to push the car, one teaching him about Southern hospitality. Model A cruise at 35 mph; empty battery at the start. Consequences: De facto ban on the city.
Expert-comptable diplômé, recruté à 34 a: Graduated accountant, recruited at 34 to become chief financial officer of the 'new management team'; understands the real motive only months later, when a faculty member reviews him/her 'life facts'; the treasurer in place is the noblest man he has known there, replacing him being unthinkable — unhappy arrival from the beginning. Consequences: Conflict of structural loyalty.
Cinq étudiants noirs, dont deux hommes a: Five black students, including two veterans, registered for the winter 1947 session. No black teachers could be recruited. 5 Black Students, including 2 Veteran Men Consequences: Public Statement Ending Race Program Stage “expérimental”
La faculté vote la fin du stade « expéri: La faculty votes the end of the “expérimental” stage of its race program and publishes a declaration: admission will now be “ouverte à tous les étudiants de toutes les races”. Official formula: admission open to all students of all races
Une seule des cinq étudiantes noires rev: Only one of the five black students returns for the fall 1947 session (it will remain several years); No new recruitment succeeds. 1 in 5 students returns Consequences: After 1947, almost more blacks on campus
Lowinsky part en Italie avec une bourse: Lowinsky goes to Italy with a Guggenheim scholarship, then joins Queens College. He wrote Bobbie Dreier about her pain in learning about black student recruitment and her analysis: if BMC doesn't find one, she doesn't really want it. Guggenheim Scholarship
Wallen finit par démissionner ; parmi se: Wallen eventually resigns; Among its main complaints: the “tiraillement dans toutes les directions” makes BMC an “chaos académique”. Consequences: Departure of the principal lawyer from the “communauté” pole.
Après une visite de deux semaines « merv: After a visit of two weeks “merveilleuse”, Penn, 24, entered as a regular student in 1947, attracted by the stories of his brother Irving on the Bauhaus. The theatre is then almost non-existent, which does not bother him: he hopes to become a writer while feeling that he will make “sa vie” theatre. 24 years; Two-week visit; former actor/register/technician at the Neighborhood Playhouse in Philadelphia; One more year in the army to stage plays to fund his studies. Consequences: Start of the Black Mountain theatre with Penn.
Après des récits de son frère Irving sur: After stories from his brother Irving about the Bauhaus, Arthur Penn learns that former members of the Bauhaus are at Black Mountain; he made a two-week visit there, he liked it very much and decided to register as a regular student in 1947. Penn was 24 at the time; Two-week visit. Consequences: Birth of the theatre at Black Mountain after the departure of Wunsch.
Wallen propose au Board of Fellows que s: Wallen proposes to the Board of Fellows that its chair become “community development” and that students can graduate in “community service”: rural sociology seminars, readings, and fieldwork in neighbouring communities (help with harvests, teaching card weaving and drawing, group discussions, conferences and concerts, daycares). He offers to contact people in the neighbourhood himself. It targets units of less than 5,000 inhabitants. “less than five thousand population”; Weaving on map, drawing, daycares, help with harvests Consequences: the Board accepts softly keeping the wording “psychologie”; Wallen reads a refusal to get involved
Le Board accepte que Wallen reste et ens: The Board accepts that Wallen stays and teaches exactly what it proposes, while continuing to call it “psychologie”. M.C. Richards, favorable, asks tougher questions: will the goal stated by fifteen students suffice to John? Does he not leave the community of Black Mountain for that of the outside? She confesses an “jalousie” to those who will help Old Fort. reaction summarized by Wallen as “do anything you please, John” Consequences: Wallen confirms resignation
Arrivé en 1945, Levi trouve sciences soc: Arrived in 1945, Levi finds social sciences and humanities relegated to the arts; He wants to develop them around “problèmes actuels et pressants” public policy. In autumn 1947 he taught “Logique” and “L'individu dans la société”; Mary Caroline Richards (his wife) poetry and fiction; Rondthaler adds “Histoire de la langue anglaise” to its Latin; Frank Rice (John Andrew thread) teaches German; Wallen “Processus de groupe”; Max Dehn, at the request of students, “Problèmes de philosophie”. Consequences: Domination of art and partially reduced music — the source of conflict when the Albers returned in 1948.
Tasker Howard Jr., ancien diplômé, sept: Tasker Howard Jr., former graduate, seven years at the National Labor Relations Board at Washington, comes back to teach “Économie introductive” and “Problèmes économiques du travail”. Natasha Goldowski, a 100-pound acrobat dancer who became an international physicist of nearly 200 books, Russian, doctor of the Sorbonne, who arrived in the United States in 1942, published Introduction to the Study of Corrosion, worked on the Manhattan project in Chicago and telefilm in Princeton; he teaches physics and chemistry (Hansgirg on final leave). His mother, tiny and spectral, known as “Madame”, gave private lessons in French and Russian.
Molly Gregory décide de démissionner de: Molly Gregory decides to resign as Corporate Secretary and to refuse re-election to the Board of Fellows; Albers then blames him for having it “vendu” (leashed). Albers tells her she had “sold down the river”; Molly judges the remark “silliness” (absurd). Consequences: She leaves the community before the open explosion of the crisis.
Elle quitte ses fonctions, excédée de se: She quits her duties, exceeding her sense of ownership of Albers and Dreier; Albers blames him for having “vendu”. Consequences: She leaves the community before the open explosion of the crisis
BMC interroge ses anciens élèves, notamm: BMC questions its former students, particularly about their experiences in admission to higher education; published in the BMC Bulletin, vol. 6, No. 1, January 1948. Nominal list of all graduates 1935-1948 with fields, examiners and careers, at the archives of Raleigh
L'atelier d'imprimerie, dormant depuis u: The printing shop, which has been sleeping for some time, is being revived by the acquisition of a government surplus press; It is hoped that he will print the college documents and publish student texts. government surplus press; Bulletin BMC Vol. 6 No. 4 (May 1948); Quality and design of official printing significantly improve Consequences: Creation of the Tite printing course
Des sketchs burlesques montés par Penn p: Burlesque sketches mounted by Penn cause “un petit choc” because they are slightly grivois, a popular comic. Penn remembers: "faintly bawdy . . . sort of low-class comic"
Agitation en 1947 pour transformer BMC e: Agitation in 1947 to transform BMC into college year-round, an idea initiated by Wallen and vigorously pushed by Mary Caroline Richards, for financial and emotional reasons. M.C. Richards: "living year-round rather than skirting a breakdown for nine months and borrowing money to get away from it all the other three"; Five-page “Re: Wallen Proposal” Manuscript Consequences: Adoption of the Hansgirg Calendar Revision
Outre les cours informels de Penn, Holl: In addition to the informal courses of Penn, Holl and Tite, small groups are studying French conversation with a staff member's wife, stenography with Rondthaler, and the history of intentional communities.
Kahn est invité pour la première fois à: Kahn was invited for the first time to Yale as a guest reviewer in architecture in autumn 1947; The following year he coordinated the invited critics and organized the first collaborative problem. Consequences: He will be responsible for the first collaborative problem in autumn 1948 (designation of a UNESCO headquarters).
Anni Albers écrit qu'il faut prendre le: Anni Albers writes that it is necessary to take the material in the hand and learn from it, approaching it in a receptive and non-aggressive way — a point of view already implicit in his work at Bauhaus and parallel to the teaching of Josef. Consequences: Illustrating the couple's intellectual symbiotic relationship
Albers accepte de devenir recteur à cond: Albers agrees to become rector provided that Ted Dreier provides administrative support; Dreier takes over as treasurer. Consequences: Albers will lead the college until the 1949 reorganization
Comme nombre de ses condisciples, Asawa: Like many of his fellow students, Asawa joins the Albers in Toluca in the sabbatical year; She volunteered as an art teacher and became the pupil of the local vanniers, discovering the hooked wire. Consequences: Birth of hooked wire sculptures
Elle visite le collège pour voir son ami: She visits the college to see her close friend, the weaver Trude Guermonprez, who teaches with Anni Albers.
À l'automne 1947 arrivent les couples Mo: In the fall of 1947 the couples Moles and Trayer (Trayer had been secretary of the college and then registrar in 1942-43); influenced by J. I. Rodale and his magazine Organic Farming and Gardening (founded in 1942), they improve the soil and clear for pastures, and offer the courses Introduction to Agriculture and Soil and Steel.
Albers, reconnaissant le talent de Johns: Albers, recognizing the talent of Johnson, obtained the commission of the cover of the industrial design magazine Interiors Consequences: First professional recognition of Johnson
Anni Albers rédige l'essai daté 1947, pu: Anni Albers wrote the essay dated 1947, published in this collection, on design as a coalition of functional and aesthetics and on the anonymity of the good designer. “1947” test at end of text
Pendant les congés de Black Mountain Col: During Black Mountain College's leave, Asawa teaches children the weaving of palm leaves in baskets and discovers the metallic thread that it puts itself at “crocheter”. She said in 1957: “Crocheting bores me to death. But working with wire is fascinating”; She also studied with Cuban designer Clara Porset Consequences: Birth of the technique of curly sculptures made of wire
Pendant ses études au Kansas City Art In: While studying at the Kansas City Art Institute, Rauschenberg works on making cinema sets and photographer accessories — objects made to be consumed by the camera's gaze.
S'inscrit au Kansas City Art Institute f: Joins the Kansas City Art Institute funded by the G.I. Bill.
Arrivé trop tôt le matin pour appeler Pa: Arrived too early in the morning to call Pat Pearson, he waits for dawn and decides that his new life as an artist deserves a new name: he chooses Robert, the first name of his German grandfather. German grandfather's name: Robert Consequences: he will now sign Robert Rauschenberg (born Milton)
Suit Pat Pearman à Kansas City ; change: Following Pat Pearman in Kansas City; changes his first name from Milton to Bob (then Robert), after spending an entire night in a Savarin coffee shop thinking about the most common names. Working at night at various small jobs, taking courses, saving money to study art in Paris. Full night in a Savarin café
Olson rencontre Duncan, alors âgé de 28: Olson meets Duncan, then 28 years old; Duncan remembers a conversation about economic relations between cities and their surrounding landscape, a topic that Olson was already meditating on. Consequences: Start of correspondence within the Black Mountain network
À dix-sept ans, sachant déjà qu'elle veu: At the age of 17, already knowing that she wanted to be an artist, she visited Black Mountain at the senior level, observed the style of progressive education and decided to go there to study with Josef Albers, who had arrived at the college in 1933 two months after the opening. She had also applied to Bennington and Bard; her father demanded that she go to college Consequences: She signed up for Black Mountain
La maison-machine vendue comme ensemble: La house-machine sold as a bundle (hull + equipment) fails: no customization possible, buyers already have furniture and appliances rendered superfluous, curved interior walls unsuitable for current furniture, prohibitive unit cost due to lack of actual mass production. Lot including furniture, appliances and appliances; silhouettes standardized in several sizes in theory only Consequences: The dome finds its real financiers in American military agencies
Cage donne à une composition le titre «: Cage gives a composition the title “Music for Marcel Duchamp”. Consequences: Sign of Duchamp's importance to him before BMC
En 1947 elle exécute ses premiers dessin: In 1947 she executed her first drawings conceived without the weaving in mind, exploring the chance of an abandoned wire (plank 1), which she then developed in graphic and weaving. a thread thrown, its random plot Consequences: prelude to the passage to the graph
Frank Rice quitte Charleston pour un pos: Frank Rice leaves Charleston for a German position at Black Mountain College, knowing that his father is furious about this decision. La exact cause of anger remains conjectural: loss of family support on site, slight feelings towards George Grice who had hired Frank, or reanimation of bitter memories of Rice on college. Consequences: Rice wants to get closer to its New York publishing contacts.
En 1947, vingt-cinq ans après son arrivé: In 1947, twenty-five years after her arrival, Anni wrote in English — a language acquired with an Irish governess in childhood and became eloquent at Black Mountain, where she and Josef had lived for fourteen years — the story of her arrival: students in white “vestal”, bags and dresses “homemade”, a place of trial, exuberant confusion, against the outside world made of “espoirlessness” and energy without direction. “Baggy white dresses and saggy white suits”; “vestal white”.
Elaine accompagne son mari au collège ex: Elaine accompanies her husband to the experimental college run by Josef Albers; She became friends with John Cage and Merce Cunningham and deepened her friendships with Fuller, Kline, Vicente and Tworkov. Consequences: Birth of a series of biomorphic paintings; lasting friendships with avant-garde figures.
Pendant son séjour, Elaine peint des abs: During his stay, Elaine painted biomorphic abstractions with oil on brown wrapping paper, showing the influence of Willem of Kooning, Arshile Gorky, Miró and Hans Arp, but already marked with the “E de K” seal. oil on brown wrapping paper; rediscovered and exhibited at the Joan Washburn Gallery (recently compared to the editorial) Consequences: Works forgotten and then rediscovered; characteristic of his “scrutation féroce” for the next forty years.
À l'instigation d'André Breton, en super: At the instigation of André Breton, overseeing the construction of the 'Hall of Superstition' in Paris, Kiesler executed his first sculpture, an immense Totem of religions. Totem inspired by a primitive fire device: wooden cross with attached rope Consequences: start of massive production of paint and sculpture in five years
Bolotowsky charge quatre jeunes filles d: Bolotowsky loads four young girls into her tabot and drives them madly through winding roads to places of dream — ornamental lakes, mica mines, peaks. Despite the private torments of each one, they cavalk and pose as he films continuously; The world seems peaceful. Atmosphere: magic, carefree, suspended Issue: rare escape from Ravin's fears
Après condamnation pour vitesse et vagab: After conviction for speed and suspended vagrancy, the battery dies; the same two policemen push the car while one does the lesson on Southern hospitality Atmosphere: grotesque and humiliating, absurd comic Issue: the racial hostility of the South against the college
Wallen griffonne dans ses notes du momen: Wallen scratches in his notes as the situation lacks human satisfactions: we always talk about college, never time to relax between people; His relations with most teachers seemed superficial. Words: "Situation here devoid of enough human satisfactions… always talk about college… There is a shallowness and a superficiality in my relations with most faculty here…" Atmosphere: Solitude within the community, fatigue Issue: Intimate disillusionment that will lead to his proposal and then to his departure
Arrivé trop tôt le matin pour téléphoner: Arrived too early in the morning to call Pat Pearson, he waits for the dawn of the day and decides to change his name: Robert, like his German grandfather, for his new life as artist Atmosphere: night ending, empty station, founding decision taken alone Issue: re-birth of oneself as an artist
Conversation sur les relations économiqu: Conversation on the economic relations of cities with their landscape; Duncan discovers that Olson was already thinking the same thing. Words : Duncan : “That day I talked to him about the economic relation of cities to the surrounding landscape… he'd been thinking about the same thing himself.” Atmosphere : Meeting similar hungry spirits Issue : Birth of a poetic alliance at a distance
Elaine accompagne Bill au collège ; elle: Elaine accompanies Bill to college; She paints biomorphic abstractions on brown paper, meets Cage and Cunningham, deepens her friendships with Fuller, Kline, Vicente and Tworkov. Atmosphere: Experimental school, brief but influential, led by Albers. Issue: Avant-garde emulsion — painting, music, dance, architecture — that marks the career of Elaine.
Wallen soumet sa démission à mi-mars 194: Wallen resigned in mid-March 1947; Levi and Rondthaler urge him to reconsider his decision. “mid-March 1947” formulation Consequences: Wallen instead proposes a redefinition of its role
De retour et désireux d'enseigner à nouv: De back and eager to teach again, Dreier supports the election of Levi as Rector, which forms with Rondthaler the reorganization team. Consequences: fee reform, staff reduction; Albers departure on leave in Mexico.
Alice McCanna Stark écrit que les noirs: Alice McCanna Stark writes that the blacks on campus “auraient aussi bien pu être en prison”: their lives were in danger if they crossed the portal, they could not go to Asheville. Peggy Bennett Cole, back in early 1947, finds “deux jeunes Noirs” who didn't get along and wonders if they didn't feel “en vitrine” permanently. Letter from Stark of 20 March 1968; manuscript by Cole.
Après sa démission de mi-mars et les ins: After his resignation in mid-March and the instances of Levi and Rondthaler, Wallen exposes his turnaround: no longer doing psychology for psychology, moving to “community development”, creating a degree of “community service”, sending students to neighbouring communities. Words: Wallen: he wants to live “comme une personne et non dans l'isolation de sa spécialité”; the Board, in essence: stay and teach exactly that, we will continue to call this psychology Atmosphere: malaise; a permissive offer experienced as a disengagement Issue: Last chance to keep Wallen in college
Le Conseil refuse le renouvellement de N: The Commission denies the renewal of Niebyl (notice dated 27 March 1947). A student petition of 27 March 1947 and a second petition requesting a community meeting; the Council held its meeting on 8 May 1947 and published two notices to the community on 9 May maintaining its prerogatives and claiming to have already weighed the “qualités positives” of Niebyl. Wallen signed the March 27 petition requesting “la discussion la plus complète possible”, without sympathizing with the request to reconsider the reappointment. Consequences: Departure of Niebyl
Arrivés le 30 avril avec un congé sabbat: Arrived on 30 April with an extended sabbatical leave (first visit since the end of the war), they remain a whole semester until the expiry of tourist visas at the end of October. Porset and Guerrero visit the gardens of Barragán. Group photo at Anahuacalli (Rivera Museum, built in black volcanic stone with Juan O'Gorman, still unfinished), around 1947 or 1949. Josef works frantically on “Adobes”: about eighty studies, ten of which remain in Mexico. Letter to Charlot: “je pense que j'aurai fait environ quatre-vingts études”; ten paintings entrusted to Inés Amor Consequences: Sustainable Friendship with Inés Amor
Premier voyage depuis la fin de la guerr: First trip since the end of the war, on extended sabbatical leave: arrival in Mexico City on 30 April, departure at the end of October at the expiration of tourist visas — their longest stay, six full months. Josef writes having made “environ 80 études” of Adobes, 10 of which remained in Mexico; need to paint “sans être dérangé par les obligations du collège” Consequences: Ten Adobe paintings left in Inés Amor
Bulletin du collège (vol. 5, no 4) décri: College Bulletin (Vol. 5, No. 4) describing the three-season farm: winter compost in rectangular piles turned and examined with an “solennité presque morbide”, milking machine, cemented cow stalls, individual drinking cups, freshly painted herses, bright blue wheelbarrow; reduced herd of slaughter, expanded dairy herd; The heifer Guernsey vagabond Junket foils the plans by putting down a black calf of meat breed; 4500 trees planted on the eroded slopes of mountain pasture. 4500 young trees (robin trees, balsam trees, white pines); 8 acres of Bennett land rented in spring oats, barley, clover, lespedeza
Albers, arrivé récemment à Mexico et abs: Albers, who had recently arrived in Mexico City and had been absent from Black Mountain since September 1946, requested that his leave be extended by twelve months. Levi, rector since March 1947, tells him that the year was not easy, that relations within the faculty were rough, that everyone was upset, and that his students would be desperately lost without him. Consequences: Pressure on Albers return
Depuis Mexico, Albers demande une prolon: From Mexico, Albers requests an extension of leave; Levi replies that the year has been rough, that the letter finds all upset, and asks if it knows how much it is wanted and necessary; The students would be desperately lost without him. Words : Levi : “je me demande si vous savez à quel point vous êtes voulu et nécessaire” Atmosphere : tension, call for return, fatigue on both sides Issue : the college breaks apart as its pillar moves away
Les Rice quittent Mt. Pleasant (Caroline: The Rice left Mt. Pleasant (South Caroline) where Frank taught at the College of Charleston, a difficult and lonely year; hosted at Asheville by Nell Rice and Fritz Hansgirg, owner of a Cadillac; Housed in Last Chance. Baggage: summer clothes, baby equipment, Johnny 3 years, Frances 6 months; Train to Asheville.
Exposition internationale du Surréalisme: International exhibition of Surrealism devoted to myth, superstition, magic and occult; reveals the return of the movement to non- clandestine activity, despite bad press and attack by Sartre. July 7 – September 30, 1947 Consequences: William Rubin will see in 1968 the “coup de grâce” of the movement
Un candidat au poste d'enseignant d'hist: A candidate for the position of history teacher, former education and fine arts officer at the Military Government in Germany for a year, speaks in front of the community; His presentation is appreciated but Dreier is troubled by his “objectivité détachée” on denazification and German educational problems. Candidate spent a year at the Military Government in Germany Consequences: Starts the reflection at Dreier on a possible departure in Germany
Un ancien officier du Military Governmen: A former officer of the Military Government in Germany, candidate for the post of history, speaks before the community about the denazification and the problems of German education; Most appreciate, but Dreier is deeply embarrassed by its detached objectivity and confidentially writes to Ise Gropius. Words: Dreier describes “l'objectivité détachée” speaker disturbing; he confides that the idea of going to Germany touched him but that living at ease among hungry people would be almost impossible to him Atmosphere: Fascination of the audience, growing moral discomfort at Dreier Issue: Dreier between the desire to be useful elsewhere and fidelity to a decomposing college
Josef écrit avoir peu voyagé contraireme: Josef writes that they had little travel contrary to their habit in Mexico, painted almost all the time, day and night according to Anni; it describes the colors that lose their identity (green becoming blue, neutral grey becoming purple red), opaque appearing transparent.
Albers écrit à Charlot que les jardins d: Albers writes to Charlot that the gardens of Barragán are “la plus grande architecture de jardins nouvelle que nous ayons jamais vue”; Clara Porset and Xavier Guerrero had taken them there, he and Anni. Letter of 9 September 1947; uncertainty between gardens of Tacubaya and Jardines del Pedregal (started in 1945) Consequences: Years later, Barragán, very selective on the art of his house, would give the compliment
Lettre de Josef à Franz Perdekamp : cont: Letter from Josef to Franz Perdekamp: unlike their Mexican habits, they have travelled little; he paints almost all the time, “jour et nuit” according to Anni, about 70 studies of a single theme since January. about 70 studies since January 1947; “jour et nuit” Consequences: Birth of the Variant/Adobe series, which will exceed two hundred canvases
« The Meaning of Black Mountain » : disc: “The Meaning of Black Mountain”: speech to the entire community during the fall 1947 opening exercises, defining BMC as an experimental college and educational community.
Étudiant du cours expérimental de Gute/S: Student of the experimental course of Gute/Switzer, Huff writes: “My art class is a little puzzling” — one does not paint, one does not draw, one does not burn, on “remplit l'espace” with planes, lines and solids, with as cardboard media, wire and clay.
Lettre à Perdekamp : depuis janvier, un: Letter to Perdekamp: since January, only one theme in 70 studies; Josef describes how colors change each other in proportion and claims to be proud when they lose their identity; He would like to pursue without being disturbed. Words: “I'm especially proud when [I can make] colors lose their identity and become unrecognizable” — “je suis particulièrement fier quand je peux faire perdre aux couleurs leur identité” Atmosphere: Laboratory Excitation Issue: La discovers the power of pure color interaction
Levi ouvre sur Whitehead (300 ans pour l: Levi opens on Whitehead (300 years for the mature university, so 186 years of waiting for BMC), mocks the senility of the major universities, chained Plato, the Empire State Building, Yale and its offices, confesses its concerns about the 90 students, tells the cross-dismissions, and builds its theory of the four dimensions of self. Words: Shaw quote: “La jeunesse est une chose si merveilleuse — c'est une honte qu'elle soit gaspillée sur les jeunes”. Atmosphere: scholarly irony and morning solemnity; Community Gathered Issue: Defining BMC's soul as its growth threatens it
Dans le cours expérimental réorganisé, H: In the reorganized experimental course, Huff and his comrades do not paint or draw: they fill the space with plans, lines and solids of cardboard, wire and clay; He writes his parents his perplexity. Words: “My art class is a little puzzling... we're 'filling space'.” Atmosphere: Perplexity of a student confronted with design pedagogy before Albers. Issue: Yale is working towards the method that Albers, invited in 1948, will come to embody.
Pour accroître l'efficacité, Charles Blo: To increase efficiency, Charles Bloomstein, an accountant (C.P.A.), joins staff to maintain college books and supervise farm, store and workshop accounts.
Première édition de poèmes de M.C. Richa: First edition of poems by M.C. Richards, composed and hand printed by the author, printed 50 copies, sewn under cover of sober rigid paper. “With love to Brunson” signed example. 50 copies, Futura characters, 8vo, rigid sewn cover
Pavia imagine un clubhouse d'artistes su: Pavia imagines an artist clubhouse on the model of Italian and Greek immigrant social clubs, financed by contributions; After abolishing the rule excluding women, Elaine and Mercedes Matter are invited; a former member remembers that one could not keep Elaine away from what she wanted wooden staircase worn in the middle by decades of steps; dust balls and butts in the corners; neon light; wooden folding chairs along the walls Consequences: centre of intellectual life of the New York School
Albers, premier enseignant recruté au co: Albers, the first college-recruited teacher after a career at Bauhaus, offered the summer position to Bill after Mark Tobey's refusal, having seen reproductions of Painting and Orestes in the February issue of Magazine of Art. Consequences: Departure of Kooning for the North Caroline
Chaque matin, Elaine suit le cours de da: Every morning, Elaine takes the two-hour dance class of Merce Cunningham, six days a week, in the college dining room. two hours a day, six days a week
Bill travaille tout l'été sur une seule: Bill works all summer long on a single painting, Asheville, superimposed abstract and almost figurative elements (one eye, one window, a face with a profile) animated with pink and orange, on cardboard. Elaine painted on wrapping paper: 17 abstractions with small rounded shapes on milky background, some in bright colours (pink, orange, turquoise — the spouses probably share the enamel jars), others in discreet neutrals; She's experimenting with Hofmann's push-pull theory. 17 abstractions; cardboard and wrapping paper as supports Consequences: Returned to New York, it stores rolled canvases as a closed chapter; They only reappear after his death at the Benton Gallery (Southampton) and Washburn Gallery (New York).
Trente-cinq ans plus tard, Elaine minimi: Thirty-five years later, Elaine minimizes these canvases: “un hommage à la durabilité de la peinture, rien de plus”. Lawrence Campbell sees “l'optimisme triomphant de l'art abstrait des années 40” and influences of Gorky, pre-Columbian and Amerindian art; The New York Times notes a resemblance of “étrangement similaire” to Bill's early 1990s canvases (exaggeration according to Curtis, the structure of Elaine being more tightened).
En geste d'adieu, Elaine et un groupe d': In gesture of farewell, Elaine and a group of students avenged themselves from a neighbor who had accused them of damaging his expensive grass by adorning his lawn with tens of hundred brilliant. tens of cents
La fête finale de l'été est un bal où El: La Summer Final Party is a ball where Elaine waltzes with Fuller, telling her that it is “une performeuse formidable au gramme près”.
À la fin de la session, Elaine reste sur: At the end of the session, Elaine remains on site while Bill returns to New York with his student Pat Passlof.
Cet automne-là, Bill peint Woman : figur: That autumn Bill painted Woman: figure with apparent teeth, giant eye, marked nostrils, asymmetrical arms and breasts, long blonde hair; On the left, a star gaud at eleven points approaches his raised face; On the right, the pale outline of a house. 11-point yellow star Consequences: The first of a series of female figures that are increasingly exaggerated.
Après une soirée trop bruyante à son goû: After a night too noisy to his liking, Bill takes Elaine on a country road; Total silence and starry vault panic: “Retournons à la fête. L'univers me fout le trac.” Consequences: Curtis suggests (assumption) a link between this experience and Woman's giant star.
Elaine, lasse des nuits de peinture de B: Elaine, weary of Bill's nights of painting (she thinks that we paint the day and go out for fun in the evening, according to her brother Conrad), multiplies outings — often at the Cedar Tavern with Frankenthaler, Greenberg, the Phillips — and an intimate affair with Charlie Egan, Bill's merchant, who marries a woman recently met but continues with his wife's agreement. Betsy Egan surprises Bill drummer on a closed bedroom door where are Elaine and Charlie.
Bill commence une liaison avec Mary Abbo: Bill began an affair with Mary Abbott, a lively and pretty abstract painter, separated from her husband for two years; he multiplies occasional connections and gives each one a particular bell ringing code for his workshop. one bell code per mistress
L'assistante éditoriale Arb ayant rappor: As the editorial assistant Arb reported to Hess a conversation where Elaine criticized the ignorance of contemporary art writers, Hess invited him to the office; it starts with six “test reviews”, including one on the exhibition Giacometti at the Pierre Matisse gallery, while Giacometti is unknown in America six essay reviews; Giacometti unknown in the United States early 1948; the favorable report of Hess not yet published Consequences: beginning of his career of criticism, lasting influence in the magazine
Autour de la première exposition de Bill: Around Bill's first exhibition, the couple spends a weekend in the tiny farm of Pollock and Krasner; A few months later, at an evening at Clement Greenberg, Krasner launched Elaine: “Tu as le cœur du tigre” — Elaine chooses to see a compliment, “mais c'était une attaque”. Consequences: Still tense relations between the two women, wives of the two rivals of American painting
Elaine et Bill visitent pour la première: Elaine and Bill visit Pollock and Krasner's home for the first time. Fireplace Road, hamlet of The Springs Consequences: Initiate stormy relationships between the two rival pairs of American painting.
Le sculpteur Peter Grippe recommande à J: The sculptor Peter Grippe recommends to Josef Albers Bill of Kooning, whom he describes as “un peintre qui crève de faim”, for the summer session. Grippe Formula: “a painter who is starving” Consequences: Bill (and Elaine) spend summer 1948 at Black Mountain.
Eva Diaz donne la hauteur du dôme constr: Eva Diaz gives the height of the dome built with the students; Martin Duberman (who interviewed Fuller in 1969) indicated that he had to be 50 feet tall. Both measures diverge. Fifty feet according to Duberman/Fuller 1969
Elaine donne habituellement le chiffre d: Elaine usually gives the figure of five dollars per critic, but tells Gruen four dollars; Hess reportedly entrusted him with “test” reviews, including one on Giacometti and one on Misha Reznikoff's (“j'ai été assez cinglante”) paintings, which have not been found since. $4 or $5 (contest); critical test on Giacometti, Reznikoff Consequences: Starts of Elaine as a critic.
L'auteure affirme, en corrigeant Gail Le: The author claims, by correcting Gail Levin, that Kooning was at Black Mountain during the summer of 1948, not visiting Lee Krasner as Levin was at that summer. Consequences: Allows you to date the visit to Krasner at another time
Elaine rencontre John Droll au collège,: Elaine meets John Droll at the college, where he is a student during the summer session 1948.
Cage l'entraîne dans le Satie Festival,: Cage trains him in the Satie Festival, a radically new experience; its exhilarating presence rips the community apart into two musical camps; At the table, people stand up and make statements about the very existence of music; tensions last all summer; for Wood, time to question the musical status quo and the dominance of European culture. Standing statements at the table Consequences: Durable liberating effect on American music at the college.
Pendant l'institut d'été 1948, Wood suit: During the Summer Institute 1948, Wood took a color course of Albers that captured her more than almost everything she had done; years later she made collages derived from these concepts. Consequences: Subsequent collages.
Après son départ et une courte période d: After her departure and a short period of internal research, she writes for local newspapers; After her marriage to Jonathan Aley in 1948, she worked seven years at New York for Look magazine; in the mid 1950s children arrived. She credits BMC with a sustainable liberal vision, a lesser awe of professional intellect, an eye for design via Albers. Seven years at Look, marriage in 1948
Été 1948 : Fuller vient bâtir un dôme gé: Summer 1948: Fuller builds a geodetic dome with its students from the Chicago Institute of Design (including Jonathan Williams); Cage mounts a Satie festival and asks Richards to translate The Mistress Trap. Penn shows, Fuller plays Baron Médusa, Elaine by Kooning his daughter, Cunningham dances the interludes of the mechanical monkey, Cage on the piano. Full Casting of Satie's piece
Lors d'une réunion communautaire, quelqu: At a community meeting, someone proposes a collective sacrifice for the victims of war (national effort to rescue Europe); Instead of an individual gift box, we think collective sacrifice. Speech on moral responsibility and universal guilt; Ted Ronthaler, a non-smoker, proposes that everyone give up smoking; He was told that he could give up milk rather than tobacco. Finally, motion passed by acclamation: replace dinner with boiled mush one day a week and give the difference. Dissident voices arise: the motion was swept away by a wave of sentiment making rational objection impossible; American Jews blame the Europeans of the college for projecting their guilt for having escaped the fate of their own. The Community Council publishes a note in the canteen: two nights a week the dessert will be abolished and the savings paid to the relief fund; those who do not want to participate are asked to sign. Signatories: a few chronic challengers of authority (Krikorian, Brody, Alice Jackson, Alex Parker) and Willy Joseph, who liked ice cream with his dinner. For days, everyone is looking for a sign. In the evening, a “non-bouillie” line forms towards the kitchen, welcomed by the cooks; Some non-signors eat among the rustlers and “font des convertis”. After several weeks, cooks who were over-prepared for two menus removed the boil one evening: the end of the war. To help Europe, the author remembers nothing more — he thinks nothing has happened. Note displayed in the dining room table; one day a week of boiling instead of dinner; double line to the kitchen; two daily menus for cooks. Consequences: End of sacrifice by the fatigue of the cooks; Then nothing happened for European Relief, according to the author.
