Mynheer propose, sur le modèle de Remus: Mynheer proposes, on the model of Remus killed by his brother to give a beginning to Rome, to immolate a member of the group and to plow his skull crushed in the field: death would justify the city. Silence, hostile eyes; Droyt asks furiously why his father is exempt; Horatio, in tears, evokes Raymond his only friend killed at the time of the Grand Piano, his chosen father and Arthur dead during the war, and refuses to lose Piet Duyck — he starts screaming in a terrible way; Minetta returns the situation with spirit: dead, she would haunt the city forever, “vous ne pourrez plus vous débarrasser de moi”; People laugh by showing their teeth. Mynheer licks his lips, sighs the black stone that fills the palm, raises the forearm to throw it; All recede by shouting Consequences: no sacrifice accomplished; voltage rises
Un grand roux inconnu de tous, refusant: A great redhead unknown to all, refusing to say his name or the friend who sends him, presents himself as the third displaced of the joke of Harry Tyler (“l'Afrique du Sud — si loin de quoi ?”) who came to fulfill the role of the Foreigner. He explains changing masks every two days to remain mysterious to children; he displays a mask under which his red hair is seen; he declines to be Jewish (“le Juif est l'Extérieur, le Bouc émissaire ; moi je suis l'Étranger”); It flows a number of intertwined fingers on numbers (22, 33, 55, 66). In the evening, drunk, he becomes sinister: “cherchards de communauté, trouillards de la mort”, refuses to leave when asked. a mask brought into his pocket; he drank a lot; “Nobody invited you. Why don't you go away?” — “Hell, I'll go away! Can you make me?” Consequences: it hangs where it has no place, fulfilling its role
Dans l'obscurité, un visage éclairé à la: In the darkness, a lighted face with a flashlight, a bell sounds: everyone utters his naked hatred — children who imprison, unmet sexual demands, friends who choose their hour badly, desirable strangers who do not bind themselves, of themselves cowardly, poor clothes, those who chew apples too loudly, those who beat children, of the world order. The narrator adds that he hates his poetic art, because to be the poet he had to be himself and lead the miserable life he leads. La bell rings twelve strokes; One calls it to the Creator Spirit, the only sense of a universe that otherwise “ne se recommande pas sérieusement”. creased eyes, projected jaw; a flashlight; a bell ringing twelve blows Consequences: the community is finally founded in the shared confession of hatred
Après les déclarations de haine, quelqu': After the hate speech, someone proposes to turn off and sleep. Mynheer says there's enough hate to cement “relations communautaires”. Each one delivers one last thought: Lothair removes the illusion of man to the “désirs simples”; The dancer Rosalind mocks the artist who weeps about life sacrificed at work. The first to fall asleep is “le Stranger professionnel”, which snores in confidence; Rosalind falls asleep in the middle of the narrator's protest Consequences: the “existe, inutile de la prouver” community; fully trained personalities (mothers, fathers, teachers, seducers, scapegoats)
À l'automne 1948, Elaine de Kooning lit: In the fall of 1948, Elaine of Kooning read Kierkegaard, forerunner of existentialism, to her husband Bill; She perceives an affinity between Bill's taste for obstinate perseverance and Kierkegaard's exaltation, as well as between Bill and K's ordinary heroes. Consequences: Kierkegaard becomes an intimate reference to the painter; he will later re-use the title Fear and Trembling
Pat Passlof étudie avec de Kooning en 19: Pat Passlof studied with Kooning in 1948; She will testify in 1989 in Art Journal.
Lors de son premier été à Black Mountain: In its first summer at Black Mountain, Fuller tried unsuccessfully to assemble a geodetic dome. Geodesics defined as arcs of large circles Consequences: He recovered thanks to the innovations of student Kenneth Snelson in “tensegrity”
Les innovations de l'étudiant en sculptu: The Kenneth Snelson sculpture student's innovations in “tensegrity” (discontinuous compression, continuous tension) are reorienting Fuller from his “géométrie énergétique”. Discontinuous compression and continuous tension; Physical models of tight spheres Consequences: The geodetic dome, prototyped with tensegrity, becomes the matrix of the holistic plane of Fuller
Tirage argentique de Cage au collège en: Silver print of Cage at college in 1948 by Kalischer. gelatin silver print
À la fin des années 1940, Cage rencontre: In the late 1940s, Cage met resistance as a composer (less as a prepared piano performer). Albers offered him a teaching position for the summer session 1948 — his first musical composition position. Cage is “ravi”. prepared piano: objects inserted between strings, percussive play Consequences: First Cage composition teaching
Cage joue exclusivement l'œuvre de Satie: Cage exclusively plays Satie's work all summer instead of brushing a panorama of the “musique moderne en général”; An introductory speech denouncing Beethoven's harmonic tradition in favor of rhythm and duration at Satie particularly angers German migrants. Consequences: Durable resentment against Cage in college
Production universellement admirée de la: Universally admired production of Satie's long neglected play, translated that summer by Mary Caroline Richards. Arthur Penn directs: Fuller plays Baron Medusa, Elaine by Kooning his daughter Frisette, Cunningham the mechanical monkey Jonas. Decors and accessories by Fuller, Willem and Elaine from Kooning, and students Ruth Asawa and Ray Johnson. accessories: velvet foot stool with giant human feet, monumental thermometer with an oversized paper knot, “bureau du baron” painted in trompe-l'oeil on an “technique secrète de guilde” Elaine Kooning says he learned teen in Holland, surrounded by huge triangles on four sides around his feet (eye club with tetrahedrons of Fuller) Consequences: Renewal of the experimental theatre tradition of the college, dormant since the departure of Schawinsky in 1938
Lors de son premier été à Black Mountain: During its first summer at Black Mountain, Cage remembers that it “voyait eye-to-eye” with Albers and that their conversations were agreed, despite a generation of deviations. Consequences: As soon as Cage introduces chance into his practice, they will be in permanent disagreement
En travaillant la Deuxième Sonate pour p: By working on Boulez's Second Piano Sonata (1948), Tudor confesses to Richards that his difficulties do not relate to notes but to music; To understand, he read the sources of Boulez: Mallarmé and Artaud. Quote from Tudor: he had “pas de problèmes avec les notes, mais avec la musique”. Consequences: Richards discovers Artaud by Tudor.
Fuller enseigne à l'été 1948 un cours qu: Fuller teaches in the summer of 1948 a course which he first entitled “comprehensive design”; He then refined his conception of experimentation as a test for completely rethinking the post-war technocratic society. he writes the expression for the first time as the title of the course Consequences: Third model of experimentation in college, after Albers and Cage
Fuller forge la formule « comprehensive: Fuller forges the “comprehensive design” formula as the title of the course he teaches at the college during the summer session 1948; he then refines it during his summers at Black Mountain Consequences: La formula becomes the heart of his theory of experimentation as total design
Albers invite Fuller à enseigner à la se: Albers invites Fuller to teach at the summer session 1948; Fuller is a last-minute substitution for the architect of Harvard Bertrand Goldberg, a former student of Bauhaus, the faculty having received several refusals from too busy candidates Consequences: Beginning of two decisive summers for Fuller and for the rhetoric of experimentation at the college
Un article de Fortune au printemps 1948: An article from Fortune in the spring of 1948 revealed the collapse of the Wichita House's mass production plans; the invitation of Black Mountain closely follows this publication Consequences: Fuller arrives at the college in full notoriety of failure
Un profil de Fuller proposé pour Science: A profile of Fuller proposed for Science Illustrated generates internal queries asking to include the reasons for the failures of its projects and why it “ne va jamais au bout des choses” Consequences: Illustration of the discredit of Fuller on the eve of Black Mountain
Fuller accepte sa toute première commiss: Fuller accepted his very first teaching commission in the summer of 1948, a refuge while his career suffered setbacks and criticisms. Consequences: Beginning of his involvement with the college and his relationship to pedagogy.
À son arrivée en 1948, Fuller rencontre: Upon his arrival in 1948, Fuller met the student in sculpture Kenneth Snelson, excited by the new instructor's ideas. Consequences: Collaboration that leads to tenegrity.
Chaque matin de l'été 1948, Fuller, Cage: Every morning in the summer of 1948, Fuller, Cage and Cunningham together take breakfast outside under the trees and elaborate by having fun with the scheme of an “finishing school”: a school-caravan traveling from city to city, which “finirait” everything — that is, would break all conventional approaches to the school. Daily breakfast in the open air under the trees Consequences: Common formulation of a test model as an act of radical transformation, opposed to the systematic method of Albers.
École « largement germanique » : la dévo: “largement germanique” School: the devotion of Cage to Satie irritates. Albers, to soothe, requires a talk from Cage before each concert. In the middle of the session, Cage made a longer lecture than others where, to expose the anti-Beethovenian views of Satie, it “dénonce Beethoven”: effect “comme une bombe tombant sur l'endroit”. Consequences: A memorable tension between Cage and the German music culture of the college
La première tentative d'assemblage d'un: La first attempt to assemble a geodetic dome by Fuller to the college fails; he would then have pronounced the sentence reported (see quotations). Consequences: Fuller perseveres and returns in the summer of 1949 with reinforced materials (known elsewhere).
Cours d'été 1948 au collège, version rem: Summer 1948 class at the College, revised version at the Institute of Design from 4 October 1948 to 29 January 1949; the synopsis becomes the “Comprehensive Designing” test (1963). Synopsis dated “Oct. 4, '48 – Jan. 29, '49”, pp 1-1h, Fuller Papers. Consequences: La “design complet” method enters college.
Hansgirg suggère d'acquérir deux des str: Hansgirg suggests acquiring two of the Fuller structures (Wichita/Dymaxion houses) for campus, after the May 1948 Fortune article “What Became of the Fuller House”. Consequences: Project not completed (domes built instead).
Selon Snelson, Fuller arrive pour la ses: According to Snelson, Fuller arrives for the summer session 1948 in place of an architectural teacher who withdrew at the last moment; It's his first teaching position. Consequences: Beginning of the Fuller-Snelson relationship and legendary summer 1948 (Cage, Cunningham, Kooning...).
Selon l'étudiant en sculpture Kenneth Sn: According to the Kenneth Snelson sculpture student, Fuller arrives for the summer session as a replacement for an architectural teacher who withdrew at the last minute; It's his first teaching position. Consequences: decisive encounter with Snelson and Elaine of Kooning
Cinq ans après son mariage avec Willem d: Five years after her marriage to Willem from Kooning, Elaine begins to publish regularly in ARTnews, where Thomas Hess will be editor-in-chief. Consequences: She actively contributes to her husband's reputation and to the public image of the couple.
L'exposition de peintures en noir et bla: The exhibition of black and white paintings establishes the preeminence of Kooning as an abstract painter. Consequences: Consolidated as a major figure of the New York avant-garde
Elaine déclare à Renee Arb, qui rendait: Elaine tells Renee Arb, who reported on Bill's first personal exhibition at the Egan Gallery, that Art News critics are amateurs, made by art historians who know nothing about art. Renee repeats the remark to Tom Hess, who answers: “Tell her to come in and see me”. As he went to the office, he entrusted him with five exhibitions; Four artists seem mediocre or dreadful to her, the fifth is Alberto Giacometti, on whom she writes a passionate and authorized critique: the exhibition seems to be the output of a civilization more than the work of a single man. Bill, upset, walks out of the gallery, walks around the block to calm down, then comes back to study the work more closely. Hess hires him as an associate editorial and gives him a list of twenty exhibitions to chronicle for the issue of the month. Five exhibitions and then twenty; magazine policy: situating the artist, describing the work, judging it; fee: $2 per critic, whether she makes two sentences or two hundred words. Consequences: Beginning of a regular career as an art critic; Report of the founder Giacometti.
Elaine peint en 1948, au « collège innov: Elaine painted in 1948, at “collège innovant” Black Mountain, its Black Mountain series, where the inspiration of Arshile Gorky on his painting is the deepest. Consequences: La Black Mountain series becomes a major set of his work.
1948 est l'année où Rothko « entre dans: 1948 is the year in which Rothko “entre dans son Présent”: previous work no longer represents it as we now know it. Consequences: Beginning of the classic period of large rectangular canvases.
Pollock adresse à Gorky des commentaires: Pollock gives Gorky unpleasant comments about his painting; Gorky, smiling dangerously, pulls out a pencil from one pocket and a prank from the other and, without leaving Pollock's eyes, slowly sharpens the mine on one inch. Gorky replica: “Pardon me, Mr. Pollock, you and I are different kinds of artists”; Pollock, titubating a little, responds with a cunning smile and approved and turns away, satisfied
Au printemps 1948, Greenberg organise un: In the spring of 1948, Greenberg organized a cocktail to present Leo Castelli to American artists: Gorky, Pollock, Smith, Kline, Kooning — the five future topics of “Strokes of Genius”. Consequences: symbolic meeting of the five artists of the future series
Deux semaines après Noël, chute brutale: Two weeks after Christmas, the lake freezes with a sudden drop in temperature; everyone slides and pulls sledges; the group of the daycare walk on chairs and laundry baths; Natasha Goldowsky, former ballet dancer physicist, exuberant star. Skates in turn.
Hess prend la direction d'Art News, essa: Hess takes over the direction of Art News, trying to appear neutral in the rivalry of Kooning–Pollock, which its connection with Elaine and hiring them compromise. Consequences: Elaine enters the Art News editorial
Après une fête trop bruyante, Bill entra: After a noisy party, Bill drives Elaine on a country road; absolute silence and the vault of stars crush it; He breaks his peace and wants to go back. Words : Bill : “Retournons à la fête. L'univers me fout le trac.” Atmosphere : total darkness, silence, dome of stars Issue : Reveal the fear of emptiness under the mask of the feaster ; illuminate the giant star of Woman.
Après trois mois, Frankfurter encore dub: After three months, Frankfurter again dubitative accuses him of writing only favorable criticisms; it retorts: “That's disgusting, isn't it”, and exits from the office Words: “C'est dégoûtant, n'est-ce pas”; on favoritism: “Ils étaient tous mes amis. Je connais tout le monde. Aucun favoritisme possible” Atmosphere: dry confrontation, theatrical release Issue: his conception of criticism against editorial authority
Pendant le Satie Festival, les convives: During the Satie Festival, guests rise and proclaim their positions on the very existence of music; The community splits into two camps for the whole summer Atmosphere: Electricity, excitement, quarrel Issue: Aesthetic battle for the soul of the college
Une ou deux tables très bruyantes et joy: One or two very noisy and joyful tables; to each, two or three people who are stiff and mute; the unboiled line winds towards the kitchen, served by the cooks; Some conscientious people wear their plates in mushers to win converts. Atmosphere: Theatre of ideologies at fixed time, trays as flags. Issue: La community discovers live that it is not unanimous — and that unanimity is not decreed.
Proposition de sacrifice collectif pour: Proposal for a collective sacrifice for European relief; speech on moral responsibility and universal guilt; zealous chain suggestions; Rondthaler proposes to stop smoking; voice suggesting that he would rather give up milk; final motion: weekly boiled, adopted by acclamation, meeting adjourned; the half-dissidents barely articulated remain in the room. Words: Let Ronthaler give up milk instead of tobacco; talk about universal guilt towards the persecuted. Atmosphere: A wave of moral fervour making rational objection impossible. Issue: Utopia takes its feet in its own virtue: dictated good becomes ultimatum.
Penn, inquiet que personne ne vienne aux: Penn, worried that no one would come to the tests, insisted on his roommate; Stiles reads from the Saroyan, gets a role in the Stein Words: Penn on Liliom: your reading is 'hammy', but I'll give you a boost. Atmosphere: chamber complicity, youth anxiety of the director Issue: launch the theatrical project
Sur un banc, la blonde se demande ce que: On a bench, the blonde wonders what it's like to be queen; arrive two kings with crowns of paper and axes of cardboard that invite him to choose; She doesn't care; They kill each other; It straightens, head high: kings are useless Words: 'I am Phillip Hall, and that is all' / 'All you have to do is to be first, and then you are a King' / 'I am a Queen; I can tell by feeling. It is so lovingly to be a Queen.' Atmosphere: children's play, triumph 'with brilliance' Issue: the only Stiles actor triumph
Après l'exposition vide, une lettre d'un: After the empty exhibition, a letter from a stranger — Albers, whose name tells them only Bauhaus — offers $200, board, train for two and one studio each; They budget: $70 for Bill's workshop, $36 for the flat, $94 left; Rejoicing. Atmosphere: Du desperation in euphoria: “tous nos problèmes étaient résolus” Issue: The invitation that changes an artistic trajectory
1 h 30 de manipulations stériles par les: 0130 hours of sterile handling by engineers; Bill enters, weighs, studies, slams both pieces: perfect cube. Fuller nods, no surprise. Words: Bill later: he sought the least logical path Atmosphere: amused astonishment Issue: The artist's intuition against the logic of engineers
Jour de pluie ; l'école entière vient ri: Day of rain; the whole school is stinging; the fully assembled dome remains flat on the grass; Yet all know that he is theoretically brilliant. Words : Bucky : “Mettons-le quand même ensemble. On ne connaît jamais les voies du Tout-Puissant.” Atmosphere : rain, collective derision, faith intact of Fuller Issue : Public failure of a great idea
De nombreuses répétitions nécessaires po: De many rehearsals necessary to not burst laughing in front of the lazzi of Fuller; Penn extracted from total amateur characters; making Bucky's gown and costume. Atmosphere: Laughter, Crafts, Collective Creativity Issue: Engineering genius revealed actor
Albers aborde Bill à la fin de l'été : d: Albers approaches Bill at the end of the summer: ten students, six go to New York in September, does he know? Bill answered straight away that he told them to drop out of school, take a studio and paint Words: Albers: “Tu avais dix étudiants. Six quittent le collège pour New York en septembre. Est-ce que tu en sais quelque chose ?” Bill: “Bien sûr. Je leur ai dit que s'ils voulaient être artistes, ils devaient quitter l'école, venir à New York, prendre un studio et se mettre à peindre.” Atmosphere: tense and then relaxed; Albers doesn't seem to take it badly The game: two conceptions of the artist's formation; oracle of the future (Yale)
Table du trésorier ; Bobby taquine Oates: Treasurer's table; Bobby teases Oates on his Chinese painting and suggests the ascetical painter of the misty mountains; Oates's response raises Mark, bypasses the table and kisses her Words: Bobby, nicely mocking, proposes to go to the mountains painting mist landscapes in Ascetics Atmosphere: warm welcome, emotion of the new Issue: everything can happen here, and I can be in it
Bill, dégoûté de la foule, propose une m: Bill, disgusted with the crowd, offers a walk; ten minutes and no more light from the college; velvety blackness, almost terrifying silence, multitude of stars; Then Bill wants to go home Words : Bill : “Retournons à la fête. L'univers me donne la chair de poule.” Atmosphere : starry immensity, cosmic fear Issue : the painter facing the void
Des étudiants entreprennent de tanner un: Students undertake to tan an entire farm skin with a manual but without the ingredients or tools; every day the smell worsened; They scoop valiantly; the skin is never playable and ends up as an Atmosphere sketch accessory: More and more powerful and nauseat; small group game application Issue: Craft enthusiasm against recalcitrant matter
Pendant les numéros de danse, une équipe: During the dance numbers, a team runs the relaxed drums to the kitchen, holds them above the stoves, gives small blows, hears the note rising, brings back the instrument for the following number — unrecognized heroes of the Atmosphere program: Race, heat of the stoves, small sound plinks Issue: The show continues thanks to an invisible logistics
Fuller attrape Davidoff dans le couloir,: Fuller catches Davidoff in the hallway, pulls it in a dark closet, points with enthusiasm a matter that shines in the dark; He would have caught the first come to share his discovery Words: You must definitely come and see something Atmosphere: Obscurity, absolute childish joy
Après les provocations anti-Beethoven de: After the anti-Beethoven provocations of Cage, Bodky reacts gently during an evening by a rather spiritual pastiche of Satie at the piano Atmosphere: Party atmosphere, elegant response Issue: Beethoven/Satie aesthetic war in minor
Un étudiant demande à de Kooning à quoi: A student asks Kooning what he is thinking by painting; it designates a canvas and explains that it comes from the sight of a woman's heel in an open shoe, seen from behind: the flesh of the heel overflowing the edges of the sole
Penn affiche l'annonce d'une classe de j: Penn displays the announcement of a game class twice a week; He expects few people and sees twenty to thirty people disembark, including the three professors he studies with himself. Words: Penn: “I just simply didn't know very much... I really hadn't read properly almost anything” — I really didn't know anything, I hadn't read anything seriously Atmosphere: Astonishment and collective momentum Issue: A 24-year-old student becomes the teacher of his own teachers
Le conflit sur la reprise des pièces est: The conflict over the resumption of coins is played in class; initial vote 11 in favour, 1 against — the tenacious opponent holds the main role; Wallen launches the task: to develop an action that satisfies the one as much as the eleven; the class moves the debate and invents the show-demonstration; Wallen warns against imposing the solution on the rest of the troupe; the cast adopts a modified version. Words: Actors: “We've given the plays already... we work for ourselves” — we have already given the pieces, we are working for ourselves Atmosphere: Tension, then inventiveness and collective relief Issue: Consensus at eleven against one: community democracy at the test of one man
Version hostile : Penn entretient délibé: Hostile version: Penn deliberately maintains the love of a fragile student to deepen her game, then tells her a cold farewell after the last — she approaches the breakdown. Favourable version: before him, she was only an “nebbish, un protoplasme palpitant”, and the game flourished; Penn only acted as a good manager. Words: Defender of Penn: she “blossomed into a beautiful human being” — she grew into a magnificent human being Atmosphere: Rumeurs, camps, reputation in play Issue: The psychological price of Stanislavsky method applied to amateurs
Les étudiants dénoncent le projet comme: Students denounce the project as a barracks or beach house, challenge its “fonctionnalisme”, require small dormitories of ten to fourteen people, and present their own plans. Words: Denunciation of building “plus propre à une caserne ou une maison de plage qu'à un dortoir”, disagrees with “l'aversion connue de Black Mountain pour les affaires de masse”. Atmosphere: Polemic, engagement. Issue: Test the real power of students against the Council and teachers.
Lippold, refusé faute d'argent et de log: Lippold, refused for lack of money and housing, writes that he bought an old hearse: transport for wife and two children, dormer on the spot, for the plumbing of the college; He's offering a talk on Rilke. Cage bid by night telegram: the hearse has been tested to sleep. Words: Cage: “ils ont testé leur corbillard pour dormir et cela fonctionne”; “je n'ai pas mentionné tous les nombreux autres qui veulent aussi venir” Atmosphere: Tragi-comique, joyous poverty of New York artists Issue: Allowing a family without a penny to enter a college without a penny
Deux semaines après son arrivée, Droll e: Two weeks after his arrival, Droll in rolled sandals and khakis begins to understand the conversations — until that night when Fuller explains to him that holding in a certain way can feel the earth moving. Words: Fuller: If you stand in a certain way, you can feel the earth turning Atmosphere: Starry night, vertigo of conversion Issue: The intimate swing of a boy from the military academy
Au déjeuner, Levi fait tinter son verre: At lunch, Levi makes her drink tinter; serious, it announces an insoluble split of the faculty and proposes, as rector, a duel to death: the Bethovenians armed with cold wiener schnitzel, the satists of crackers Suzette flaming, in the kitchen. A general food battle breaks out. Words: Levi says that only unprecedented means can solve an unprecedented crisis Atmosphere: Serious-imperturbable Levi, crazy laugh, flying food Issue: Defusing the absurd quarrel Cage/Bodky
Aux répétitions ouvertes, très fréquenté: At the open rehearsals, very frequented that day, Fuller confesses to Penn his fear of “se rendre ridicule”. Penn improvises a series of exercises where both jump, laugh artificially, roll on the ground; exercise becomes fun, then liberating, then inventive; Fuller flourishes. Words: Fuller: he's afraid of “se rendre bêtement ridicule” Atmosphere: Initial fun, joyous madness, liberation Issue: Psychological levier: making Fuller feel that ridicule is not mortal
Il demande à chacun ce qu'il a lu l'été: He asks everyone what he read in the summer; each title is condemned to eighteen, twenty-one or twenty-four years and now recognized terrible. Martha says it's read all Proust “parce que c'était là”. Later, in an oral presentation about Madame Bovary, where she regretted that Emma had married “par convoitise charnelle”, he replied with the tac. Words: “My dear Miss Rittenhouse, for what reasons do you intend to marry?” (“Ma chère Mlle Rittenhouse, pour quelles raisons comptez-vous vous marier ?”) Atmosphere: Provocation, reciprocal insolence, war of respectivities Issue: Who dominates the class: the master or students
Chaque soir, restes de peinture jetés à: Every evening, remains of paint thrown at the trowel on the canvas of Hebei's room; at the end of the year, covered canvas, signed “Anonymous Blotch”, hung; Some seriously examine, Bolotowsky identifies each pallet and laughs, the dupes feel humiliated, Bolotowsky makes it a theoretical defense of chance to enrag Albers. Words : Bolotowsky : “He started it and I kept it up” (“C'est lui qui a commencé, j'ai continué”) Atmosphere : Workshop stuff, malaise of duper spectators Issue : La joke as a weapon in the war of the “standards”
Moins de deux semaines après son arrivée: Less than two weeks after his arrival, Dahlberg declares that he can no longer do so; Albers, very kind, begs him to stay; He refuses inside: “Que les étudiants se défient entre eux, je m'en vais” — and leaves the same day. He'll get Olson as a replacement. Words: “Albers was very kind and beseeched me to remain” Atmosphere: Exhaustion, courteous agitation Issue: College loses its literature teacher — and wins Olson
Deux étudiants non-artistes découverts d: Two non-artist students discovered sleeping together one night in the Studies Building; Albers seeks to expel them; the girl threatens to post a medical certificate attesting that she is virgo intacta; Both finally stay. Atmosphere: Sexual Scandal, a duel of authority and absurdity Issue: The moral authority of challenged Albers
La famille Lippold arrive dans un vieux: La Lippold family arrives in an old black hearse; Fuller, delighted, boasts classic columns and large windows; Richards lends ten cents for kids' ice cream. Words: Fuller: “a beautiful old motor hearse… Beautiful black classical columns and great glass windows” Atmosphere: Poor Gaiety, Mutual Assistance, Bohemian Folklore Issue: La college poverty at the very moment when the most famous summer arrives (Cage, Cunningham, Fuller)
Cage, à table, déclare que Beethoven s'e: Cage, at the table, states that Beethoven was wrong and that his influence was deadly for music; it opposes Satie and Webern which structure by durations; Bodky, outraged, speaks of desecration; The argument becomes a verbal duel. Words: Cage: “Beethoven était dans l'erreur… il a échoué la musique sur une île de décadence”; Bodky sees a “desecration” Atmosphere: sudden tension around the table, anger of the traditional music man Issue: the old musical world against the avant-garde, in the presence of students
Pendant l'exposition, Elaine et Egan ray: During the exhibition, Elaine and Egan radiate together at the bar; Bill, vaulted on a glass, turns his back and lifts his shoulders, as he has always done for the lovers of Elaine and for the women who left him. Atmosphere: smoke, ostensible and visible indifference of all Issue: the bet of the couple: infidelity as a strategy of glory
Ses moqueries sur les comptes rendus d'A: His mockery of Art News reports being reported to him, Hess, half-serious half-amused, asks her if she thinks she can do better; without hesitation, she takes up the challenge. Words: “écrites par des étudiants en histoire de l'art qui n'ont jamais rien regardé” critics Atmosphere: provocation and aplomb Issue: entry of Elaine into critical institution
Soirée très arrosée ; Betsy, jalouse de: Very watered evening; Betsy, jealous of everything at Elaine, defies it with the arm; elbows squarely placed on the table, hands tight; lots of grunts and breath; draw; The two women fall in love with each other. Words: Elaine laughter attack, “roaring into battle” Atmosphere: collective drunkenness, betting artists' audience, comic turn in reconciliation Issue: spousal jealousy transformed into complicity
Goodman expose Kafka devant un auditoire: Goodman exposes Kafka to a student audience, mostly G.I. bill-funded veterans; The audience frantically protest that Kafka is psychotic and unrelated to reality; Goodman notes the irony: these men lived a part of the Trial and then wander even under the Castle. Words: Students: Kafka is psychotic, you must not pay attention to him, he has no connection to reality. Albers explique le système alimentaire :: Albers explains the food system: no choice, everyone eats the same, no waste. Today's dish: sausage salad and bananas. Bill: “Looks like something Elaine would make”, mutual compliment with Albers. Bill eats two bowls of soup first to treat the salad as dessert. Meals announced by a ringing bell; meet at 6 p.m.
Assis sur le dock, ils ignorent la cloch: Sitting on the dock, they ignore the bell by laughing (Elaine: “Pavlov's dogs”), arrive 20 minutes later and find the room empty: each rest has disappeared. So they sprint to the sound of the bell. Consequences: Never arrive late at a meal again
Certains membres du corps enseignant abs: Some members of the teaching staff absent from the festival — second index of open and veiled hostilities that form an oppressive countercurrent all summer.
Elaine retient sans effort tous leurs no: Elaine keeps all their names effortlessly, forgetting those of the teaching staff.
74 étudiants d'été (environ la moitié no: 74 summer students (about half new). Guests: Peter Grippe (sculpture), Richard Lischer (carpentry), Winslow Ames (history of print in July, director of the Springfield Museum of Art, Missouri), Beaumont Newhall (3rd summer, completes his History of Photography), Charles Burchard (architecture in August, Harvard School of Design), Erwin Bodky (pianist-clavesticist, “Développement de la musique de clavier” and “Les sonates de Beethoven” — source of a notable confusion with Cage), Edgar Kaufman Jr. (industrial design, MoMA), Isaac Rosenfeld (Tolstoy and “creative writing”, which according to Kazin “méprisait” Black Mountain). Albers signs Color and Design; Anni Albers and Trude Guermonp the weaving. 74 students; wages: accommodation and food, $100 travel, $25 per week
Droll, sorti de la Valley Forge Military: Droll, released from the Valley Forge Military Academy after two years at Michigan State College, arrives at the end of June among some 40 new students and suffers an immediate shock: he has never heard of Cage, Cunningham, Kooning or Fuller, and has never seen so many young men in jeans, khaki pants cut to the knee, dyed shirts, sandals, and even beards. 19 years; “loyal, digne de confiance et coopératif” according to the principal of the military academy; Sport jackets with ties Consequences: Personal transformation; decides to remain as a full-time student the following year
Sous la surface étincelante de l'été se: Under the gleaming summer surface, a critical confrontation between Albers and Dreier on one side, Levi and Rondthaler on the other side is being prepared. The people of the summer know almost nothing about it — except Fuller, because Dreier confides in him. Consequences: Future crisis in the community
Fuller, toujours à court de matériaux po: Fuller, still short of materials for its structures and courses, will look for them at Asheville; Kooning likes to accompany him to speak philosophy. Fuller : “Bill est un penseur vraiment, vraiment merveilleux.” Car journeys Asheville–campus
Fuller dort par siestes de deux heures t: Fuller sleeps two hours every six hours and spends much of the rest of the time talking: theories about everything — “enlever les murs des bâtiments”, differences between indoor cultures and water cultures, stacking hundreds of homes in aircraft for “lâcher” on less favoured areas. 2 hours of sleep every 6 hours
Conférences de quatre à cinq heures ; à: Lectures from four to five hours; mid-term Fuller calls “une petite intermission”, opens the curtains behind it and, while others smoke and talk, exits tables covered with geometric figures — “Fuller et son magic show”. Elaine Kooning reportedly said he fell in love with Bucky when he said: “Et voici notre vieil ami, le tétraèdre.” Tables of geometric figures; curtains
Unique concert solo de Cunningham pour l: Unique Cunningham solo concert for the community in 1948, assisted by Louise Lippold (former student) and Sara Hamill (current student). The public, unaware of modern dance, cannot measure the radical nature of its rupture — as children rejoice by a Klee because they do not know that portraits must look like Rembrandts. What they see: an “discipline ordonnée” and the concern of the “développement de la personne d'une manière individuelle”.
Chargé de cours sur « La structure de la: Lecturer on “La structure de la musique et la chorégraphie” and modern music concerts, Cage devotes the entire series, apart from a single concert of its own, to Erik Satie — culminating in Satie's play, Le Piège de Méduse (the sentence is cut by the footnote). One concert of works by Cage Consequences: Tension announced with Bodky and the established musical taste of the college
Juste avant le début de l'institut d'été: Just before the beginning of the summer institute, the Board of Fellows blocks on Levi proposals: hiring new teachers and expanding the Board by election of new members. The Board also refused to allow a trip of the Levi to Chicago to recruit. On one of the points, Camp Levi wins by one vote, but during a session break, with some supporters of Levi leaving the room, the vote is reconsidered and overturned. Levi sees it as a deliberate and malicious manoeuvre: “s'ils veulent tellement cet endroit, qu'ils le gardent”, and resigns from his position as Rector (not from his teaching position). One-vote victory; reversal of the vote during an adjournment; refusal of a recruitment trip to Chicago. Consequences: Bill and Mary Caroline get a one-year leave and leave campus shortly after.
Dreier assure temporairement le rectorat: Dreier is temporarily rectorate after Levi's resignation; Some social science students leave immediately, including one steals three or four books from the library, including Kenneth Burke's Permanence and Change. Stolen Book: Kenneth Burke, Permanence and Change Consequences: Beginning of the Fall of the Workforce
Lors d'une réunion de faculté, M.C. Rich: At a faculty meeting, M.C. Richards presented a survey asking students what fields to add to the faculty. 16 for English; 13 for a second art teacher; 19 for social studies; 10 for psychology; first choices: 11 psychology, 3 social sciences, 5 art, 3 English Consequences: Justify the orientation of the humanities claimed by M.C.
Fuller arrive en juin dans un camping-ca: Fuller arrives in June in a three-wheeled Dymaxion motorhome filled with models of energy geometry; his optimism and exuberant personality immediately earned converts. Three wheels; models of circular hinged polyhedrons. Consequences: The most enthusiastic reception of Fuller to date.
Fuller édifie des constructions avec l'a: Fuller builds constructions with silverware, assisted by Elaine hairpins; the arrival of the Elaine hamburger, which refuses to pick up its cutlery and pulls a clip out of its bag to hold its dish; Fuller immediately learns a lesson from it Words: Fuller: “Ce qui nous amène au paradoxe de la résistance à la traction !” Atmosphere: A great child's game, an involuntary comedy of the waitress Issue: Engineering invades daily life; Fascination of Elaine
Bill veut intituler une toile « Interior: Bill wants to name an “Interior” canvas; Elaine poses an ultimatum: a precise piece must be named; Bill answers “Attic, because you put everything in it” (“Grenier, parce qu'on y met tout”). Words: Bill: “Attic, parce qu'on y met tout.” Atmosphere: Marital badness around titration. Issue: The role of Elaine as editor of Bill's work.
Refus silencieux, d'un regard, des oreil: Silent refusal, with a look, of pillows at 50 cents; twitching on hard surfaces; reading police novels until dawn; at dawn, ascent of the mountain, magnificent green landscape. Words: Silent look: a dollar of pillows would be an enormous luxury Atmosphere: groggy but exalted Issue: The saving of every dollar against comfort
Conversation sur le dock, cloche, course: Conversation on the dock, bell, general race towards the refectory; They stroll, arrive 20 minutes later: room emptied of each rest. Words: Bill laughs: watch them run. Elaine, haughty: “les chiens de Pavlov” Atmosphere: hilarity, then lesson Issue: The lure of observer superiority
Le camp Levi gagne un vote à une voix ;: Camp Levi wins one vote; during an adjournment or postponement, some supporters of Levi leave the room; the vote is reconsidered and reversed; Levi sees it as deliberate and malicious and resigns as rector. Words: Levi: “s'ils voulaient tellement cet endroit, ils pouvaient le garder”. Atmosphere: Parliamentary tension, suspicion, feeling of betrayal. Issue: The tipping point of the Albers-Levi schism.
Fuller débarque en juin dans un camping-: Fuller landed in June in a three-wheeled motorhome full of models of energy geometry; by the strength of his exuberant personality and malicious enthusiasm, he immediately converted professors and students. Words: It slides in its marathon conferences of the aparties of the genus “notre cher ami, l'hypoténuse”. Atmosphere: Energy, charm, infallible optimization; Fuller's most enthusiastic reception to date. Issue: The renegat in chess series finally finds an audience that embraces it.
22 h : le wagonian propose des oreillers: 10 p.m.: Carers offer pillows for rent, 50 cents. Bill and Elaine look at each other: instant silent agreement — with $94 for the whole summer, a dollar of pillows would be a disproportionate luxury. La night lengthening; wherever they turn their heads, hard surfaces and prominent angles. They give up sleep and read all night police novels. Words: No speech: everything goes through an exchange of eyes and an tacit agreement — matter of actor play Atmosphere: Obstinate gaiety, fatigue, reading glow, train clapotis Issue: Money counted up to the pillow, a month before Black Mountain solves everything
À 22 h, le wagonier propose des oreiller: At 10 p.m., the carrier offered pillows at 50 cents; exchanged eyes, silent decision to refuse; the night stretches, hard surfaces and prominent angles; they give up sleep and read police novels until dawn, when the train climbs the mountain in a dazzling green landscape Atmosphere: groggy but exalted at dawn Issue: $94 saving for all summer
Par un jour de pluie, la classe boulonne: On a rainy day, the class bolts the aluminium strips; the dome rises only a few feet before it collapses; “types du Bauhaus” laughs like Fulton's steamboat bastards, but Elaine is convinced that Fuller is right. 6 large slat circles of aluminium venetian blinds; expected height: 22 feet (approx. 6.70 m); calculation requiring double bands but budget for single bands; Named Supine Dome Consequences: Fuller will later claim to have wanted to demonstrate the safety of a collapse
Cage monte la pièce de Satie sur un pian: Cage mounts Satie's piece on a discordant piano; Elaine plays Frisette, daughter of Baron Médusa; Fuller plays the baron; Cunningham dances a mechanical monkey between the scenes (60 seconds dances); Arthur Penn is staging. William Schrager, “l'étudiant le plus beau du campus”, plays Frisette's sighing
En quinze jours, Droll porte des sandale: In 15 days, Droll wears sandals, has rolled his khakis to his knees and starts following conversations — except when Fuller tells him, at the top of a mountain one night, that holding in a certain way can feel the earth turning: relapse of cultural shock. Late summer: He knows his life has changed. Sandals; khaki rolled to the knees; Night on a Summit Consequences: Stay as a full-time student the following year
Après leur départ du campus, les Levi sé: After their departure from the campus, the Levi stayed with the Rondthalers in their home in Ocracoke, preliminary to departure for Europe. De there, M.C. wrote to the Dreiers a long letter of a brutal frankness summarizing his resentment against the Albers putsch. Consequences: La letter formalizes the ideological rupture between the two sides.
Environ vingt professeurs tournants en s: About twenty rotating professors from July to August, including Albers, Cage, Cunningham, Fuller and Kooning in the core, joined by about 75 students in painting, sculpture and theatre. About 20 teachers, about 75 students; Ray Johnson talks about “galaxy of talent”
Les trois hommes prennent le petit-déjeu: The three men have breakfast together every day; they imagine a fantasy “finishing school”: “We would finish anything” — abolish all conventional approaches to school. Consequences: A lifetime friendship between Cage and Fuller born from their common immersive results
De Kooning faisait des dessins dans le s: De Kooning made drawings in the residence; Elaine: “He was in a vacuum that he began to fill with pastels”; he worked feverishly for a few weeks until he covered the walls with pastels, then fixed a sheet of paper 25 × 32 inches on a easel and passed to oil: Asheville was born. pastels covering the walls; sheet 25 × 32 inches (real work: cardboard, enamel, ~26 × 32 inches) Consequences: Asheville (1948), the first manifestation of his mature style on a small scale.
De Kooning grattait et reconstruisait pl: De Kooning gratified and rebuilt rather than stacked; Elaine reports the painful experience of returning and finding a beloved image “blasted away”. fine surface, scraped and rebuilt
Willem travaillait dans le cottage mais: Willem worked in the cottage but the spouses were separated and Willem often slept elsewhere (Stevens and Swan).
Diplômé de Pratt en 1948, Ray vit la pet: A graduate of Pratt in 1948, Ray saw the little ad in The Nation announcing Mark Tobey for the summer and took the train. Travelers descended along the way; remained alone, he went to the two men of the background: Cage and Cunningham. Cage informed him that Tobey was sick, replaced by Kooning. Small ad in The Nation ; Nice train ride; Almost empty car Consequences: Arrival of Ray at BMC for summer 1948
Environ soixante-quinze étudiants en pei: Approximately seventy-five students in painting, sculpture and theatre, including Ruth Asawa, Joseph Fiore, Betty and Peter Jennerhahn, Ray Johnson, Hazel Larsen Archer, Kenneth Noland, Arthur Penn, Kenneth Snelson, Paul and Vera Williams. about 75 students Consequences: Paul and Vera Williams will financially support Cage and Cunningham; Williams Mix (1952-53) will bear their name
Pendant l'été à Black Mountain parvient: During the summer at Black Mountain, news of Arshile Gorky's suicide arrived. De Kooning, the protector of his friend's mind, refuses any tearing analysis. Kooning reaction: “Gorky était un paysan. Il était très fort, alors quand son corps l'a trahi, il s'en est débarrassé.” Consequences: De Kooning then writes a letter to ARTnews about Gorky.
Cou du brisé dans un accident d'automobi: Broken neck in an automobile accident, painting arm temporarily paralyzed; Three weeks later, after warning almost everyone he met, he committed suicide by hanging. Openly warned of his intention Consequences: Shock in the New York environment
Albers décrit animément la construction: Albers animatedly describes the construction of each building. Visit to Quiet House, a meditation place built by a student in memory of another student who died in a car accident, son of Ted Dreier. Long building with tiny Bauhaus style studios; Bill refuses to paint and chooses the living room of the cottage; Elaine pushes his desk against the window overlooking the lake and painted on kraft paper pinned to the wall. studios with narrow bunk, solid office, chair; pontoon in the distance, students diving in the sun Consequences: Installation of both studios
